review: beware if you're getting a covid-19 nose swab test...linda, after she installed two new phones first, because that was obviously more important than attending to waiting patients, did a fine job of making my nose bleed profusely. and the head nurses who were called to have the damage done to me (so i assumed) checked out merely told me i could go to my primary care provider or they would escort me to the er...so i could wait and pay exorbitant fees? not impressed at all with the level of service or care (not) received today.

what kind of ceo person runs kindred hospital brea calif ? let me tell you. the kind of person that doesn't give a damn about his clinical staff. he runs the place with little to zero amount of staffing to adequately

meet patient and family needs.now and also in this corona pandemic, allows families to freely roam the facility to possibly spread infection, get infections,and endanger patients who are already comprised.also, lets not forget and dismiss our front line personal who don't even have sufficient amounts of protective masks and no n95 masks! gee, what a disappointment... you don't even care about the company you run.

ended up being here longer than expected so i ventured to the lobby for starbucks and then to the cafe on the 3rd floor.  bunless burger and fries.  all cooked fresh and the burger is flame grilled.  delicious and inexpensive! $5 burger and $1 fries.

as a seasoned health care professional, i can spot incompetence, laziness or lack of empathy a mile away. i didn't find any of the above at pomerado hospital. in fact, quite the contrary. the doctors, nurses, ancillary staff, and every professional who took care of mom were absolutely outstanding. i could not have been more impressed. they nailed her diagnosis, missed nothing and expedited the right treatment in the most compassionate way. cheryl and dr. marzack in the er, dr. baswani, catherine, n.p. and ashley, rn on 4 east and others were literal life savers. sam at the front door? a ++. they epitomize excellence in clinical medicine. god bless them all. we will be forever grateful. don't be afraid to seek treatment at this hospital. it is extremely clean and they are very careful. mom is 91 so we were afraid to take her in because of covid, but it was perfectly fine and she is so much better now! thank you, palomar hospital!

if i could give negative stars i would. every experience i have had at this hospital is atrocious.

my daughter spiked a high fever (above 104) with a slight cough, lethargy, loss of appetite, drooling, stomach pain, bloat and gas. we brought her in to the hospital since it was 1am and we were frightened it might be something serious.

they put us in the covid area and quarantined us. the doctor barely looked at her. checked her ears and mouth and vitals and sent us on our way! no covid test, no urine analysis.. she didn't even exam my child's abdominal or body at all.

how is this standard practice!? this place is employed by clowns.

such an incompetent hospital! i went in about 3 weeks ago to er because i had covid-19 symptoms, they rufused to test me because i didn't have a fever, tested me for the flu (which came back negative) and told me i was good to go back to work 2 days later. 

guess what? after spreading it to my entire household, my brother went into er with severe symptoms and tested positive for the coronavirus. great job guys, your incompetence not only gave my entire family coronavirus, but i almost went back to work and infected more people as well! thankfully my common sense told me i shouldn't go even though the nurses and doctors said it was fine. 

fast forward 2 weeks and i get a bill of $1,500 for my er visit where they did practically nothing. i will definitely be disputing that.

if you want an emergency room where nothing gets done after waiting 4 hrs and where they have incompetent workers, then get charged over $1,500- come here! otherwise, beware for the sake of your health and family's health. luckily my parents and brother are recovering but it anything would have happened the blood would be on this hospital's hands!!

this place is a joke. my 1 1/2 year old son went in because he had a seizure due to a high fever. paramedics said to keep his clothes off to keep him cool. they stuck my wife in a hall way with small dividers separating her from people that were actually coughing. my son had no other symptoms, so where is the logic putting a small child that just had a seizure in a hall way with people coughing. not to mention there was no safety/ sanitation procedure in place. so we left and went to children's. if your going to quarantine people you should do so by level of risk. the. you have the audacity  to call and tell us that you could neither confirm nor deny that anyone tested positive for covid and if we wanted to get tested you would expedite testing!!! so we were concerned about covid before and now even more so with your lack of sanitation and common sense. i will never go to this place again. do not bring your children here. it's sad when other medical professionals can agree that your a joke.

my son had spiked a fever and had a febrile seizure a couple nights ago. i've never experienced that with any of my other children before, so i was terrified. we called paramedics and they told us we can take him to the hospital since it's 5 minutes from our house and they felt he was okay, just maybe have him monitored. when i arrived i checked him in and told them what happened, and since he had a fever they said they needed to rule out covid so they sent us to the designated area for people displaying covid symptoms, which is a little hall with chairs along the wall and small barriers between them that really aren't protecting you from anything. i stood there carrying my frightened son (who was only in a diaper as the paramedics said we should keep him that way to help cool him- and won't wear a mask because he's 1 and a half) for well over an hour around three coughing adults. i was told 3 times within that time frame that my son had a room and they were coming to get us. i ended up walking out of there and driving all the way to children's where he was seen much faster. oh, he was negative for covid there. so thank you for potentially exposing my baby and myself and having absolutely no compassion.

probably by far the worst er experience my husband and i have ever been through. my husband broke his leg and so we took him to this nice looking hospital thinking it would be better than tri-city hospital, boy were we wrong. i took him there at 1 pm, i couldn't stay with him because of the corona virus, so i waited in the car, he had to wait until 7 pm to see the dr. and get his leg taken care of, meanwhile he was freezing, thirsty, hungry and in an extreme amount of pain and no one would help him, do not go to this er/hospital unless you like waiting forever and want to suffer!!! we will never go back!
update---my husband just went to a specialist, the diagnosis that the dr. at the er gave him was totally wrong!! first off he would not take x-rays or an mri, he told my husband that he had a broken knee cap and that there was nothing that they could do, when in fact, he tore all the ligaments in his knee and needs surgery! do not go to this hospital! they don't care or know what they're doing!

historically i've had no issues with this facility. 
my apouse required an mri. she has mobility problems (uses walker), short-term memory issues, as well as aphasia (speech/comprehension) problems. i assisted her in the completion of required documentation and was then told i needed to leave due to current virus concerns.
upon making the appointment , i explained the issues and my desire to be with my spouse in order to assist her and was told to merely explain this upon arrival.
i noted a similar ocurrence with another couple while there.
i am fully aware and agree with all reasonable precautions due to the virus situation, however caregivers should not be required to leave the presence of a spouse.
need to look at this unnecessary issue.

i wanted to take a few minutes to say thank you to the whole banner thunderbird staff. let me start off by saying, i was incredibly nervous, as it was my first time being admitted, having an iv and being put under. and, with covid, doing it without a visitor. 

it started the day before with an extremely informative phone call from admissions asking questions and giving great direction on where to go surgery day.

i checked in, sat a few moments in the waiting room then was checked in. i was escorted back to another waiting room by a gentleman, wish i could remember his name! but he was so pleasant, singing and dancing through the halls. 

i was then brought back to prep, where i was with lizette. she was amazing to say the least. extremely gentle, comforting and communicative, always letting me know what was going on. for my first iv experience, she made it essentially painless. i then met with the anesthesiologist, wish i got his name. very helpful and friendly. then, cody came in, the surgical nurse. she was also very assuring and kind. dr. matlock was also very kind, as always! she was assuring through the whole process, even before surgery day. takes the time to answer any questions and you never feel rushed speaking with her. lastly, after surgery, i woke up to sandra and michelle. i dont recall meeting sandra before, i think she was in the or? mustve been the anesthesia! michelle though, i cant say enough about her! so sweet and caring when i woke up. got me whatever i asked for and was willing to be there with me the whole time til i felt comfortable getting up. 

all in all, a great experience in a weird time we are in. the hospital was organized, cautious and still very caring. thank you for easing the mind of this big baby! :)

i wanted to share my experience with the hospital that helped my wife give birth to my baby. once we entered the hospital for delivery, i did not know what to expect. with covid 19 they will hand you a mask, greet you with a smile and walk you to labor and delivery department. at the labor and delivery department you start finding out these amazing nurses and doctors who not only go out of their ways to help you and assist you in any possible way but to make you feel comfortable and safe. the biggest moment in the woman's life is to give birth and the best moment in the dads life is to see the baby healthy. i won't go in details and mention names because each and every individual from doctors, nurses, cleaning crew helped comfort and assisted to take care of my child. the amount of passion, love, respect, attention to details at this hospital is enormous. the blew my mind how powerful this team is, i can say they are angels from heaven. the amount of care they offered my family is beyond, you cannot put money on that and you cannot pay them back for the service they did to help with everything. 
i know most people share only the negative reviews, but it is very unfair to such an amazing hospital to have any single bad review. 
i wrote my review and honestly it is short to thank each and every department that helped. 
god bless each and every single person that works in the medical field who puts their lives on the line to save others. can't thank you enough

i feel compelled to write this review as i genuinely feel that this hospital has some of the best, most compassionate nurses and doctors in the country. it's devastating enough to have a relative admitted to a hospital in the best of times. during a covid pandemic, it's absolutely heartbreaking as even your closest friends and family members are unable to be there with you to help you through things. my grandmother was recently admitted to glens falls hospital and the staff has been nothing short of fantastic. dr. cleaver has been in daily contact with my father, providing him with updates on her condition. then i spoke to the most amazing nurse on t3 who immediately put my mind at ease (she got my grandmother to eat and take her meds- which in itself is an epic feat!)  and she arranged for a facetime chat with my grandmom when she is feeling up to it. they are just beyond compassionate and helpful and fantastic during this horrible time and i am so grateful to have them taking care of grandmom right now. so thank you dr. cleaver and the awesome nurses from t3 who are taking care of her! you are so appreciated!

in my 31 years of life i've never been on the receiving end of any hospital care or services, during a pandemic nonetheless. even amidst what people would describe as chaos within healthcare centers, i received the highest level of care and attention. these healthcare workers really made me feel taken care of and safe after enduring a multi bone injury right in the middle of the covid-19 outbreak. after being taken to the er and being told i broke 2 bones and would need surgery i for sure thought i was going to be out on a list since in ca surgeries were told to have been put on hold so that all workers can focus on covid-19 related cases, but no i was told i'd be worked on within 24 hours. from the time i was admitted to the time i was discharged i can't think of one instance when things could have been better. where i don't suggest you find yourself in a hospital at all other than giving birth to a child, if you're going to be like me and wait 31 years for your first injury i highly suggest you take yourself to memorial hospital within dignity health's network of centers. thanks for taking care of me!

without writing a long essay (which i did and sent it to dignity health and the hospital), when i simply asked to call my sister and leave this place ama, the attitude of the entire floor went from accommodating to mistreatment. these people should never be allowed to treat humans or animals. if i had the option, i'd leave no stars. with covid19 so prominent, i was not allowed visitors or contact with my sister until i asked to leave. they fully abused me and probably all patients on the floor. with no visitors allowed, they fully took advantage of that. they were cruel and fully intended to 'teach me a lesson.' further, a few of the pt workers were also mistreating me. upon leaving, two women who i have never seen before looked at me and said, "there's the shit stirrer." what? how did they figure this? the only 'shit' i stirred was asking to leave. i was called names, told they didn't 'like me,' and was accused of coming in for an overdose. which was patently ridiculous. i went in for a recurring issue. listen to the negative reviewers. don't fall for that whole 'they rock' attitude. they don't. stay away from this hospital at all costs.

review: my son broke his leg a few weeks ago and the healthcare team at children's handled that very well. this review is for the cast removal. my husband took our son to children's to have his cast removed while i stayed home with our infant. my husband took a few pictures of the nurse removing the cast. i looked at the pics later and was shocked to see the nurse removing the cast had a hole in his glove. i was upset and worried so i called the orthopedic department. the nurse i spoke with said the hole in the glove may have been made intentionally by the nurse when removing the cast. seriously?! that makes zero sense and i was pretty offended by this excuse. she said she would report to management and that was all. the end. holes in ppe are never a good thing, but during a pandemic i would hope people would be extra cautious. i now have to keep a closer eye (not sure if that's even possible) on my son and family's health. thanks children's for more worries during these frightening and uncertain times!

if i could give this place triple zeros for professionalisms i would. my father had to be rushed to the emergency room due to him having influenza b. the emergency room staff on the night shift is horrifying. they had us in the er for 14hours before my 70 yr old father was placed in a room. multiple patients came in and because of the area they perceive most "blacks and hispanics" are drug users or mental illness patients. i witnessed nurse  george making fun of a patient that was coming down off of something and they all sat and laughed when he fell and hit the floor. it got so bad with them not checking on my father or letting us know any information that i had to address them with my law enforcement badge to let them know that every patient in here is not a drug user that you can make fun of which is so sickening to me. another nurse that need to considered finding a new career and learn how to talk to patients is adrien midnight shift nurse. it was so bad i feel like he's a racist. if covid wasn't happening i would've transferred my father out of that hospital in a second but when i called and spoke with his doctor at northwestern he advised to stay their and let him get treatment. never, let your love ones go here ever!!!!

the nursing staff was fabulous, so professional, great communication, so caring.

the hospital was quite nice, if large. her room was private and she was being taken care of quite well.  i was impressed with the parking garage and the elevators and how well everthing was laid out.

oh man.. soo let me just say most of the nurses were great while i was staying here the main nurse i loved was the one that was in my recovery room after my c section. once i finally got to my room i was a little disappointed it was very small the bed was tiny and some nurses were nice but not really on point i had to ask over 3 different nurses on different shifts to bring my baby formula i felt like they were avoiding that because they were pushing me to breastfeed (which i am) i'm doing both. also i couldn't pee on time and kept being kinda pushed as we all know after a c section it's hard to pee right after and they kept coming in basically saying if i don't pee i would be back on a catheter which i didn't say anything too because if it came down to it it's really up to me to say yes or no. anyways i ended up going and avoided any issue. it's a stressful time considering the covid situation we couldn't even walk the hallways according to the nurses until one of the nurses said we can but with our masks on which is understandable but not everyone on different shifts gets that memo and we didn't go out to avoid a problem. they also bothered my baby a lot one nurse came in to check his temperature etc and 5 minutes later another nurse came in and she said oh we have todo this because we don't share notes ? kinda disorganized to me. anyways i'm home with my baby now thank you to my ob and the nurses that actually cared for me and my baby during this time.

on sunday the emergency room took a culture. most cultures are ready in 48 hours. it can take up to 72 hours. 96 hours later the results are not available. on sunday early afternoon an mri was performed. the technician could not tell me what he sees, there is protocols restricting that. later that evening i asked the nurse to follow up with getting the pictures read. nurse contacted the dr on duty but she could not read the results because, and i quote, the doctor is on her boat. on monday night, after the podiatrist had done some small surgery on my foot i could not sleep. i asked for something to help. i was given ambien. an hour later the nurse woke me up to ask if it was working. that was at 11:30 pm. at 4:00 am the lights all came on in the room and the garbage cans were emptied. at 5:00 am all the lights came on so they could take my "room mates" vitals. i was still waiting for the results of the culture. my questions led me to believe that i would not get the results any time soon. there is a current pandemic. a hospital at hospital rates was not a good place to wait. i told them i was going to go home. my foot had a new open wound, i asked them to please dress it so i could leave, the hospital staff refused. i found some bandages in the room and dressed it myself. i then hobbled my way to the entrance to leave. they refused to help me. it was like dealing with a group of spiteful children. i and my doctor have been working for two days to get the culture results so the correct antibiotic can be identified to cure my ailment. neither of us can get anything from the hospital. there is no provision for patient advocacy. the last thing i heard is, " we have 24 hours to respond to you" not likely but if i have cellulitis as suspected it could get into my blood stream, my bones, vital organs or brain.
                  i would highly recommend you to steer clear of tampa general. i think they are the anti-christ. and don't be fooled that this is due to the pandemic. the floor of the hospital i was on was about 40% occupancy. governor of florida announce that throughout the pandemic, this hospital had 59 corona patents,  52 have recovered. i assume they have gone home. they are not overwhelmed. i think they do this to maximize income by extending patient stays. very profitable.

coming here to work for three months as a first time travel nurse i don't think i could have picked a better place to start. the facility was on the top of their game dealing with the covid and all
of the new policies getting changed (with what seemed daily) by the cdc and government. the staff here is very supportive and they really care about the patients. the patient to staff ratio here is also amazing which is why patients get the best care. super blessed to be a staff member even if it was just for the summer. :)
during the corona virus situation,  great to see kp-sf has isolation tent setup to deal with infected patients.

review:
i always said kaiser is fine - i'm a healthy 60 year old, no meds no conditions (other than lifelong asthma).  i'm a retired nurse.  i was dx with head & neck cancer in march.  i just finished 7 weeks of radiation and 7 chemo infusions.  i was admitted may 30 with a fever. neutropenia.  shocked. i was told i'd have be here a week.  covid precautions ppe at kaiser are dismal.  kaiser had the worst outcomes for covid pts in the bay area and i can see why.  i had to demand that anyone coming into my room wear a shield over their surgical facemask (no n-95). telling people didn't work, i threw the phone receiver at one woman as i had asked her but 10 minutes 
i will make other, more specific posts, but my care has been third world. i cannot get food - after working hard on my own (covid, i've been sheltering since march 3, the only people i've had contact with are kaiser people) to not lose a lot of weight during radiation (some h&n pts end up on feeding tubes) i cannot get food i can eat at kaiser hospital.  i need bland, pureed, gluten free.  i received no food for my first 14 hours, despite repeated requests. the first breakfast wasn't bland or gluten free.  we decided cream of rice - arrives as a solid mass.  scrambled eggs ok.  in 4 days i not received cream of rice that is edible - i have to thin the solid mass with hot water. there isn't enough room in the cardboard cup to add more water.  all i want is some instant rice cereal that is edible.  
i have to constantly phone to ask for my food.  my nurse won't do anything.  last night i asked about my dinner at 5:45, my nurse leaves and says nothing.  6:15 i use the call light to ask about my dinner.  someone who barely comprehends english says "it on way."  i call kaiser outside line (833-2000) i ask the operator if i need to call the police to do a welfare check. after using the call light some 4 times, 4 calls to kaiser operator, i get someone in nutrition who says "oh, you're on a pureed gluten free diet and we don't have anything for you."  they never sent a dinner and didn't tell anyone.  this was after i spoke with some in "nutrition" (just a title, no one i spoke with has any education or training in nutrition, they are microwavers and bussers) 7 pm i had some dinner.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Medical Center and Offices

review: don't go to this hospital if you want to get healthy. my relative entered with a cardiac arrhythmia and was discharged 2weeks later with covid 19 which i believe she got during admission indicating infectious disease protocol issues.  staff members were pleasant but callous. staff provided contradictory information. administration did not respond to messages. the switchboard indicated the hospital did not have a patient advocate. the case manager was minimally competent and was unable to identify post hospital care resources requiring me to do so by myself. the end result was transfer to a rehabilitation facility at 10 pm which would have been unacceptable if we did not believe that discharge from this facility was needed to save my relative's life.

i brought my son to jupiter medical center for an mri this morning. we went through the usual covid screening and were sent to the admitting department to fill out paperwork and pay for the test. after he was taken back for the mri i asked the nurse where i could get a cup of coffee while i waited for him. she very nicely pointed out how to get to the cafeteria. on my way past the front desk, the security guard stopped me and told me i had to leave the building immediately. i explained that i was waiting for my son who is having an mri. he said he didn't care. i continued to explain that i had already been let into the hospital after going through the screening process. he then stood up and came out from behind his desk so that i could see he was carrying a gun. i found this to be extremely threatening. it's certainly not the type of service you would expect from a high-end hospital in a community like jupiter. while i was checking in originally i noticed that this particular security guard was nasty to everyone in line in front of me.

i took my mom into the emergency department due to severe epigastric pain and vomiting blood on 3/24/20 around 8pm. there is a new policy and guideline they must follow a "strict no visitor" policy due to the covid-19 pandemic but the nurses especially the triage nurse was nothing but rude. i understand that everyone is on edge with the pandemic, but what about the "sharp experience". this would be the time to show more compassion and empathy to patients and families don't you think? 

there were only two patients in the waiting, and when they finally called her to check in, the triage nurse, visibly more interested in talking to her fellow staff members than patients, spoke to her in a rude tone. at this time, my mom was already having trouble speaking, yet alone answer the nurses screening questions. i was trying to answer the most i can and the nurse sighed as if she was annoyed. when she asked if she had/possibly been exposed to covid-19, i mentioned to her she is an er nurse at sharp grossmont, she sighed again and became more short and annoyed.

i was more than understanding about the no visitor policy and i was given a card with a phone number to call for updates and to call the nurse who was going to be assigned to her. when we called approximately an hour after they called her in, the phone rang twice and it was disconnected. the second time we called, the operator transferred us before even asking who the patient was, and when we finally got a hold of someone, the person on the phone was short when we were asking for any updates. before we could even ask how she was doing she hung up the phone. 

i would hope that they understand how everyone must be feeling at this moment. everyone coming into the ed must be there for a reason and that this may be one of their worst days of their life, and yet the nurses we experienced today in the main waiting room was nothing but short of compassion. 

shout out to the cna/na who helped her getting a wheelchair. she was the only one who spoke to my mom with genuine care and concern.

my mom just had a stay at northwest community hospital for chest pain. they eliminated heart problems after a day and then discharged her while she was still in level 8 pain. i tried to talk to her doctor (had to request it 2 times) and when he called he was mad at me for wanting to talk to him about what was going on! she is older and needs to have someone helping her explain the situation. the problem with chest pain has happened 5 times - 3 with hospital stays at northwest community. i couldn't believe they were going to discharge her with the pain. he hung up on me while we were on the phone. no i wasn't yelling. no i wasn't rude. i was just trying to tell him the situation and he wasn't interested. she was discharged. in this covid era, i had no one to speak for her. pathetic.

this is a review for their labor and delivery part of the hospital.

i'm currently writing this in the recovery room, having just delivered my second baby (first one with el camino, first was with ucsf in the city). i just wanted to use this moment to rave about my experience this time around compared to ucsf.

from triage to l&d to recovery, all the doctors and nurses here are by far the most experienced, kind, knowledgeable and kind people i have ever met. due to covid i never got a chance to do a hospital tour, so i had no idea what to expect when i checked in 2 nights ago after laboring for 24h at home.

at triage i was greeted by nurse melissa, who checked me and i hadn't progressed enough to be admitted. instead of just sending me home, she asked me to walk the hallway for 1h to see if it'll speed things up. and it did, i went from 3cm to 5cm during that hour and was admitted right after.

the rest of the nursing team were all super pleasant, knowledgeable and explained every little thing to me without me having to ask. there's a really positive energy and rapport between the nurses so it carries through the whole bedside manner. my iv drip at ucsf last time was a traumatic experience, they couldn't find my vein and blood kept spurting everywhere. this time at el camino, they had a nurse who specialized in iv insertion and she did it painlessly and perfectly in one to without any blood. 

i knew i wanted an epidural this time, and instead of dictating to me when i should get it, they told me to tell them whenever i wanted it. i decided to walk for another hour before asking for the epidural. now let's talk a bit about the epidural. i had dr. k (forget the full name) and he was so good. no pain, super calm, and the meds took effect almost immediately. with ucsf i was in so much pain and the injection didn't even work the first time, i had to wait 2h for the anesthesiologist to come back to up my dosage. this time, the dosage was perfect because i had no pain but eventually i could feel the pressure as i was nearing 10cm. i could move my legs and could feel the pressure of contractions so my pushing was super effective. i'm told this is the perfect dosage and that the doctor is really good.

now onto the pushing phase. at ucsf (since it's a teaching hospital) there were 10+ people in the room while i was pushing. some were helping while others were just spectating. this time, i had one nurse stay with me the whole time helping me push, and once it got to a certain point she called my ob and she came and took it to the finish line. hardly tore, got 2 stitches and no hemorrhages. i tore second degree and hemorrhaged pretty badly with my first.

once baby was here, they moved us to the mother & baby section. since the epidural wore off rather quickly i was able to pee way faster than with my first, and the nurses in recovery were all super nice and accommodating. i also had a fabulous lactation consultant help me with breastfeeding, who really gave me the most helpful pointers that i never got with my first. when i was at ucsf with my first, i had a lot of pain in latching and the lc there told me that nothing was wrong and a "little" pain is normal. basically made me feel like a wuss. turned out my firstborn had a tongue tie and lip tie but i didn't get that diagnosed til she was already 3mo. of course by then my breastfeeding journey was already a hot mess and did not go well at all. the lc at el camino (stacey was her name) took her time to teach me how to latch and basically said that proper breastfeeding should never hurt. after 30min of training i was able to find a good latch and now my baby is breastfeeding really well. night and day.

anyways, i just wanted to take the time to give credit to an incredible group of staff. it's seriously night and day to my experience at ucsf and i wouldn't have known unless i had something to compare against. 

thank you for such a pleasant birthing experience. i never knew i would ever use "pleasant" to describe labor and delivery.

to be honest, when my kids get sick, wether it's a cough, cold, fever that lasts for days, i avoid taking them to uc or even dr. i usually just go on instinct and let the illness play it's  role. i know there is not much that can be done to speed up the healing process of cold, flu, or viral/bacterial infection. i only tryy and make my children feel as comfortable and loved as i possibly can, meanwhile give them hope and assurance that's they will be fine in no time. 

i decided to take my oldest there  yesterday because on my way to her primary physician, she threw up for the second time  in a  12hr period from an extremely dry cough that she had gotten familiarly back for the second time within a one week period. i had to turn round and go home. my oldest got the flu on jan 16th this year and while the rest of my families lasted for 4 days tops, she had the fever for over 5 days and the recovery process after the fever was not easy. i feel like it's been a month she is sick now and i thought that instead of going home to change ( because she was covered in vomit) and heading  back to pc in west hills ( i live in sun valley) and having the dr  tell me it's just this or that, i thought i should take her to the hospital we're they can run some test to see why my child keeps falling sick. that they would be maybe more knowledgeable, equipped with the right tools to rule out all possible causes to why she isn't getting bet. we checked in at 11:30am. mind you the parking lot was a parking lot. we were called in at 3:30pm. i honestly couldn't believe it. my daughter laid in her fathers arms for 4 hours with a fever that would escalate to 102. if she wasn't feeling that bad prior to the visit, then she was during the wait. the entire waiting area was packed after an hour of waiting. i'm almost 9months pregnant and i can't deny the anxiety i was feeling with the sounds or coughs, sneezes, kids breathing on my neck and thier parents doing or saying anything. children with all thier clothes off because they had a fever, babies throwing up. i mean it was a scene out of a movie. i-3 pts were being called in per hour. it was absolutely ridiculous. i would have been better off at a regular hospital. 

they finally called us in. the experience inside was a relief really. it's annoying to say we waited 4+ hours to have the doctor's run zero test but i was content with hearing that it's a viral infection. any parent would rather hear that then anything else. they made us wait 20mins more after examining my child because her heart rate was a little high because of the fever she had earlier. but they had a section for children to color, so my daughter was distracted by her symptoms. they gave her a popsicle which made her smile. after the 20mins, they checked her heart rate and she was fine. they sent us on the way with advice on what to do if this or that happens. my daughter ended up being put on an antibiotic 4 days after the hospital visit from her pc because of a bad sinus infection. she much better now.

i'm grateful my husband and i didn't leave that hospital sick ourselves. the hospital needs to make it absolutely mandatory for all persons young and old to wear a mask. it's a waiting room with a bunch of people coughing without the common decency of closing their dam mouth and child running around sneezing, having their booger's dripping, jumping on chairs touching other people. i mean seriously i pray that i never have to ever bring my children here ever again. 

ps: this was a complete shock to me and i couldn't wrap my head around it. they don't run any test to see wether or not ur child has the flu. or at least that's what they told me. the only "treat" the flu not check for it. lol. ok, and this is a hospital?

when you call someone from a hospital at 6 am you better leave a message. you know what someone is thinking to see a missed call when they wake up? why would your staff call and leave  a message that is just call music. 
i called all three locations to see if a family member had been checked in overnight. i was told no at all three places. so why do you guys call me then during a pandemic and leave a message with call music? scare or stress someone out for nothing. 
then when i get lb er and ask well what is your policy? would that person call back? i don't know, she says, i would but don't know what someone else would do. policies by definition are the rules for a company's operation, and as such, are the way you should all operate. or does your hospital allow everyone to make up the rules as they go along. i doubt that. there should be a policy somewhere in your operating procedures on how a staff member in that hospital does their job in every instance, including notification of family. so hearing someone from your staff say they do not know what another would do in that case, makes me wonder if your staff knows what procedures are. if not, is retraining in order? 

either way leaving a message of only music and not calling back is ridiculous during a pandemic. i called the operator and spoke to someone else to see what the policy was so i could know if i should keep trying to find out who called me. the lady also did not know policy. i cannot believe there is not a policy handbook given out when staff goes through orientation. or do they think reading it is optional? really? 

i think someone should check into this hospital. i am surprised with all these reviews they have not already been investigated. the behavior is unprofessional and unacceptable.

let me suggest that if you do not have a policy on notification, you get on it as part of your next risk management review for your organization. i also suggest that these yelp reviews are an indicator of how well your hospital is performing, and if you are not resolving the issues mentioned here, that you are missing an important part of your risk assessment, every patient deserves a standard of care. do you have the bar set too low???!!!

covid19 drive-thru test is one of the worst experiences i ever had in my life. they put the ear cleaning tip up in your nose so deep that my tears started pouring out right away. it's a really sharp pain for a moment and i been feeling soo much discomfort and headache all day long.

it's hard to put an exact star rating. every medical facility has its good and bad. but my two stars are a reflection that if i had time on my side and another choice of a medical provider, would i choose dominican? no. why?

my mom was rushed here. while the er care got my mom forwarded to icu where she belonged, they didn't explain to my sister what a dnr was. my sister was hysterical and passed over the care to me. i lifted the dnr because we didn't know yet what was going on and she deserved to be revived (if she coded) and time to be diagnosed.they need to explain legal definitions to people when they are making these kind of decisions.

the icu was a dream team. every single one of her nurses, if we weren't in a pandemic where i can't go in the hospital, i'd give them all hugs for their a+ care and compassion. dr. singh soon became my favorite doctor ever. he got to know who my mom is. he listened. he respected us. he's the guy you'd trust with your life because he's trustworthy by going above and beyond with earning it.  even specialist that we interacted with in the icu was just top notch. 

so why the low rating? once we had her moved to telemetry, the hospitalist was abusive screaming at me instead of giving facts or letting me check with the experts that i needed to verify risk versus reward in what was being requested. i fired her. then i got the grim reaper dr. binesh. he spoke fatalistically and pushed hospice on us when we didn't have a terminal diagnosis. when we said we didn't want it, he also sped up discharge to less than 24 hours but notified us on a saturday evening when we couldn't get in home care set up because it was after business hours. i had expressed to them that my mom's wishes was after she was stable enough, her transition goal was to be cared for at home. when my mom was able to talk she told the doctor that she wanted to go home as her next step. so why weren't they helping us?

hospice would get preferential treatment with a magic extension to allow her to stay in the hospital if they took the case,  but we weren't allowed to have an extension to set her up at home with a home health care company outside of hospice. without a terminal diagnosis, isn't that medicare fraud if you engage hospice? we didn't go that route because it wasn't applicable or part of our goal to let our mom go when she was still recovering and we didn't know what was going happen next.  

what happened felt unehtical and like medical blackmail. our only other option was to contest it with medicare and be on the hook for the bill for that time in the hospital past the premature discharge. so now she's in rehab (against her wishes but our best option under these circumstances) until we can get home health care set up because any money that we do have should be reserved for making her better, not fighting the grim reaper and his games. 

they never notified us that they were transitioning her meds from iv to oral. they are supposed to notify you as soon as possible to discuss discharge so you have time to plan. that wasn't done. it would be one thing if she's magically better and could walk out.  she's not ambulatory, can't feed herself, requires meds, still not all coherent, requires aids, nurses, physical therapy, occupational therapy and meds to sustain her. it is pretty heartless to push her out that fast and not give the family time to discuss decisions, find a nursing organization, medical equipment and assist us with setting up support. they passed the buck. unless we chose hospice. no seriously, what's up with that? do they get a commission or something for patient referrals? (shakes head)

i'm happy that she's out of there. when you have a few rotten apples, it spoils it for the bunch. what we went through was extra hard because there are precautions that no one enters the hospital.i appreciate that. i had to advocate over the phone with limited time, limited information. they could have taken extra time or found a way to better share her chart or scheduled extra time to allow the medical advocate to absorb information and get back to them,  and/or not freaked out when you request a consult from a specialist where the risk is to make the best decision possible. even the discharge nurse said get back to me. i said i'd call her right back and she didn't tell me that it was the end of her shift that she was going home. i couldn't get a hold of her and it was someone else on shift the next day. what's wrong with these people? seriously, i hope someone treats them the way that they treat others some day so that they get a taste of their own medicine. 

your name is dignity health. the icu lives up to that name but there are other parts of the hospital that definitely need fixing.

rex  has made some unfortunate decisions regarding throat and nasal cultures that may require a visit to labcorp instead, but for the most part i highly rec rex outpatient labs . further praise :rex hospital labs do an an excellent job at turn around times on labwork  and the results are often available much more quickly than from its competitors

i had a full replacement knee in 1  1/2 months, january 9th. at this time i realized that i had spent a whole year in pain dealing with the iha orto department. wow! my knee is doing great thanks to him.

my next experience is with another department just yesterday (06/03/2020).
i am having severe anxiety and have falling into a depression. i don't know how to handle this or what to do. it is very scary. with my doctors referral i went to the iha emergency room to get admitted for some time to get me through with what i thought was professional help. i walked in begging for help because i did not know what to do and all i can really do is cry. i was checked in and placed in a room. this room had no usable sink and no bathroom in it. i was visited by a nurse right away around noon. another nurse come in and drew blood for the lab and i was given a covid test, (never got the results from that test by the way)they brought me a sandwich and a glass of water. a short time later a psychologist came to see me and asked a few question and wanted to know why i was there. i again begged for help and explained that i just don't know what to do. she assured me they would help. she asked all kinds of very good questions and i told her i was having a hard time functioning in daily life. she finished her questions and left. a short time later, i got a call from a social worker and fielded questions from her and again begged for help. she told me i would most likely be admitted shortly.

i sat in that room for 11  1/2 hours with nothing but a bed and a tv that predominantly played hospital commercials and music with but a few channels to try and watch. at 11:00 p.m. i found the strength to walk out to seek care at a more professional facility. as i was leaving, i saw nobody including nurses anywhere around. i walked out the door at 11:00 and will be going elsewhere for help. 
i am writing this in hopes of saving anybody reading this a lot of trouble. 
as a side note, my wife is a nurse, and i do know what goes on in hospitals. i am not just some impatient customer. both experiences should not have happened. i am afraid iha has no real customer friendly managers. incompetence seems to be the norm here.!

today my mom had a surgery and the treating doctor is contracted with providence saint joseph medical center. we were very pleased with the doctor and thus did not want to change the provider and had to schedule procedure with providence saint joseph medical center. let me summarize todays experience as an outline. 

- i brought my mom to check in at 0900, due to the covid-19 i was not allowed to be with her in the hospital and was asked to wait outside the building and the nurse will call me once she is ready for the pick up.
- my mom has an extensive medical history that includes: heart issues, diabetes, arthritis and spinal stenosis.
- after she was checked it, she was escorted for the covid-19 testing. the testing center was of long distance and because of heart issues, arthritis and spinal stenosis she had difficulty to walk and was in pain. the escort, instead of offering a wheelchair or some sort of assistance just crossed hands and implied that she should walk slower. my mom had to walk to and from the testing place in pain and no support.
- the treating doctor talked to me before heading to the hospital and on the way from the hospital, as i was waiting downstairs, and there were no problem with the procedure. procedure lasted 2 hours and was finished at around 1400. 
- she was taken into the recovery room where she was placed under observation of nurses.
- as i was not allowed to be with and was calling every 40 to 50 minutes the provided number to check on her status and every time i called i was told that she is ok and is sleeping. but when i picked up my mom at around 1720 she told me how she was neglected and mistreated. i have never  heard her to say anything so negative about the health providers.
- since she came out of anesthesia nobody came to check on her, she is diabetic and was asked in pre-op to fast and no water since midnight before the procedure. so nobody came and checked if she needs some food or water. she could have easily gone into hypoglycemic shock and nobody would even know to intervene. in addition, once she came out of anesthesia the oximeter was not on her finger. once again, she could have had post operative complications and nobody would have know. the room was cold and there was no way to ask call a nurse to give her a blanket and what was worst she needed to use bathroom but been weakened by the procedure she could not walk by herself and spent about 2 hours calling for help and assistance. she could not call too loud as the procedure was done within the area that inhibited breathing and talking and she try to call for help and hit on the side of the bed to attract any attention. until somebody walked into the room hours later and asked what she wanted. when mom asked the person who walked who are you the reply she got was "and who are you" which was uncalled for. when she asked why nobody came to check on me in such a long time she was told that because she has medicare they do not have to check on her. seen how upset she was somebody asked for supervisor who tried to smooth everything out and started to offer food, drink, help, etc. 
- as i said i was not with her and could not represent to helper and take names and prevent this abuse and negligence. when they rolled her outside for me to pick her up at the curbs nothing i could have done and just listen to my mom tell me what happened in tears on our way home. 

this is unacceptable behavior and elder patients who can not stand for themselves should not be treated these way.  the providence saint joseph medical center personnel lied to me every time i called and allowed this negligence and abuse to continue without any repercussions. the website for the hospital does not have options to file a complain and reading all the negative reviews it seems not to care for the well being of their patients.

our family's story as briefly as possible:  my 79 yr. old father fell at home and fractured his hip.  he was taken via ambulance to our small town local hospital.  of course, during these times of covid, none of his family were permitted to be with him.  he has quite a list comorbidities, so our small town hospital deemed his situation too critical to treat.    they recommended we transfer him to hmc for surgery, post surgery care and then on to a rehab facility.  to say we were relieved was an understatement but unfortunately, that feeling left quicker than it came.  our father was taken into surgery without notifying any of his 6 daughters, 2 of which are his medical poa's.  the first call one of the poa's received was that our father was out of surgery, he did fairly well, but his bp was critically low so he would spend the night in icu.  oh, and by the way, can you complete these consent forms with me!  yes, if you're following, this was after surgery, not before.  this was unsettling but fortunately, it wasn't "another type of notification call" and we just wanted to start the road to recovery.  well, i'll spare you all the emotional, in between details, but basically our dad laid in a hospital bed incoherent and non-responsive from thursday until the next tuesday when we had him transferred to another hospital!  i can't even describe the fear, frustration, and heartbreak my siblings and i endured during these 5 days.  we couldn't see him.  we couldn't talk to him.  to say we were living in hell is not an exaggeration!  we fell apart every time our phone rang thinking it was going to be "the call"!   and if this stress level wasn't enough, hmc has the absolute worst staff i've ever experienced in hospital care.  the nurses are incompetent, lack compassion and are plain unprofessional!  we were lied to, repeatedly, hung up on repeatedly, (yes, you read that correctly) and told by one nurse carly, "i'm at lunch right now, i can't help you"!  after staying in icu for 2 days, he was transferred to a step down floor.  we asked if we could facetime with him.  when they finally "found an ipad", we were told it only had 18% battery so not sure how long it would last.  then a person who announced to us she wasn't his nurse, laid it on his stomach and walked out.  he was so weak and disoriented, he couldn't hold it so we couldn't see him.  we tried talking to him over facetime but if he tried to speak, we couldn't understand him.  between 6 of us, we are rarely speechless or unable to come up with some type of solution; but there is a first time for everything.   we tried begging, pleading, crying, and yelling to get care for our father but we were hung up on, ignored and dismissed; all while he continued to lay in a bed deteriorating.  the doctor experience wasn't any better and the patient-care advocate/liaison, who is supposed to advocate for the patient, basically declined to address the matter and began "circling the wagons" once we told them we were initiating a transfer.  when they heard this, they then tried to threaten and scare us that a transfer would be a lateral move so insurance would likely not pay for his stay and we'd be responsible for over $200,000 in medical bills!  well, if the man laying in the bed wasn't practically comatose and able to communicate, he would reply, oh, the hell you say, just try to get blood out of this turnip!  i sincerely hope that another human never has to suffer the way my father and my siblings and i have over the last 5 days.  i'm so thankful that 3 of my sisters are nurses and knew he would not last much longer with this substandard care.  we advocated every minute of those 5 days to get get my dad transferred.  my heart hurts for those patients who do not have 6 relentless daughters in their corner as advocates!

this review is not about the care for my loved one, but about the protection of his identity and personal belonging while in the care of inova alexandria hospital. my brother was admitted and went straight to icu on a ventilator from the emergency department. his friend was with him and asked for his wallet that included his identification, medical cards, money and precious memories, his cellphone and his keys. since she is not his wife or family member, the ed nurse would not give them to her. there is video of the nurse giving his bag to a security guard. the story told to our family is that guard put the bag down as he was called away and another came behind him and threw my brother's personal belongings in the trash. over a 23 day period, i spoke with the icu nurse, patient relations, icu unit director, left a message for emergency room director, emergency room manager, head of security, security director, back to patient relations and ed manager. i left messages with the admin asst. for dr. rina bansal, president of alexandria hospital as well as the admin for john gaul, chief general counsel for the hospital to receive no return call. 

patient relations and the ed manager were the chosen ones to deal with me by finally requesting we provide an itemized summary and cost for replacing my brother's personal items, offered us $100, 1 year of identity theft protection and provided a "memo" with someone who had not been involved with this issue as the point of contact. this memo is to be used as supporting documentation for trying to obtain hard copies of the items they threw away. they agreed to give us copies of the cards on file, but provide no additional assistance. my nephew who is my brothers "legal next of kin" is expected to pay for these items and submit an invoice while he is unemployed and caring for his family during the covid-19 pandemic. to make matters worse they will then issue a check in my brother's name. he asked for a final settlement using a good faith estimate so that our family can move on and focus solely on the care for my brother which has not been responded to. he has gotten no acknowledgement or response to his email. 

i could go on and on, but i think you can get the message that inova alexandria hospital has taken no real responsibility in their negligence and failure to fully protect my brother while he was in their care. they continue to demonstrated the utmost disrespect to my brother and our family at such a crucial time in the world. 

let me end by saying my brother is no longer at that hospital and as expected, patient relations has gone silent as it pertains to this issue.

review: i came into the emergency room on sunday june 15th, turns out i tested positive for c diff and pancreatitis. it was a rough first two miserable days. not being able to get comfortable, missing my home and bed, doors opening and closing not to mention getting woke up every few hours to get tests done. not to mention i was in isolation because they had to wait for my covid results to come back, and no one could come in with me. i know this isn't a hotel, or some luxurious place to stay but i needed some sort of comfort. that monday i had a rn woman named julie- she got me a fan and an extra pillow, i had justin that night and he was there for me above in beyond making sure i was comfortable. i then met an angel (melissa harris). the bed side manner she displayed was over the top. she fixed my fan that broke made sure i was on top of all my meds and just genuinely cared. she asked if she could pray with me and i told her yes, she was exactly what i needed to find comfort in staying there. melissa you love your job and it shows! never ever ever lose your heart, you are so special! on my last two days i got to know sonia, she was incredible to. so very nice and made sure she did all that she could for me. ellen and vanessa, and alicia were very good cnas. i'm so grateful for each and every one of you that helped me heal. thank you!

on 04/02/2020, i had a surgery at corona hospital. i was at the outpatient department and all the nurse there were very friendly and professional. 3-4 nurses came to me if i'm ok or need anything and they tried to make me feel comfortable and explained the process smoothly. after surgery, i was open my eyes at the recovery room. two friendly nurses were helping me to recover and promptly proceed the discharge process. she gave a heads up to my husband that i'm coming out soon and another nurse was kindly pulling my wheelchair to outside of the building. i couldn't remember all the nurses names but all of them were awesome and i'm so thankful for their help on that day. it was my first time experience at corona regional medical center and i'm very satisfied. 
today 04/03/20, actually one of the nurses called me for follow up and asked me if i'm ok or i have any questions. 
thanks to all of you, i felt my surgery went great with all of nurses extra care. strongly recommended :)

special thanks to everyone at corona regional medical center for your hard work, dedication and sacrificing your personal time with your family to make sure that your patients are taken care of. i truly appreciate every single physician, surgeon, and anesthesiologist that saved my life with my emergency surgery. thank you to all the nurses and cna's that nursed me back to health and took great care of me during my time at corona regional medical center. i will forever be appreciative and grateful for you all going above and beyond to make sure that i was in good hands.

review:
due to covid19 i had my eyes set on delivering at queen of the valley hospital originally since it was a whole separate building. eventually i changed obgyns and this became my delivery hospital. it is one of the best things to happen.
labor and delivery has always been amazing to me. went several times for monitoring due to a risky pregnancy. every time we went i was treated wonderfully and had all my fears put at ease.
when the day finally came the nurses were on it! it was a busy night but they made sure to accommodate us in a timely manner. explained everything clearly, continuously monitored to make sure i was comfortable, and always made sure dad was doing great too. 
had a csection and the anesthesiologists was amazing. he always made sure the safety of my baby was monitored as well as me. his humor helped so much during a time that was full of fear.
after delivery our recovery room was clean, well maintained, and the nurses were great. millie and christine were great they gave us several tips for being first time parents. all the nurses made my recovery easier with the love and care we received.
the hospital is very breast feeding and bonding. we went the formula route and not once did they ever make us feel bad about it they encourage you to still try which i think is great. you want to deliver at a hospital that meets all your needs and is understanding of your decisions. we're glad i was able to deliver my baby here.
p.s. the romantic dinner is so sweet!

in all my years of life, i have never (not even when i had my two girls at this hospital) encountered a nurse more caring and loving than this last time i was hospitalized during this pandemic. as all and most nurses showed how much they feared me, the only one who talked and treated me like a human and genuinely cared to make sure my needs were met and i felt most comfortable during my stay, is arc angel! i was in pulmonary and he cared for me as though i was his family. he was most respectful and if i ever did page the nurse station, he came in a heartbeat. he is the true definition of what any and every nurse should be like. he made sure my room was always clean and my ice bags were nice and filled. my water cup was full of ice water and i had all things in my reach. he knew how lonely i was in there, be it that nurses only came in and out once every 4 hours to check my vitals and my tv did not work. i literally was becoming so depressed. he is quite special and saw in my eyes how sad i was. he talked about random things or about life in general to help take my mind off my situation. for all that's going on, he was the only thing that gave me sense or normalcy. his talks made me feel as though i was talking to an old friend. he made me laugh and happy, something that was very hard to feel all the meanwhile i was scared. i want to thank him from the bottom of my heart for believing i'd come out winning. for treating me the way he did and letting me know, i am human. there's nothing to fear about me. he made sure his vow and duty as a nurse to care for me with utmost empathy was executed. i was so sad when i was discharged that i couldn't thank him personally. he is truly an angel. anyone who gets the chance to be cared for by him, is blessed. please let him know, how much my family and i appreciate him!

i never had or seen the type of sloppy careless nurses ever it's such a shame they use covid-19 for there excuses to not see someone...i got a ambulance ride to the emergency for them to have me waiting for 20 mins while the nurses were all walking around laughing..i had one guy he was in all black scrubs just giving me dirty looks and looking at me like he had a problem..so said that this what they had jet fighters fly over for what rude uncaring people so sad so sloppy dirty couldn't even give me a tylenol for pain...

we were induced for labor on a saturday night with an 8pm appointment. when we arrive promptly at 8, we are told they meant to call us and tell us to come 3-4 hours later because they're backed up. they say just wait an hour and we'll have your room ready (which they did). the labor went great, specifically the nursing team. so unbelievably friendly and welcoming. the only downside was it seems they are just under-equipped and understaffed. they had only 1 blood glucose monitor for the entire department and it seemed they have only 1 person on staff who is able to do the things you need. for example, before we could leave, we needed our baby's oxygen test or something. it was supposed to be at 6pm, but here we are at 9:30pm waiting because apparently they have only 1 person on staff who can do this test. this is during covid, so i'm sure glad this hospital is slow otherwise i can imagine waiting hours for anything.

had to be seen at ob triage due to stomach pains at 27 weeks pregnant, baby was fine thankfully but then they wanted to send me down to the er for a possible stomach ulcer. nurses weren't that nice and a dr decided er would be best for me based off of a projects call he had with the nurse. everything was so dirty in the er, i know with covid on the rise hospitals are swamped but being in the medical field myself this was terrible. when i was wheeled into the emergency room there was a man laying on the floor in considerable pain. when we were in the hallway we passed a covid patient being wheeled away, my husband works at st. joes so he knows their usual protocols. just baffled that they would want to send a pregnant woman to the er with the possibility of being exposed to a positive patient. their vitals machine was also obviously very dirty and thr nurse never wiped it down . we opted out of the er visit and will be seeing a pcp for now.

so i brought my 3 week old daughter to the er upon her pediatricians recommendation.

i'm very disappointed with the er medical staff at mercy gilbert. i've heard all great things about them. however when i was checked in at this hospital on tuesday, march 24, i had a completely different experience. 

it all started when i was told by the covid 19 hotline, that i could go to the banner urgent care on higley, to get tested. i waited a good hour before getting called back. (no it wasn't busy) appointment was @ 11:30, i checkin 11:15, called by 12:16pm. once i entered the back room, my legs gave out on me and i ended up collapsing. the nurse helped me to the room and onto the bed. at this point my fever was 102.6 and my body started to have convulsions. the banner urgent care called 911 and i was sent to this hospital. i wasn't tested  for covid 19 with banner urgent care.

i was asked a list of questions by the emt about where i work and have i traveled lately. told them i was a flight attendant based in jfk/nyc. also told them i started experiencing symptoms on monday night march 23. during this time my body was in so much pain and i had this excruciating headache unlike nothing i felt before in my life. 

we quickly arrived (which felt like forever) and i was taken to a room where i was met by er dr. kent first,  then by nurse rene a little later. and i was asked again the same list of questions from each. i just wanted to pop my head off from body at this point because the pain was so unbearable. 

here is where everything went downhill. 
dr.kent said she was going to run a flu and strep test on me. i asked her what will happen when they came back negative. (which i knew were both negative because i have had the flu and strep before and my body has never reacted like this, plus i got the flu shot back in october 2019).

dr. kent became very short with me and slightly raised her voice and seemed very irritated because i wanted to know about getting tested for covid 19 (which the next day my doctor now tested me and i was indeed positive). she was so concerned about state regulations and not admitting me to the hospital, that she sent me home with antibiotics after my xrays showed i had  community-acquired pneumonia and i was told i could return back to work after 3 days if symptoms improved. and when she told me about the pneumonia, dr. kent stood by the curtain and quickly walked away. really?!? 

so i knew something was off with my body and this was not normal, i don't have any underlying health issues. never in my 10 years of flying as a flight attendant have i had pneumonia. i'm in my early 30s and pretty healthy. i went to my doctor now and nurse john shipp was the only one who believed me enough to test me on wednesday, march 25, and by friday (yes two days later) i had a video chat with my doctor now and was positive for covid 19. later on that day i ended up collapsing yet once again experiencing hypoxia (lack of oxygen to the brain) and was admitted to banner baywood hospital. where i spent the next 6 days on antibiotics, blood thinners, and malaria medication hydroxychloroquine. 
if it wasn't for me taking the initiative to find help, i more than likely wouldn't be here today and my child would be motherless.

if not for the doctors, and the doctor i saw yesterday (6/11/2020) for my heart blockage which will require a cath and possible stint or more...i would have given cleveland clinic of vero beach a zero.  i showed up for my heart appt. with dr. vikranth gongidi on time with my wife who knows and understands more of my med conditions that i do.  when i approached the front desk (both of us having our n95 masks on) i started to have them check me in and told the desk i wanted my wife to be in the room with me as the doctor went over my case.  the desk clerk reiterated the cc policy (only you), to which i said, i want my wife in the room with me, to which they had the cardiology administrator (a lady) come out, and before i could utter another word she started in with her montra saying only you can see the doctor, to which i said, "i want you to ask dr. gongidi if she can come in with me because i need her...."  the administrator cut me off once again saying absolutely not, it his cc policy and that is that.  well, boy that did it,  i stated in a very loud voice i want you to go back and ask the doctor if my wife can come in---you are not the doctor, the doctor is so go ask him!!  she  then order the desk clerk to call security on me, and they ended up sending three "jack booted thugs" to harass and threaten me.  at no time did i ever make any threats, but i did use the words, "i am telling you damn it to go back and see what the doctor has to say about this!!"  she just walked away from me.  the your dumb army of thugs came to harass me, a 68 year old with a dangerous heart condition, and having blood pressure of 190/108, to make my stress even worse.  

once my appt. came and the nurse took me in and read my bp it was 210/108!!!!!  she immediately got the doctor, he say me, and after i explained to him how rude and nasty your cardiology administrator was and that all she had to do was say, "sir, let me go and talk to dr. gonjidi for you and see if it is ok or not, it is up to him, or maybe we can conference your wife in or something.  ended up, the good doctor took his phone our of his pocket and said what is your wife's phone number (she was waiting outside in the hot sun).  he called her, conferenced her in to our medical discussion and all was well and understand!!  that's it, that was all that was needed,  no being nasty and rude to paying patients, no saying no!   all that is needed for cc to reap a better understanding with patients is to say, "you are right, you are the patient.  let me check."  that is all that is needed.  as a former military officer and ceo, i do not appreciate anyone tell me flat out no, without checking and doing the proper vetting of the situation.  that is what makes me angry and pisses me off sending my bp spiking....no not do it.
