review:
*do not go to this hospital!* their er staff is unprofessional, rude and has no empathy whatsoever. if i could give it 0 stars i would. i don't even know how this place is still operating. arrived at 6 am with a severe strep throat that is spreading to my ear. i could not swallow, talk and was weak from not eating. 

when we arrived there no one in the waiting room. and no one in the lobby greeting area. my fiancé then had to bang on the glass to get someone's attention after waiting 40 minutes with no greeting, no paperwork. then a lady arrived and she instructed us to wait outside because apparently strep throat could be corona virus. i was compliant and went outside in the cold with my fiancé. 30 minutes later a nurse comes outside to take vitals and instructs us to wait for the doctor who has to screen me before i am allowed inside. mind you i had no fever or other corona symptoms. the nurses knew i was in extreme pain. i waited outside for 1.5 hours and was never seen by the doctor!! my fiancé had to yell through the electric doors for someone to pay attention to us... he was ignored for a while but kept trying to get their attention. after getting the attention of one of the staff he let them know if they could find out how much longer we would have to wait to be seen by the doctor for just a screening not even for treatment - to which the staff responded "you can leave if you want to!" with a very rude and uncaring attitude. my fiancé and i were shocked by the staff laughing, cracking jokes and completely ignoring their patients. i could have gotten better customer service at walmart or the dmv....

after flagging down and crying from pain in front of the nurse she finally claimed there was a glitch in the system and that the doctor could not see me until the "computer was working". yet they were treating patients that got their after i arrived. i ended up leaving and going to culver city urgent care right down the street. they provided excellent care in less than 30 min. they staff at urgent care all told me that they would never recommend this place to any of their patients... if only i had known before i got there. if you value your health and customer service don't step foot in this place. i work in healthcare and i am extremely disappointed. 

they clearly don't care about the reviews. from what i see they gave you a fake email and phone number just to pretend like they care but the hundreds of negative reviews say otherwise!
fac_name: Southern California Hospital at Culver City

review:
if i could i'd give a -0¹!!!!
don't let any of your loved ones visit, stay, or even pass by this place! my brother recently passed on "june 21st" and the reason for quotations is i think he was gone days before. there's an incompassionate and extremely unprofessional "nurse" there by the name of grace who tells any and all people any information about a patient they want want to know about! when grace called to tell my mother that my brother was "code blue" and they were working in him said says "ok i gotta go back in there bye" then just hung up and my mom calls her back and she just says "oh i'm sorry momma he passed we tried" then hung up! as we, my mother and i were crying cause we just lost my brother i started getting messages from family with their condolences i'm like how does everyone know we havent gotten around to making any calls with tears coming out our eyes and boogers coming out our noses! how? so i called june 22nd because i wanted to speak to a supervisor or the one on the highest pedestal regarding some questions, concerns & complaints so they transferred me to "supervisor ray morales" whom is in my opinion as incompetent as the janitor pretending to be a doctor in fact it may have been for all i know. i asked him "about grace and her giving just anybody information about a patients condition who isn't immediate family" he made that sound you make when "you get caught or the jig is up" i said also all the information that grace was giving us "is fishy" i said "honestly i think my brother was gone a lot sooner than the day we were told, i think my brother died a week ago and that's why grace was telling us we had 30 minutes to get there to see his body cause you guys took him out the freezer to thaw a little bit so we can see him so you van throw him back in the freezer!" and he said nothing. no denial, no defense no answers for me none! he just informed me to call the hospital number with extension 333 (satans son's number?) to speak to "quality assurance" i'm like "is that like the surveys to say how you did?" (with sarcasm) he said "it's to let them know you weren't satisfied"  are u kidding me!!! if i'm not satisfied were they gonna give us back my brother or a coupon for 2 for 1??!!! a free hamburger perhaps ‍!? my brother was a life and he mattered to a lot of people not just another "covid-19" count!! my brother went to kaiser in baldwin park on june 11th cause he had trouble swallowing, he did have diabetes and "dysphagia" is a common complication of diabetes. at kaiser there's all kinds of tents outside because no one can go in due to covid-19 so you wait outside and they take your temperature and vitals outside my brother had no fever, no cough so eventually they take him in and tell his girlfriend she can't go in so she's like ok call me when your done as we live a few blocks away he says "ok" and he goes in. she talks to him a few hrs later he said they were gonna give him an mri cause he said "they don't know what's wrong with him and he didnt have covid-19" his girlfriend is like "ok well call and keep me updated" he said "ok"  my brother got transferred to los angeles community hospital and when he got there they told him he they were gonna give him another mri and something about taking spinal fluid then they told him he had covid-19 so he calls his girlfriend crying "come pick me up they're saying i have that sh**!" he was scared and alone!!! utterly alone! there is more to this review but they have a limit to rewiews!

this is by far the worst hospital i have ever encountered. i don't know how these people are still in operation, i trust the fresh out of basic training 18 year old medics when i was in the army a year ago. we waited in the parking lot for over five hours barely being updated by the rude "nurses" that somehow are still employed. i'd rather die at home from flesh eating viruses than trust any of these incompetents with my health. plus they forgot to take care of an elderly family member of mine when he was admitted here.  if you value your health and the health of your family members, steer clear from fannin regional hospital. you will probably die from whatever you have while waiting before they give you inadequate care. just take my advice from personal experience and go somewhere else.

wound up here due to an acute back injury that occurred 2 hours before; on a saturday too. i loved their triage set up which is in front of the er- emergency room department. it was in the shaded area and it was organized. awesome!

i was seen within less than 2 hours of registering. loved that and the er was darn near empty. not so pleased with the diagnosis because they explained that having a mri to diagnosis this injury which was located at the very base of my spine was not warranted because upon her exam i didn't meet the criteria for radio-logical testings.

she was a nurse practitioner and i've encountered some amazing ones and then some that rush in and rush out. this lady rushed out. it's been several weeks now since i injured my back and there is no residual pain. thank goodness. back and brain surgeries/injuries are the top two that send shivers up my spine at the thought of needing to have invasive procedures. 

my niece was born at this hospital over a decade now; place still looks pretty much the same. clean.  i will say that covid-19 has altered, adjusted and tweaked the ways that many businesses are doing business now. i hope emanuel hospital keeps some of their new systems for triaging patients and the positive attitudes; if so i wouldn't mind coming here again.

my dad woke up a few nights in the last couple weeks feeling like he couldn't breathe with a heaviness in his chest. i would talk to him and it would calm down pretty quickly. however, i still did a teledoc consult because better safe than sorry. the doctor who we talked to was adamant that with these symptoms and his age (almost 73) we need to go to the er asap and get an ekg, x-ray, and bloodwork. i asked if it could be stress/anxiety and he kept telling me we need to go and get this done because of the symptoms and his age. that heart problems need to be ruled out. 

so my parents go to emanuel and are there for about 2 hours and they don't do any of the stuff he recommended, even when my mother told them what he said. they prescribed an inhaler and said to talk to his pcp about anxiety medicine. 

i don't get why they didn't even do an ekg? how can you just say it is anxiety after one meeting with someone and no testing? why was this other doctor so adamant but they're not? isn't it better to be safe than sorry? what could an ekg hurt? are they holding back resources? this isn't new york and the hospitals aren't overrun with covid19 patients. i've heard hospitals are actually less busy because people aren't going to the emergency rooms as much. so why couldn't they do at least an ekg? did they get lazy in the last month with less patients and don't want to do anything? i went in once after fainting and stomach pains and even i got an ekg. will never go here or take anyone here as long as i can help it.

horrible service in the er. all they do is come into the room turn the light off and leave. if you ask them for something they don't come back just turn the light and leave. my moms mouth was very dry she wanted water n asked three times each person turned the light off and left. when she went to the bathroom her vitals alarm went off they never came! like someone could be not doing well and they are ignoring alarms! after she came back the bathroom they didn't even hook her back up to the monitor for hours. i would never want to go back here. it's very scary if someone is really sick or serious, imagine what they would feel. my mom was shaky and the doctor slowly assessing her like she had no idea what she was saying and she didn't even try to figure out the issue. they just seem so incompetent from the nurses techs to doctors. the tech came in and starts stocking gowns like is that necessary at a time like this with corona virus? he's so close doesn't know what social distancing means? he should know better, no need to stock a cabinet that is 1-2 feet away from me!

i  just retired and will 
not be picking kaiser permanente as my provider in the future. up until covid-19 i was going to keep them. i have lupus treated with hydroxychloroquine unlike other pharmacies that tried to getting patients who use this drug as regular treatment kaiser simply said you are not getting your medicine eventhough nothing has yet to be proven to help covid-19. i know this drug will remain in my body for a while, then what?? do they get to play hide because it's "the in disease". why do they get to play god and who or what group might be next??
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Sacramento Medical Center

review: my mother is a breast cancer patient and was experiencing severe side effects after her last cycle of chemo. we rushed her to the ed for care. i am a healthcare professional and understand the precautions being taken because of covid. upon arrival to the ed, there was no one at the front door so i walked my mother in because she needed support. after she had already entered and sat down, a security guard came and informed us that she had to walk through the metal detector. if there was really a security issue, a guard should have been at the door instead of waiting inside. after walking inside, i could see the staff was too busy socializing to acknowledge patients coming through the door. after getting registered, my mother was called back to be screened by two nurses. they were very unprofessional, and joking and laughing with one another while my mother was slouched over in discomfort in the chair. i had to ask them to be professional and provide care for my mother who was barely able to sit up on her own. i was asked to leave the waiting room because of covid which i did. i sat outside and could overhear the security guards having an inappropriate conversation at the entrance to the ed as other patients walked in through the doors. i was appalled by the unprofessionalism displayed by all the people i interacted with in the ed. i truly hope we don't have to come back to this ed again for any issues because based on our experience, the staff that work here do not care about their patients.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Sacramento Medical Center

review: my mother had stage 4 pancreatic cancer and was sent to st anthony's by skfd recommendation even though we told them to take her to harrison. the fireman said , oh well st anthony's is a great facility and they would have all my mothers info from harrison. no they didn't. the fireman were to lazy to abide by my mothers wishes. so they sent her to st anthony's to die. during her first evening the doctor called our house and said our mother was in a life ending event and we needed to come up right away. before arriving, i called the head charge nurse to get the latest. she told me she was stable??? i got upset and the head charge nurse started spitting out covid bullshit and i told her to go confirm what's happening with my mother and quit wasting my time with this shit. she told me she wouldn't speak to me if i was cussing at her. i asked her if i could speak to someone with more knowledge about my mother and she said i would have to call back and hung up on me! keep in mind my mother could've been dead already but this jillian or whatever the head charge nurses name was didn't give a shit about my mothers quality of life. my mother wanted to go home and was cleared of covid. this head charge nurse didn't leave any notes about my mother being  cleared of covid for the next shift so my mother had to take another covid test to keep her longer even though the head charge nurse had cleared her that previous evening of covid. this hospital will not go with the wishes of the patient, the staff will only do what's convenient for them. my mother was yelling from her bed with cancer all through her body just to go home and pass peacefully at her home but that was too much for the back water hicks of st anthony hospital to understand. please take your family anywhere else but st anthony!

holy name women's center: as a loyal holy name patient for over 7+ years, i am appalled how i was treated today. i had an appointment for tomorrow which was scheduled months ago. i completely understand why the appointment was cancelled (covid-19 closure). i called in today to reschedule. shelly who took my call immediately had an attitude. i let it go! i asked her if she can reschedule my mom and i (original appointments for tomorrow) and she said no. she was the only staff member at the office and can only reschedule me. fine, i let it go. i had asked her if i can schedule to be the first patient. she ignored my request and said she had a 945am for thurs sometime in july. i asked her if it was the first appointment; she raised her voice and said "no i'm telling you what is available". once again, i let it go. i asked if they had a first appointment sometime in september. she seemed irritated and said it would take a while for her to look through appointments for me. at this point, i told her to forget it. i don't need this nonsense. i was very patient with her and as a long time customer i feel this is completely unnecessary. 

with all that is going on in the world, why would anyone behave this way? not to mention, i'm concerned i can't get my mammogram and ultrasound done at the time i was supposed to get it done. so many people losing jobs and shelly wants to behave as if she is not grateful to even have a job? i"m furious right now! quite frankly, all she had to say was that she was very busy and could call me at a later time to get my appointment situated. perhaps some training on etiquette is in order! you lost a patient. i've dealt with long waits and never complained. stop treating patients like animals.

all kaiser due to this virus kaiser need to find away to open up to people that don't have the symptoms i been dealing with a sinus infection. i tired of have a phone  visit i need to be physically seen by a doctor we all shouldn't have to suffer they need to open up facilities that they just treat people with ear infection  sinus infection yeast infection i feel safer letting a doctor look at me instead of miss diagnosing me with the wrong medication that's not working i am getting so ffrustrated come on kaiser  you all can do better!!!!!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i went in for shoulder surgery, and was concerned about doing it during the covid 19 crisis.  i had a great experience. i was screened immediately when i entered the hospital for the covid virus.b the front desk admin folks were true professionals.  the nurses, doctors and others who gave me treatment from prr-surgery, the actual surgery, and the recovery phase we're all very caring and professional in giving me the best care possible. i highly recommend this hospital over the large, corporate hospitals.  best decision i've ever made.

the way that many rrmc staff have treated me as a patient during this coronavirus pandemic has been terrible! like really, there's no reason to be rude or condescending. rather than kindly give pertinent information, they'd rather just treat you like a leper! i'm being diligent when i leave my home, wearing a protective mask and gloves so i don't pick up germs. but then people think i'm sick! i get people should stay home 24/7, but the pandemic doesn't give medical professionals an excuse to not treat people who need care other than for coronavirus treatment! at rrmc, you get stopped at the door by two staff members. they go through a list of questions. if u say yes to any of them they tell you to leave. if you insist on being treated, they send you to another department. i was then treated like a child by a nurse because according to her i should've called my pcp rather than stay. like i knew that? maybe the folks at the door could've told me that! like hello! i don't want to be there any longer than necessary. i asked how long i would be there because the longer you hang around a hospital, the more chance you have of picking up an illness. some guy in the waiting room was coughing with no mask on! so the staff girl tells me she isn't at liberty to give me a wait time and called a security officer to stand by. at least the doctor who would see me treated me like a human! their excuse that staff "is just scared" is pathetic! you're all medical professionals! you ought to be able to behave accordingly and with "bedside manners"! waiting until after you've upset me to try to make things right is just messed up.
 my advice to people is to stay out of hospitals right now. they don't want you there. they won't be nice  to you. just call and if u have to go, be prepared for the rudeness

don't go here!!! i came to the er for a crohns' disease flare up, and wound up getting covid!!! i know i got it here cause they tested me while i was in the hospital and i was negative then about a week later i was back for stomach symptoms again. of course it was because they didn't treat me during the first visit (pain medicine for a crohns flare is like putting a band aid on a gun shot wound expecting it to heal).  i tested positive on this visit after only spending time in my apartment during the in between time (i still felt like garbage so why go out?). now i need a negative test in order to return to work. they're telling me i can come to their er and pay a copay ($100) and they will test me again. i don't have hundreds of dollars laying around to give this hospital til i test negative especially when it's their fault i got the virus in the first place!!! in addition most of the staff i encountered were extremely rude. one told me to stop crying cause it doesn't do any good as i was writhing in pain unable to control my body (that's what happens when my stomach is on the fritz). i seriously think this hospital should be shut down.

my husband had his knee replacement surgery this morning at oakbend hospital on sw frwy in richmond, tx and so far our experience has been awful. his call button doesn't work, the nurse appears to be very busy, he hasn't had his vitals taken since arriving from recovery 2 1/2 hours ago, his lunch finally arrived at 2:30, he called the nurses desk from his cell phone for a urinal and was offered a diaper!  because of covid 19 i can't be there to advocate for him and i am furious. i called his doctor's nurse and she brushed me off and told me how busy she is. on top of all this nonsense, the anesthesiologist told him how painful this surgery is and then proceeded to tell him that pain meds are addictive and have many negative side effects. so tylenol with codeine is what he is being offered the day of a very painful surgery.  fail oakbend hospital!
fac_name: OakBend Medical Center - Jackson Street Hospital Campus

review: this was my first time admitted to this hospital in corvallis.  i arrived at the er with labored breathing, high fever and severe coughing.  the staff was amazing.  they were so gentle and kind.  because they needed to test me for covid-19 i was isolated and couldn't have family near me.  the nurses became my family and were so very kind.  fortunately, i didn't have covid-19 and was treated for a severe case of pneumonia.  i was in the hospital a total of 5 days and only had kind, caring nurses and informative and gentle doctors.  they truly were angels during a very scary traumatic experience.

labor and delivery department nurses are wonderful. 

i've been anxious while checking-in as my family was not able to stay with me at the hospital due to covid-19 - kids under 12 years old are not allowed so we agreed that my husband will stay at home with our daughter as we didn't know how soon i will deliver the baby and be discharged. 

ashley was the first (night) nurse i met and she made me feel so comfortable and relaxed, she was very caring, she helped me whenever i needed something and supported me when there've been any doubts. 

natashia and vick did a great job during the day hours. 

and finally, channel was the nurse who assisted with the baby delivery, she's amazing! she coached me, and cared for me, and inspired me when i had no more power to proceed. 

when the baby was born she's been placed skin-to-skin on me and she was checked by the doctors right there, we stayed together for a rather long wonderful time before she was taken to that baby-table for weight check and the shot. nurses reminded me and took many photos for me to share with the family. 

i never felt lonely during my stay at the labor and delivery department and received an excellent care. i am very grateful for that to each person whom i met there.

marie was the night nurse at the mother and baby department and i felt at home with her too. she was a great help and so passionate! 

i would like to mention how quick and easy was the process of baby vital documents submission, the lady was great at gathering correctly all the information by phone (we have not so simple names and last names, you know :)). by the way, no issues this time - we received them all soon by mail. 

the meal services were so kind to check with me several times if i really didn't want anything as they 'saw' that i was getting late with the discharge from the hospital. 

it was a great experience. many thanks to everyone involved!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
during the covid-19 healthcare situation, it's nice to see kaiser-scl streamline the screening process so you can enter quickly. i've been to nearly every kaiser hospital in the sf bay area, and this place has the best screening setup.

parking is still a challenge, so come early or late.

campus is at lawrence expressway x homestead, near i-280
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
labor and delivery team 04/02/20 - 04/04/20

i gave birth to my daughter crystalli rose one week ago and had to share our stay while in kaiser. as a first time mom and having to give birth during covid 19 of course i had so many worries and fears. i was pleasantly surprised with how calm, clean and attentive everyone was. from hard working cleaners, maintenance workers administrators, food handlers, nurses and doctors. i felt completely safe and well taken care of. 

i wish i had a kept track of every single nurse and doctor by full name or id number but here are a few that really went above and beyond.

04/02/20: dr. nelson and rn debbie explained every treatment and made sure i was as comfortable and cleaned up as possible. 

04/03/20: aipang was very attentive checking in with me every strong contraction and when my daughters heart rate kept dropping she told me her recommendations and got the approval from the doctor immediately to keep my baby closely monitored. aipang made sure i ate, had juice and stayed active to help prep my body for the next stage of labor. when i finally reached my pain limit and asked her opinion on when to get the epidural she reassured me now was the time and called to have that prepared. 

within minutes the anesthesiologist kevin was there! he was very good at explaining the process to me and coached me to relax my body before placing the epidural. he gave me breaks in between the most intense contractions and checked on me in 20 minutes to make sure i was okay and feeling better! i was able to get sleep, drink fluids and still move around in bed but was numb in all the right places.

04/04/20: rn liz was very sweet and attentive. we had great conversations as see took care of me. when ever my daughters heart rate would dropped she would help me position myself another way and that happened many times. during my active labor she was extremely compassionate and helped me get through my contractions and pain management.  before i knew it it was time to start pushing! she was fantastic explaining and coaching me to push properly. which i greatly appreciated since i was pretty numb down there. 

dr. fernandez explained me options to help assist my delivery. i was scared, exhausted and feeling overwhelmed but she gave me her opinion and understood my wishes( no episiotomy) 

rn velvet was wonderful teaching my husband and i how to feed, hold, burp, clean and bathe our. velvet worked with us to get discharged and back home as quickly as possible. she gave us formula to help the baby urinate and we were finally headed home. our daughter was born completely safe and healthy thanks to the amazing team at kaiser santa clara's l&d department!!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
kaiser permanente facilities, locations, medical and other staff are all fantastic!

however, kp is very bureaucratic and paperwork is worse than a govt. dept.

worst part of kaiser permanente is their billing department..oh! yeah!!

i had this experience with kp billing dept. of telling me that i owe money after i canceled a policy even though i made the payment before canceling. i provided to them bank statement as proof.

apart from this drama, every time you call kp billing they keep transferring the call from one group to another and you have to parrot your story all over again!  

i must say many a staff members (especially ladies) go out of their way to help and sort out problems. they are very patient and helpful but victims of their incompetent leaders because of who they have to face the music. 

kp needs to overhaul their billing dept. leaders all the more because of covid-19 pandemic all transactions happen online (digitally) and they are simply not able to cope with this!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
this review is specifically for the women's imaging department (396). i went twice (once for imaging and once for a minor procedure). everyone was prompt and super nice (from reception, to medical staff, to the md who did my procedure). 

easy parking around 9-10am on a weekday. no long wait. competent staff.

due to covid-19, all the employees in the building appeared cautious of social distancing procedures which i highly appreciate (especially being a medical professional myself). would recommend!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review:
untrained and incompetent staff at the entrance.

being high risk for covid19 and having been in isolation for the march and april i needed medication that kaiser won't deliver by mail.

lathered myself up with hand sanitizer, put on gloves and a mask. i got to the front door, they asked me if i was sick or had a temperature. i told them no. they then asked me to spay my hands with purell. i showed them i had gloves on, they said i still had to spray me hands, so i went and spray my gloves. then they wanted to take off the gloves and spray my hands with purell. 

i tried to explain to them that doesn't make sense if i there only to pickup medication. only my gloves need to spray and they were putting me at risk. so i ask them if they were doctors or certified nurses. no none of them were, so they couldn't understand the concept of cross contamination that could affect me.

now there was two security guards plus the four woman at the tables who all did want to listen to reason or logic. all of whom were rude to begin with and just keep saying this what i was told to do. 

i really wanted to have them call a nurse, doctor, and police just to straighten them out about how to correctly make things safe for everyone. in the interest of not wasting a doctor's time i relented and quickly did it so that i don't have to come into contact with more people than these guys.

kaiser neeeds to have a qualified nurse or doctor supervising the staff at the door for everyone's safety and have everyone use some common sense.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Santa Clara Medical Center

review: do not go to the er here!!!!!! i just spent an hour on the phone trying to figure out why i was charged close to 6000 dollars for a ten minute visit. the hospital billed my insurance, but they let their physicians charge patience independently from the er visit. they did this by charging through a different state. i have ohp and i was sent an 1800 dollar bill on top of the (already covered) er bill... i have since gotten it taken care of, but fuck that shit. this is criminal. plus it was quarantine and the doctor didn't wear a mask.

i have a relative in trinity hospital who is very sick. please avoid this place at all costs. drive the extra distance if you want good care. he hit the call button when his iv fell out. they came in after a few hours cleaned the floor. did not talk to him or fix the iv.  some clothes were dropped off for him that are badly needed. they took the clothes out them in a patient bag and said they would be delivered. 4 hours later he never got them.  went back to hospital the guy outside the er was extremely rude to us and said the nurse picked everything up. not so.  he said everything was logged except for his belongings.  we called the number back that called about him and it just rings no answer. i called manager on call absolutely no help.  this hospital needs to look at leadership starting at the top and resolve the terrible conditions at this hospital. i am terribly disappointed and will 100% of time find care elsewhere. please 
update son in law got released to quarantine at home. was told no need to get checked again to see if covid19 is gone. what hospital in it's right mind would even think of saying something so stupid in this world at this time. find care elsewhere

i wish i could give negative stars. i am 33 weeks pregnant with covid-19 symptoms and they won't have me tested because they claim i don't have symptoms and that my symptoms are pregnancy symptoms (coughing ??) so if i'm positive for this and my baby suffers they are to blame. worst experience ever

this hospital is a joke. none of the doctors seem invested in their patients and their health and they just pass you around to as many specialist and tests as your insurance will allow and nothing actionable seems to come from their results and diagnosis. the doctors are asked to see too many patients, and they don't listen to what you have to say they are just in a hurry to collect on their next appointment. i've spent a lot of time and money seeing doctors here and am ready for a practice that actually will help. i've gotten similar opinions from people without expressing my own first. 

on top of that they've been cancelling appointments for the last two months during this covid issue, which imo you can take precautions but you're a hospital that is probably well equipped and are leaving people with serious conditions out to hang. shame.

not how i planned to spend a saturday night in bethany beach, but here we are.  

my husband knocked his head on a beam in the attic while opening up a client's beach house.  he ended up with a bit of goose-egg knot on his head.   he did not think much of it at the time but the next day, he came down with an excruciating headache, unlike anything he has ever experienced.   worried it was related to the head injury the day before, we decided not to take a chance and took off for what siri told me the closest er to our location.  

i had to wait in the car due to covid restrictions but hubby kept me informed by text throughout the process.   luckily it was only the after effects of a mild concussion and not a more serious head injury (according to the ct scan).  he was pleased with the md he saw and follow-up instructions he received.   he was in and out of there in about an hour too!  hard to believe for a saturday night.

from now on, i think i will make him wear a bike helmet when he is in a low clearance attic.

let me just start off by saying i am a pregnant lady that got diagnosed with covid & pneumonia and was admitted for 4days. 
i've rewritten this many times, because i always go over my character amount. 
the only way i know how to describe my stay is miserable. i was treated like a piece of trash thrown in a room for 4 days. all the nurses i saw acted terrified of me. like they all just wanted to run out of my room as soon as they got in. i'm 100% certain they weren't sure what to do with me since i was a pregnant covid patient. i was in the hospital for 2 days until i saw someone from respiratory, and an ob nurse finally came by to check on my unborn baby on day 2 of my stay at around 10pm. i'm still in disbelief of how my stay went. i went to bayfront instead of sarasota, like my husband wanted me to, because bayfront is in our backyard. i should be able to trust them. but i can't and i won't make that mistake again.

i am in ssh now for the fourth time in four months. i haven't had any problems. sure it is not a luxury hotel with five course meals, but the food is very good. i did not come to this site to write a review but to find out some other information. but after seeing the ratings i had to write this. in my 15 combined days here, i have yet to find a mean/ obnoxious staff member. sure some nurses have been bossy, sticklers to the rules or brusque, but everyone of them have treated me with respect!  especially during this last stay which has occurred during the covid-19 period. yes they have been taxed, but have kept their professionalism!!  do not hesitate to come here. also remember in this life you get what you offer. be nice to the staff and they will be nice to you!
during covid my father fell and injured himself. they would not allow my mother into the er, which is understandable. however, not answering calls about his care is unacceptable.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review: last night was one the worst nights of my life. i went there with chest pains and was checked in and they were very quick about running all the necessary tests. then the nightmare  began.  we waited  4 hours in waiting room where they didn't enforce masking or spacing. finally they took me to an exam room and started the testing all over again and said it would be at least before i would see a doctor. i left after so much frustration.  do not by ever go to this place.
fac_name: General Surgery - Mercy Medical Center - Redding, CA

review:
review based on blood donation. 

during this crazy pandemic i heard that there was a shortage of blood donations due to companies being closed down, and the source for mass blood drives. 

i saw something online about children's reaching out, so i called and they returned my call with a near immediate time/day slot that became available. 

it was easy to find, wasn't busy, and the staff was available to direct me where i had to go which was not too far from the front entrance. 

i liked they had movies playing! great idea! why don't more blood donation centers do this? just gives you something to do besides just sitting there while your waiting to give blood, during giving blood, and after as you're making sure you're alright and snacking. makes total sense! i'd donate here again in a heartbeat.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review: my father has been a patient in your hospital with a fractured hip since friday. i am an rn in a maryland ed and i understand what effect this pandemic is having on our healthcare system; however, you must continue to provide basic nursing care these patients require. he is in isolation pending covid results. i have been unable to speak to his nurse, even after multiple attempts and requests to call me back. it is very difficult on the families who can't visit and it is your responsibility to keep the family informed. my father should not have been told they can't help reposition him in his bed because only 1 staff member is allowed in the room. he had slid down so far in the bed he couldn't even see his food tray. i spoke with him this am and he had still not had 1 meal. he should not have been told "i can't stand here and feed you, i have other patients to care for". i feel helpless. please take better care of your patients. do better and stay safe!!

unfortunately had a medical emergency while i was with family. no better time to have a random ailment strike than during a pandemic, said no in the world, ever, at all, in the history of time.

was taken here and seen immediately by staff, who were all in face masks. they made me hand sanitize before entering. i could see the parking lot immediately outside of the hospital main gate was set up for drive-thru covid-19 testing. 

i was taken to rush care and put in a room where the nurse came promptly and dr. brian park came shortly after that. there was a ton of waiting in between, but understandable due to the current condition of things. they assured me that the covid patients were seen in another wing of the hospital, if that was something i was concerned about.

i was in and out in about 5.5 hours, with almost no time spent in the waiting room. while this was an experience i definitely did not want to have, and almost did not review, i wanted to take the time to thank our healthcare heroes who are working tirelessly to help with covid and all other emergency situations at this time. you are appreciated.

except for the hospitals covid 19 ... management best practices .... which is totally understood & appreceiated  .... 

it's the best hospital in atl

where to start with this place? it's 2020 and as you all know we are experiencing a global health pandemic. a very serious one. it has been brought to my attention that they are refusing to give testing to employees after there have been known active cases of covid-19 in patients within the hospital. they even have pregnant staff members risking their life. there are employees that also work 2 jobs, putting more people at risk. this puts the employees and the patients in imminent danger. i have already contacted the news and will be contacting the bbb to let them know what a horrible job this business is doing. the employees also receive no hazard pay. there was also a therapist that did not want to work with a patient because they had been in contact with said patient that had covid-19 and the therapist was reported for trying to keep themselves safe. this place is a sorry excuse for a hospital and i only hope that you do the right thing for both your employees and patients or understand the consequences of treating your staff as disposable and treating patients like their lives do not matter.

not a place of healing

this place is a scam/honeypot/government subsidized trap house. patients are treated like animals, given no guidance or support, and forced to rely on each other for any real therapy. requests to staff will be brushed off, or you will be given a name (good luck remembering anyone in this super high turnover job) and also they are all wearing covid masks right now).  many of the people behind the nursing station are esl speakers from varying backrounds. they had difficulty speaking to both their coworkers and their patients. 

near the end of my stay i reported that i was having some paranoia and asked the "patient advocate" if there was a therapist i could speak with, i was dismissed with a wishy-washy aswer and left. i never heard from her again. this self-snitching was enough of an excuse for them to keep me another day ($$$) 

i finally managed to get a room all to myself for what i hoped was my final night, however in the middle of the night was awoken to the sound of med techs dragging a new roommate in. the new guy in my room apparently thought he was a snail ("i'm a snailor" - direct quote) and acted like the bug guy from men in black. he was removed from the wing shortly after breakfast and chucking a few full cops of coffee into other peoples rooms and trying to eat his food by spiting all over it like jeff goldbum in the fly.

i still had a spring in my step because of my excitement over going home, only to be told that i had not slept enough last night so i had to stay another day.

yet how can i sleep under this conditions? i felt like i was being blamed for factors outside my my control.

luckily i was able to finally sleep and overcome the many many obstacles, unwritten rules, unfollowed policies, disgruntled employees, etc. etc. etc. and prove that i could take care of myself like an adult (hygiene, laundry, etc) and finalize an outpatient treatment plan.

unless its a last resort, never send anywhere here

my 88 yr old mom was brought to er and was seen right away. x-ray and ultrasound completed within an hour. dr rothkin was so nice! he called and thoroughly explained what was being done and even sent photos of her x-ray. she'll be discharged soon.  couldn't be happier with the nurses and doctor today, esp during these crazy corona times.

i've never had any issues or complaints with the service kaiser provides.  amidst all the chaos and scare of the covid-19 they are doing their best to keep the public calm and safe. i appreciate the containment of the entrance into the facility.  wash stations immediately placed outside the door.  nurses and doctors on duty screening all who enter the facility.  you couldn't turn a corner without an employee present to answer any questions.  they are being proactive professional and patient. accommodating and kind during this time.  this is why i still chose kaiser.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Leandro Medical Center

review: this yelp review is for dr. bedi and his medical assistant craig lewis. these two went above and beyond to make sure i got a work requested physical. due to the covid-19 pandemic everyone's doctor appointment was canceled excluding mine because these guys knew the importance of me getting my physical done asap for a great employment opportunity. i can't thank you two enough for going above and beyond for me.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Leandro Medical Center

review: if i could give 0 stars on behalf of dr. raman soi .the worst dr ever goes to dr. raman soi she does not do her job never has appointments, never takes care of patient concerns,  other physicians always are reaching me  filling in for her instead of my actual physician ! i'm still trying to have a condition i have been dealing with for now 3 months resolved because she has been failing to do her job and this has gone on well before the pandemic. so the pandemic isn't the excuse. she has been this way well before the virus. always have to book 2 to 3 months in advance i have only managed to get 1 in person visit when i first met her 3 years ago. thats how booked she always is. i always go to my obgyn because dr raman soi is horrible! if you don't want a dr who never responds to your concerns, never has appts, and treats your health like a joke do not pick raman soi as your dr you will be highly disappointed. currently in the process of changing drs and possibly seeking an attorney to sue since my condition is progressed into something worse since she has neglected to take my health serious. some kaiser drs literally are shitty and i ended up with the worst of the bunch. do not pick raman soi as your dr if you care about your health she is the worst. i have already filed a grievance with member services. i just want to make sure nobody else deals with this dr who has been a complete nightmare to my life!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Leandro Medical Center

review:
this is my very first review of any kind but i had to do it because of how unsettled i feel. had to bring my elderly mother to the hospital, hesitantly because of the current global health crisis. she needed to come into the orthopedic department to have her cast removed and see a doctor for her injury.

we took the necessary precautions to minimize our possible exposure by wearing a mask and gloves. upon arriving at orthopedics and checking in an older heavyset man by the name of "rick" called my mother into the department. he told us that he will be cutting off her cast and walked us down a hallway to the cast room. he than told my mother that he will be using the "cast saw" to remove her cast, turned it on without warning us of the loud noise it made and how safe it was. but what i found most disturbing was that he handled the machine with his bare hands (no gloves). he proceeded to put the saw blade to his hand and stated "it won't cut". he continued to remove the cast off my mother while touching her bare handed no gloves!!! he never washed his hands before or after handling my mother!

i looked at his badge to check for his title and shockingly he is a "sr. orthopedic tech". this is very disappointing, that someone who appears to have the experience needed in order to have that title is that incompetent and ignores the simplest of personal protection such as gloves. 

it is very troubling that during this time of global health crisis kaiser allows people like rick to hold a job at a place where you would expect the highest level of safety. no apology needed kaiser, save it for the next person one of your employees hurts.

review: i've been wanting to post bad reviews all week but then a nice nurse has the shift that day and i change my mind. today they didn't let me in because of covid 19. my grandma is 91 and she doesn't like to ask for help. most of the nurses dont check on there patients until you push the button. my grandma never pushes the button even if she in pain. please please check on your patients at least once an hour ask them if there in pain if they need something f there hungry.  thank you   update, my grandma said you guys took care of her while we were not allowed to go in. there's a few things i should complain about but will leave it alone. thank you for taking care of her

my mom was just discharged from this horrible county like "hospital". we couldn't make sure she was receiving proper care since we couldn't be with her. first i call the main hospital number this morning, june 24, 2020 at 8am to inquire about my 67yr old mother's condition and the phone rang for minutes then i was disconnected, finally i reach someone and he gives me the rm # and ext and hangs up. i call back and again the main number rings so many times. i tried this about 3 times. finally i ask for her unit and a nurse answers. i told her i want to know about my mother's condition, she rudely responds, "she's stable what else do you need"? finally my mom is discharged and told us her diaper wasn't changed for 2 days, she wasn't fed and nurses hardly checked on her. my mom does not wear diapers, so why would these lazy nurses have her on diapers and not change her for 2 days? she also said as she was being discharged, the rude and unprofessional, careless nurse told her to "hurry up" knowing damn well my mother just had surgery. how dare you speak that way to a 67yr old patient or to anyone for that matter. i'm still gathering details of her horrible treatment and will definitely file a complaint with medicare cms, dhs, patient rights, our attorney and whoever i need to start an investigation of improper care for my mother who in fact has medicare coverage. too many of these incompetent nurses get away with mistreating these elderly patients knowing family are not allowed to be there due to the covid visiting restrictions. the nurses and staff involved in the lack of care for my mom need to be disciplined for the mistreatment of my mother. i will attempt to contact the patient liaison, if this so called hospital has one. i can't believe this hospital hasn't been shut down after reading all these horrible reviews. i hope the nurses who mistreated my mother experience karma with their own parents, so they know how disgusted we feel. taking advantage of the fact that no one was there to speak up for her. i'm so furious this happened and will do whatever i can to make sure i'm heard!

community hospital of huntington park ceo, cfo do you not read or care about your hospital's reputation? don't you read or attempt to make your hospital a better place? sounds like all you're interested in is a paycheck. so sad.

usually a great place to receive care, this covid virus has the world in a jumble and while things are consistently changing i feel kaiser is having a hard time understanding how the patients feel about their harsh restrictions of visitors during this time. while kaiser made sure to cancel all future appointments for my pregnant wife , they failed to mention visitor policy updates. usually i wouldn't fuss but this is the most important ultrasound and kaiser has found a way to take the enjoyment out of this process. and not all hospitals are taking such extreme measures so forgive me for thinking that it jus seems too harsh but others are not as bad. 


for the record i understand what's at stake i am merely pointing out that somewhere along the way kaiser has dropped the ball and while i may be able to get over this , some people who are in a more dire situation may not be.

review: this review pertains to the opthomology/optometry department in the parkview building. i was pleasantly surprised to find my experience with kaiser's eye specialists to be excellent, even more so than the private specialists i used to see when i was living in the bay area. i never seemed to have to wait more than 5-10 minutes after checking in - even when i was early - which is an amazing feat in healthcare! all my specialists were very kind, approachable, and easy to understand. my retinal specialist, dr. nader ameli unfortunately was not able to see me in person due to the coronavirus concerns, but we instead had a phone consultation which was also a good experience. i could not be any happier with my experience here so far. thank you for all you do!

review:
we went to visit on friday the first day the hospital has allowed visitors since covid.  it was a disaster. i waited on a long line outside before finally getting in the front door. there was a very large group of people inside also waiting to get upstairs. absolutely no social distancing. we were on top of each other. i get that it was the first day, however, you had three months to prepare for this day. you waited on one line to check in and then another line to get your temperature taken and then another one to get a mask that people were putting their hand in the box to get one. i passed and just kept the one i was wearing.  and yet another line to wait for the elevator. only two people allowed in the elevator. why?  i was just exposed to at least thirty people.
then on the way out i couldn't find the exit door. the revolving door was locked (fire hazard), and someone in a wheelchair was blocking the one exit door.
again, you had three months to prepare for this day.

never again! i have never left a bad review of any kind anywhere, so this is my first.  we have lived here 7 years and heard all kinds of bad about palmetto richlands. since they are not as hard to get into see, we thought we'd give them a try. keep in mind this is the first real experience we have had at any hospital since moving to sc 7 years ago.  because of the major health issues he is having, and never having used any area hospital for services, we were already nervous. 

we came in this morning for my husband to have a colonoscopy and were told that due to the corona virus circumstances, only one visitor would be allowed per patient. patients receiving anesthesia, we were told, would be allowed to have 1 visitor.  the new security guard at the front desk sent us to the 3rd floor. upon arrival, the lady at the front sucked her teeth and asked us what we were doing up there. she seemed bothered by the fact that we were there at all. who knew people showed up at the hospital only to harass the staff members?  i did get her name and plan on reporting her--not that it will do a bit of good.  she also said that i had no business being up there and asked what i was doing with the patient. 

the security guard had sent us to the wrong  place. (i get it. she's new. no big deal). we went back down to "register" and they kicked me out. there were no instructions about his belongings, about who would contact me, there was no discussion as to where i could go pick him up, absolutely nothing!  in fact, i wasn't given the opportunity to even ask those questions. no one told me if i'd have a chance to speak to the doctor, they just said i had to go. (until it was time to pay, and they asked my husband to call me to come inside to bring payment).  

these people (with the exception of security) are very rude and have zero communication skills. it was no big deal to have to stay out of the hospital. we understand the virus has everything changed. the fact is they handled it totally wrong. when we ore-registered the previous day they told us nothing about the virus procedures causing issues with a visitor who may have questions after the procedure. we were told nothing!!  we were given no instructions. 

never again will i use this hospital system, and i will tell everyone i know to steer clear!!  i only left one star because i had no choice. staff needs some training on how to handle things during "quarantine mode." based on the attitudes, i'm not convinced that had anything to do with it though. hate the place and will never be back!!! we will likely have his records transferred over to lexington as soon as we possibly can.  save your time and don't bother with the doctors at prisma health/palmetto richlands, go 1 county over to lexington. there's a legitimate reason everybody wants to go there, and now i know what it is.

i was air lifted to this hospital from parker on april 2nd as a trauma patient caused by a truck roll over accident... at the same time i became a potential for covid-19 due to ct scans showing "glassy characteristics" which relate to covid-19. although it was likely due to the blunt trauma caused by the airbags which led to me coughing blood, the hospital still deemed it as a potential- which i totally understand... needless to say it was a scary experience and through it all the entire staff was amazing... upon my isolation in the negative pressure room my limbs were previously relocated.. i was in mass amount of pain and unable to maneuver out of bed, let alone use the bathroom or feed myself.. despite the pain medications administered.. my very first nurse assigned to me that night.. took care of me like a mother would! despite the covid-19 potential on my chart, she tended to my needs beyond expectation while of course wearing appropriate gear.. silvia f. was on her name tag.. after she helped me relieve myself of urine as i was unable to use my hands or get out of the bed, she was able to get me food and then spoon fed me!! amazing, caring soul. i never got the chance to thank her after that night because i assume she was relocated, but i hope she sees this.. furthermore as the days went on, each nurse and doctor i encountered was amazing and made my stay tolerable through the pain... i just want you all to know how much i appreciate you taking care of me and keeping me alive when i was at critical condition 86% oxygen while on three liters...

once my covid-19 test results came back negative sunday morning, i was released as i did not have any broken bones (a miracle). i'm currently at home recovering thinking about how i wanted to send 1 east edible arrangements as a thank you... but - seeing as how covid-19 would likely prevent that delivery and consumption, i thought i'd leave a review here.

i am so upset with the care my 81 year old father had while he stayed at the hospital. his doctor excellent the nurses on staff horrible. first of all i realize covid-19 is going on and they may have been busy. however, you do not forget about your patient. not only did they forget to feed him once but twice. my poor dad had to call me to tell me he was hungry and they forgot about him. when he finally got dinner at 9pm they gave him carrots and cabbage because they ran out of food. the next day he was supposed to be released at 11am but, he didn't get released till 2pm. during this time they didn't feed him. this is when i found out all this was happening because he didn't tell me till release day. i called and spoke to the nurse on duty and they apologized and said they forgot. i mean my father is elderly and just had lung cancer removal, i'm not asking for special treatment for my dad but he shouldn't have to call me to get a nurse for him. totally unacceptable! i highly suggest anyone who has their elderly parent in this hospital to constantly check up on them. he was in the hospital for 4 days, first couple of days they were attentive, the last couple days care horrible! i mean if i had the right to go and visit him while there, i would have fed him myself!

i went out to the back yard with my dog so she could relieve herself - it was approximately 6:00 am. i then got the urge to use the bathroom, then rushed upstairs. i was sitting on the toilet and instantly began sweating out of every pore of my body. i was weak, scared, nauseated - so i did what many of us do and called 911. got in the ambulance to go to the emergency room. i was only there for help.
i don't currently have insurance so i don't go to the e.r. unless i'm really worried that i need professional support. i was discharged with no covid-19 test,i was still vomiting i was given no iv support. i had to ask for anti nausea drugs - they did give me one round but i was still vomiting and the rudeness from the nurse was off the charts. and most the rest were not to much better. the overall compassion and level of care was obsolete. i am hopeful that they will wake up and do their job or better yet find a new one. shame on you for treating the members of your community so poorly when they are there for your help. yes, i totally understand that a pandemic is underway. however, this is the third time in a row i have endured the same treatment from the staff of the er. they said the only reason they didn't give a covid-19 test was my current lack of fever. after i got home, my temp was 100.1 and climbing. nope, not going there again.

i had coronavirus symptoms 8 days ago (started on thursday 3/12), i've been to the emergency on friday 3/13 at 8:30am to get tested, so i can let know my employer, co-workers and family.
i've been waiting for 3.30 hours, and for some time outside, on a rainy day, with high fever and flu symptoms.
they told me i should wait 4 to 5 days to get my results, so i called 5 days later, then they told me one more day, so i just called them and now i should wait for them to call me back and that, if i gave them accurate information, they "should" call me back... and actually, they looked pretty confused and non organized when i get the test and they collected my information.
so it's been a week, and i still don't know. i behaved as a responsible person and quarantine myself, just in case, but they also told me , this is up to me... so if i have the virus, i'm free to go out and contamine others...
this hospital is just the closest from home, but i'll do my best not to have to go back there again!
i went in at 10:17 pm on a sunday night during the covid-19 pandemic. i was in and out in less than 40 minutes. they were prompt and caring. great er staff.

review:
one of the finest nonprofit healthcare systems in massachusetts. my mother in law and sister in law have both been admitted 3-4 times over the past few years due to elderly related and other issues. the staff overall provided professional and compassionate care. both of them required physical therapy. mrmc advocacy team made the transition from a hospital stay to a rehab facility a smooth process. this eliminated the worry families experience regarding loved ones care.

during the covid-19 crisis, the staff was very creative with addressing protective wear shortages. they made plastic gowns from huge rolls of plastic sheeting donated by local businesses. an assembly line was setup in the cafeteria area where the gowns were made.

visited the emergency dept many times.  great staffing, nice people, great  professional communication between staff and with patients very respectful. . clean and sanitized well especially with covid 19 and their extra precautions in place. 
been admitted to a nice private room which the whole floor was private rooms.  very attentive respectful staff.  kept you well informed. great experience with many depts.  and interactions.

i had to go to the er this past weekend for a non covid-19 related issue.
the care itself was very good, nurses and doctors compassionate.
i was however, surprised that one nurse used no gloves or mask. i was sick in the restroom and it was not cleaned up in the several hours that i was there...which was most concerning, even though i alerted them immediately.  so the sanitary conditions were the concern.

i still give a 2 star for the gal at the admitting desk in the lobby...awhile back...grrh

but the er...during this time of pandemic, and restricted hospital entry, i had to rush my husband in and my goodness they were spot on, with a wheel chair at the car to get him...yay.
and larry rn was there got the info and whisked him away...every half hour he was checked...right now you can not go in with your loved one, so we both were worried, but my goodness they were amazing, calling me and being so attentive to him...he knows them all by name is at ease, and slowly recovering yay!!!
i can not say enough good...and thank you all...

i came in during he covid  period. 

the staff from:

nursing care. both friendly and professional. i did not feel like their kid but also not a stranger.
physician care.  capable and professional in helping me understand what had happened and what we were going to be doing for my care.

i came via ambulance to this hospital because of the emt's suggestion.  huge mistake!   i was put in the waiting room for 6 hours.  while waiting, there were no masks required.  a man was coughing, i asked the triage nurses if he could be asked to put a mask on and was advised that it was "his choice."  i was discharged from the hospital.  however, they neglected to tell me that my potassium was critically low (even though they tested it). two days later, i ended up at piedmont hospital with the early signs of a heart attack due to low potassium.  and... piedmont requires everyone to put on a mask at the door (which should be done at all hospitals during a pandemic).  i ended up being admitted to piedmont for five days due to paulding's negligence.  i am having the case reviewed because the treatment or lack there of almost killed me.  i wouldn't take a dog to this hospital. i have called the emergency room manager and the patient representative twice. i have yet to receive a response.

i've been coming down here and visiting family member and the valet parking guy name sam very friendly great customer service i'm glad he's back he's been gone for a long time again we appreciate he's attitude service to coronado hospital to valet the car's 

thank you
i had to bring my son into the ed with neurological symptoms. the entire care team was amazing!  melvin & dr. apel delivered safe and thorough care to my 24 year old "baby"!!!  #lovesharpcoronado

my experience on 3/16/20 left me in tears, well actually, bawling. i had been experiencing covid-19 like symptoms for weeks with no relief. my doctor had already done a full blood panel and tested me for mono, strep, and flu. my doctor's office did not have tests so i was referred to go to an emergency room. i arrived at sharp and waited at least 2 hours before being seen by a doctor. this wouldn't have bothered me except for someone with the same concern of covid-19 that got there an hour after me was seen first. while waiting i was tested (for the third time at that point) for strep and the flu. what do you know, they came back negative! my doctor had already done the rapid and culture tests. i was finally seen by a doctor for maybe a full 5 minutes before a nurse came in with my discharge papers asking for my signature. upon looking over the papers i realized my concerns hadn't been addressed and i wanted a re-assessment. i let the nurse know it was not her fault but i wasn't going to sign the papers for a visit i didn't feel was complete. the nurse proceeded to tell me, and i quote, "i don't care if you sign, the doctor has already discharged you from the system." she first lied and told me no other doctors were available until i told her i had seen another one and was able to name him. she hesitated before leaving the room and returning with the other doctor. i was happy when i saw him but he said if i want a reassessment i need to go back and join the waitlist again and i'd be charged for a second visit. er bills are disgracefully large as is, let alone could i afford a second one. as soon as the words "i can't afford that" slipped my mouth he instantly turned and walked away. by then i was so frustrated i walked out and sat in my car crying. i was shocked at the lack of empathy from people who are in the business of taking care of others. i wasn't taken seriously and feel like i was just another number. the service here seriously needs re-evaluated, i will avoid sharp facilities from now on.

if you really need medical attention, dont go here. dr. bealy, rn's bo and tyler. they just dont care. you sit there and listen to the staff just laugh. i guess its just the pressure of covid-19. my neice and nephew were born there when they had maternity ward. they have done wonderful things in the past, but now. they will shame and humiliate you for asking for help.

i have always had a great experience at the sharp coronado hospital lab. the staff are so caring and professional. my annual physical just occurred and i again visited the great team in the lab for my routine bloodwork. excellent patient experience, as always! thanks!

lot of blood internally, and therefore, they requested to transfer him to scripps mercy, since they have one of the biggest blood banks in the county. my brother to this day is still confined at the it sucks with the covid-19....my daughter was involved in a car accident and transported via ambulance to this place. so i cant go in and see her...but they grill her on the accident and leave her sobbing and making it her fault!! what the hell?? treat her broken/ shattered wrist and make her feel welcome!! the accident was not her fault, some guy pulled out in front of her...and they want to grill a 18yr old and make her cry it's not her fault. stigmatizing an 18r old driver??? with a shattered wrist due for surgery???

i haven't been in a hospital since i was two years old having my tonsils out. seriously, several decades (like 6?). and during this covid-19 pandemic, a hospital is the last place i want to set foot in. but my doctor ordered an echocardiogram for me anyway and off i went to the imaging dept at legacy meridian park medical center. 

upon entering the main lobby, i was directed to sanitize my hands, secure my mask and had my temperature taken (96.8 thank you very much). the imaging technician, eric, came out and directed me to the procedure room. i had to put on one of those ridiculously small hospital gowns and lye on my side on the imaging table. if you've never had an echocardiogram, it's basically a test that uses ultrasound to show how your heart muscle and valves are working. the sound waves make moving pictures of your heart so your doctor can get a good look at its size and shape. it's totally painless, although the clear gel they use to get the instrument to glide over your skin is hella cold! being a big chicken, i kept my eyes shut tight and didn't look at the monitor as eric worked. my test took less than an hour and included an injection of dye to get a really clear picture. a technician from the physiology dept was on-call to insert the iv for the dye. he saw my anxiety and joked by asking me where i'd like him to stick the needle to start the iv. i told him i had no idea, wherever was easiest for him. "how about your neck?" he smiled and i laughed out loud. everything was ok after that.

my whole experience was phenomenal! every staff person i met was professional and empathetic. covid-19 protocols were being strictly followed and i couldn't have asked for better care.

i was visiting my in-laws and need to take a trip to the clinic. i need some answers and a chest x-ray. long story short i had the flu in february but my cough lingered for over a month. i'm not sure if was a combination of the cold air and wood burning fire place that made my cough worse but i was having issues breathing. i had seen 2 other physicians in las vegas prior to heading into the clinic and my medications were not helping. 

i was able to schedule a appointment which was nice. the paper work was complicated for me and i was provided a mask (since i was coughing). the staff up front was very friendly and everything seemed very clean. 

the doctor that saw me was amazing. maybe because we were in a small town she actually had time to listen to me. i forgot her name but she was a beautiful african american woman. she made me feel very comfortable and was able to prescribe me with a medication that helped me almost immediately. she also sent me for a chest x-ray. do to covid-19 (which was ruled out in my case) i was asked to walk around the hospital to get my x-ray.

review: under no circumstances should you send a loved one to this facility.  my brother suffered a stroke and was transferred via east jeff to this facility for "long term" care.  at the time, he was unable to speak due to a ventilator, and with covid he was not allowed to have anyone (not even his wife) see him.  so all we could do as a family is to take the word of the nurses and so called "care coordinators".  what a joke.  we were told he was being given physical, speech and occupational therapy...only thing they did was sit him up on the side of the bed one time.  in several weeks there (before being transferred to a legit facility), they did not brush his teeth, much less give him anything but the side eye from nurses who seemed to care less.   one morning, out of nowhere they called my sister in law to tell her he was being transferred to a nursing home...ummm, no he isn't (i'm sure they are "affiliated" with what we refer to as the "dump nursing home").  we were told that if he stayed one night waiting for the preferred (legit) facility, it would be medicare fraud.   but claiming and probably billing for therapy and treatment he never received is also medicare fraud!  now that he is able to speak, he has told us what a horrific place this is and knowing what i know now, i wouldn't recommend this place for long term kennel care for my dog!   if you can avoid this place - do so.  they transferred him finally, but with pneumonia and a uti - very disgusting place.  if your loved one needs long term care, run like hell and fight to get them into an acceptable facility.  i suggest a place with a long running history of excellent health care in the nola area...it starts with o.   just saying, the experience has been like night and day.

this review is for west gables health care center, which is housed within west gables rehabilitation hospital. this photograph is of my 92 yr old mother's leg taken, april 14, 2020, upon her arrival home after her discharge from west gables healthcare center. the photograph depicts a large gash / open wound on the side of her calf. my mother was at west gables healthcare center from march 24, 2020 through april 14, 2020.  during her time there, i was never informed of the severity or any treatment of the wound on her leg.  i only received a phone call from a nurse who said my mother scratched her leg and she had a small cut which was being treated.  at no time did the nurse inform me of the severity of the gash / wound on her leg, nor did the nurse or anyone ever contact me or advise me of her treatment and / or progress regarding this wound.  in fact, i spoke to her attending physician, dr. homero rivero, on several occasions and he did not once speak to me about the wound despite extensive conversations regarding other medical issues concerning my mother.  additionally, because i was not allowed to visit due to the coronavirus pandemic restrictions, i also called west gables daily to speak to the nurses who attended my mother throughout her stay there, and never was anything regarding the wound ever mentioned to me. needless to say, i am extremely concerned about the possible consequences of such a severe wound being left seemingly untreated on the my mother's leg, especially since she is 92 years old. this neglect of a 92-year-old patient in their care is unconscionable and i will do everything in my power so that this does not happen to any other patient at west gables healthcare center. i reported them to the joint commission on accreditation of healthcare, ahca and other  pertinent agencies. they discharged my mother  without wound care orders and she was discharged with an open wound that now appears to be necrotic. stay away from this facility!

marian regional medical center had the best newborn baby and mommy care i could have ever imagined.  their doctors and nurses were knowledgeable, extremely attentive, and caring.  we were proud to have had both of our sons in this facility.  the experience could not have been better.

and then there is the emergency room.  our visits with our sick kids were anything but a pleasant experience.  they amounted to nothing more than:

"hey, your son has a fever and an ear infection, but sometimes fevers are a good thing, so just let it ride.  here's a bill for $500-700".  "he'll be able to sleep once he's exhausted from the pain."  we learned to rely on our physician for much better care solely.

today, i received a frantic call from my wife stating that her mom fell down the stairs, and she called the ambulance.  the ambulance brought her to marian.  when i got to marian, the nurses were dismissive.  i told them who i was and asked if my wife was with her mom.  her mother has dementia and can't always speak for herself.  i don't know what was done with my mother-in-law because the nurses wouldn't even entertain my questions.  the nurse there gave me a number to call but then told not to call because the nurses would be busy.  what the heck kind of response is that?  they wouldn't even tell me if she was breathing.

my wife provided them with legal and medical documents stating that fact.  the staff didn't review the documents my wife submitted adequately.  her mom's hospital paperwork contained nothing regarding a living will or legal responsibility.  the staff didn't give her the time of day.  additionally, due to covid-19 precautions, my wife still was not allowed to be by her side.  these actions appear to be contrary to the dignity health website.  

we called around the hospital directory and reached the floor manager who, unlike those greeting patients, was very understandable.  she put us through to the nurse treating my wife's mom.  the nurse exhibited professionalism on the phone and thankfully allowed us to speak with her mom.  her mom was very curt regarding how they handled her.  

the nurse ultimately notified us that they performed all necessary checks, and there were no fractures of any kind.  when we inquired about the possibility of a fracture she sustained in her spine, before this event, becoming worse as a result of the fall, suddenly, they spotted the fracture.  they would not pursue an mri to determine if the fracture became worse.  

in the end, they said, "good-to-go," gave her some pill and left her behind the doors to the emergency room lobby waiting for me to show up, alone, with her belongings inside of a trash bag.  my mother-in-law was so angry.  it's like they handled her akin to something in a production line.  

marian should not pretend to be filled with blindly compliant staff.  if it happened to any of their loved ones, you know they would be there as an advocate or as a visitor.  my wife wasn't a visitor wanting to spend time with mommy.  she was to speak for her legally and medically.  it would have saved time for everyone involved.  in this manner, people wouldn't have rushed to read the results of the examination and get it wrong.    

it's a tough job the er staff chose--no doubt about it.  however, it's human beings and their advocates you're handling.
