review:
this review is dedicated to my son, who is now at home and about one week-old.  looking back as parents who started a bit late in life, the decision to start a family, the actual pregnancy process, and labor and delivery all take a mental, physical, financial and emotional toll.  covid-19 does not make it easier for anyone.  in the end, it was all worth it! 

stanford valleycare was there for us all the way through, and i'm happy to give 5-stars for the ob (dr. adey) and labor and delivery department, especially all the nurses and assistants.  because of them we have our son!  shoutouts to india, jacque, brianna, jennifer, judy, geri, dr. phillips, dr. silverstein, kristen, suzanne, emily, maddie, elena, elaine, heather, yuke, lang, beth, kim,  becky, and lizet.  sorry if i left anyone off, since lots of folks helped out.

delivery room: why so many people to acknowledge?  my wife went through 4-days of labor induction that needed 24/7 care.  based on some recent blood tests, the doctors recommended we induce labor some 4-weeks ahead of the due date.  when there are conditions that can potentially harm the baby at full term, an ob may elect to use drugs, foley bulbs, and combinations to help dilate the cervix and trigger active labor.  they monitor fetal heart rate and mom's contractions continuously during this process.  the process is uncomfortable and sometimes painful, and can range from 2-hrs to 3 days, since every woman and pregnancy is different.  our efforts did not work out as expected, so we went for the c-section, regarded as a "nuclear option". the 4-day induction period was not a total waste, since baby still had time in the womb to grow and develop.

c-section: its sounds scary, but the planned c-section was fast (5-10 mins) and painless according to the wife.  the pain and recovery comes afterwards, since it is a major surgical procedure.  dr. adey did her magic to ensure a smooth delivery.  recovery is lots of rest and otc painkillers followed by light exercise and returning to a normal diet.

recovery: we got 3-days for recovery in the hospital, which gave me a bed to stay as well.  all meals for mom is free and delivered by room service, while for me it was $10/meal using vouchers.  it is during recovery where the baby rooms with us while mom recovers.  here, the baby will be poked, prodded, and tested to ensure good health prior to release.  as for the parents, you get a 2-3 day crash course in newborn care.  surprised we learned diaper changing, installing baby in car seat, burping, blanket swaddling, holding the baby, and feeding (finger feeding, breast feeding, breast-feeding with supplemental tube, and bottle formula feeding).  you'll learn how often and how much to feed.  for breastfeeding, they'll offer excellent lactation consultants and nurses who can also provide breast pumps.  don't worry if you have't picked out a pediatrician yet - the visiting staff pediatrician will help you administer tests, answer questions, and schedule postpartum tests until you choose a permanent one later.

overall:  highly recommend valleycare for labor and delivery.  free and fast wifi great to pass time during labor, and the nursing staff here is amazing.  pregnancy, labor, and delivery do not always go according to plan, so have faith and put your trust to the experts at valleycare.  thanks again to dr. adey for working her magic to deliver our son!

it's been awhile since i've written a review and since with the covid scare all the restaurants in town are closed i decided to try out one of our longest standing eateries, the powell valley health clinic.  since you can't just leave a single review at such a fine establishment, this is part 1 of 2.  starting off, i would say the curb appeal is better than in the past with multiple extra signs telling you exactly where to park which is helpful when you can't breathe, you're dizzy, and have no depth perception to begin with.  
   you're greeted at the door by what i assume is a welcoming smile behind that mask where you are asked additional questions to further accommodate you.  a hard dry cough, fever, and dizziness even gets you a shiny red sticker on your chest so that others know you've made reservations and you can use the disney-like 'fast pass' line.  a mask, some gloves, and bam! you're in!  
   the maîte d' is of course the first person you'll see, and as the position dictates in any fine establishment, they are very knowledgeable of past stays, have payment info and address on file, and will have any paperwork ready to go to speed up the process.  after just a few quick minutes of waiting...while staring at the assortment of magazines and wondering if i dared touch them...i was called in.  
   at this time i go back and they take measurements, height and weight, and then it's time to see my personal physician's physician's assistant.  some more vitals are taken here and then bam!  one step closer to salvation and feeling better!  next came the physician's assistant - finally! the person i was waiting for.  the physician is gone for the day, but the training everyone here has is impeccable..and if it's not, how would you know? 
     we went through the symptoms again and took a look at my tonsils.  then we called in a physician for a quick consult and take a swab of my tonsils and throat to grow a culture and wham bam, problem solved!  my problem?  i didn't wait long enough to see if it would go away!  silly me!  
     exiting was even easier than coming in with no lines or stops, and since they already knew where to send the bill for my visit i was back in my truck and headed home to try and not die!!  overall my stay left me feeling wanting.  i was in a lot of pain, hadn't been able to swallow since the night before, so no water or food but hopefully it would all work out.  i had no answers, only more questions, and pretty scared to be honest, but i have faith in the people put in place to protect me.  the staff was very pleasant in that small tight-knit country community vibe you've come to expect in powell, and so after saying very painful but socially required thank you's i was out.  
     i feel nothing but the best for this establishment and the people working hard to keep our community safe in these uncertain times.  they're at the front lines - not just when it's in the news, but all the time.  caring for you, your loved ones, and being there for all of us in our most vulnerable moments.  i came back to the powell valley hospital the next day, but as i am not yet done with my current stay i'll have to hold off on writing my next review - spoiler, this will include hotel and restaurant amenities!!

my child was struggling with depression and was hospitalized at this death trap.  he was on a floor with other children with active covid and staff knew.  they purposely withheld this information from me, his mother, knowing i would pull him out. my 90 year old mother and my daughter with cancer are very high risk.  the staff at streamwood put their own need for profit over the health of my child and my family.  there will be hell to pay if anyone in my family gets sick.  i am livid and will ensure no other family has to deal with this disgustingly poor level of care.  i am calling the state and the licensing bodies.

i had such a great experience here today and was pretty concerned considering some of the other reviews. i did not experience anything negative. in fact from scheduling until the end was impressive. i was seen for my yearly mammogram.

note:  i was seen today, 3/25/2020, during the coronavirus epidemic.

scheduling, i was given very detailed instructions on where to park, signs to look for and where to register when i was in the hospital.

the day before i was called to see about rescheduling for after the pandemic. i shared that i would need to call and reschedule because i was losing my health insurance. she didn't hesitate and said no way, they'd still see me.

right now things may be different. in fact, before i entered i was asked the covid-19 questions, if i had traveled outside the country and if i was feeling ok, throat, cough etc.

i went to the registration desk and was seen very quickly by the individual that is the reason i'm writing my review, rita w. i won't put her last name for privacy purposes but lisa is your manager and i hope you get some big kudos! she was fantastic. so patient with me and compassionate. i shared that i was losing my insurance and she gave me financial forms in case i needed them. she was just great. i know she was really busy and took time with me answering my questions.  i would imagine being in a position right now, working in the health field, these workers are exhausted. she was so friendly and nice!!  

i then went and sat in the waiting area for my tech, sara. i wasn't waiting long, i went to the changing room and was in and out within 30 minutes. sara was great too!  very nice and i thanked her again for letting me come in today. 

needless to say, if i ever need anything done and a doctor refers me to chi, i won't hesitate!

one star because the nurses are truly amazing and deserve to be recognized as hero's.

i'm currently sitting in a covid ward and got a negative covid test last night. i'm immunosuppressed and have a kidney transplant. i have not been transferred and could
catch covid by being here easily with my weak immune system. 

these doctors and administrators need to take a good long look at who they endanger with their lackadaisical attitude towards folks with comorbidities.

i have had no fever, perfect vitals and perfect 100% pulse ox. i have some sort of bacterial infection. so of course they assume covid and place me next to two covid patients who are coughing their lungs up!!!!

you failed to run the proper labs and every time i got a meal it was ice cold. you treated me worse than i would
treat an animal!

next time l'll stay home and deal with what comes. shame on you st david's.

ps- i tried to call emily but she didn't answer. i am still sitting in your covid ward waiting. can you please expedite my removal to either another floor or to home? this is ridiculous!
fac_name: St Davids Round Rock Medical Center

review: i expected them to take this specific pandemic seriously. i had 2 out of the 3 symptoms for coronavirus, and they red flagged me/put me aside. when i entered inside i expected tests to be done, and nothing was tested except variable questions. i've been here for a long time and did not expect the round rock hospital to take this so lightly. i've always used this hospital even as a kid, and did not think they would just do verbal questions for a virus that's global.. yall can do better. it just disappoints me to say this because they've been so good to me everytime i've been there but this is serious. and just to add to this. we went there primarily to do some check ups on my 8 month pregnant fiance and now i have to go home hoping i dont have it.. sad
fac_name: St Davids Round Rock Medical Center

review:
went to banner general on april 19th with severe abdominal pain. was reluctant to go during covid but it was so bad i knew i'd need to see someone.  all entrances were closed except the er, wirh respiratory cases physically separated in the waiting room.  no other guests allowed.  checked in quickly, triaged quickly, in an er room with pain meds quickly.  taken for ultrasound, explained everything.  then taken to ct scan, back to the er room and provided more meds for comfort.  moved to a room on 5, provided meds and allowed to rest.  diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, crazy painful.  after a couple of up and down days, started finally coming out of my own yesterday.  
all of nurses, aids, cleaning staff, doctors, respiratory therapists have been professional and very caring.

terrible reason for a review but definitely well deserved.  great job all around!

thanks for the amazing care, folks!

i recently delivered at banner gateway and i cannot say enough good things about my experience with the ob department. the staff was amazing and knew exactly what to do when my delivery resulted in an emergency c section. the resident doctor, terry huff, is amazing as well and i felt in such safe hands with him when my regular obgyn was unable to perform my delivery due to covid. i also had to be readmitted for gastro and infections issues post birth and the infectious disease doctor, dr. ooman, was most helpful. he immediately pinpointed my issues and got me feeling better within hours. huge thank you to dr huff, dr ooman and the ob staff at banner gateway.

banner gateway- i emailed customer service and never heard back. it's been over a month. who else do i need to email to be responded to? thanks for the help!

i had to have an emergency surgery to remove my gall bladder during the covid-19 pandemic and they were extremely caring and concerned. the staff had great communication and let me know what was happening every step of the way. i didn't know there was a difference in hospitals and now i know there is a huge difference. i would highly recommend them.

if you're going to the er good luck. no privacy everyone in the waiting room hears what's wrong with you. also im sitting down and someone positive with covid comes in, checks in and then sits two chairs from me. again he seemed lost himself that that's where he was asked to sit. they don't separate and they did not clean where he sat. i asked two ladies if they sanitize and they said no. and i pointed where he sat and she said yeah they sit everywhere.

my elderly mother went to this hospital because she has coronavirus and every and joint in her body hurts and is on fire and she can barely breathe. my elderly mother only had two people in line in front of her, and they took six people that came in after her, instead of taking her when it was her time. my elderly mother sat in the waiting room for over 6 hours screaming and crying, and when my elderly mother told the woman she could barely breathe she said, well you are still talking so it can't be that bad. they took a younger woman in that was complaining of stomach and vagina pain but she was all right enough to sit there and laugh with her mom and play video games on her device and she came in way after my elderly mother. it is so unethical sad and disgusting how the elderly are treated there. i plan on getting a hold of the medical board and the insurance company and putting up any reviews about this horrible degrading treatment. my elderly handicapped mother on the way out to her car also tripped and got hurt and not one employee could help her i will definitely be getting a hold of my attorney about this terrible unethical company. please, this sincerely goes out to all the people that have elderly family, do not take your elderly family members to this location unless you want them to be miss treated by unethical employees, that do not care about patients.
thank you. 
banner gateway hospital higley road.

i should of listened to the reviews.. and not go. i called to see if they did covid testing today, yes she said. went there and was told only monday-friday. i told her i just called. i was ignored. i asked do you know where i can go that's close to here? i was ignored again. they weren't busy, there were a total of 3 people in the emergency room. i felt not only stupid but was outraged at how these so called nurses treated me.

if you're reading this review trying to decide whether to go to this emergency room or not... stop! 

even if you have to drive farther ...drive farther even if you have to walk farther ...walk farther!

after experiencing the most traumatic and life-threatening experience of my life (next to childbirth) i come in to this hospital (code yellow) and didn't realize that my experience here would be almost as dramatic as the event itself. 
i don't use foul language and i don't typically call people names but i really don't have anything good to say about any of the people that were in their "helping me" ... and i can only think of mean names... 

i was crying almost to the point of hyperventilation almost the entire time... not one person tried to comfort me or assure me that everything would be ok(and in a real sense everything might not of been ok, and i completely understand that) or at the very least that everyone was working hard and doing their best. i was left in the dark about everything, my monitors were going off and they told me not in a kind way that if i could just calm down that's what i needed to do as they left the room. 

covid-19 has everyone walking into the situation alone and scared. and it is the most terrifying feeling to be so alone while you are experiencing the most trumatic experiences of your life and the guys around you are being jerks. 

i have no idea what their faces look like but hearing the people in the nurses station just laughing and carrying on and having conversations with three or more people while i'm scared to death and crying my eyes out alone in the room... waving for help for sometimes more than a few minutes... 

i would literally rather suture my own wounds and set my own arm then come back to this place!! it almost felt surreal because the people that i did see seem so normal like they might have an ounce of empathy. 

i will save the person conducting the mri was the most informative and kind of all of them.

my 80 year grandmother was admitted yesterday into the emergency room with complaints of heart palpitations and elevated heart rate. no guests were allowed into the hospital due to covid-19. the health violation i am most concerned about is admitting a patient into a hospital bed that had someone else's blood soaked into the mattress. my grandmother got out of her bed and noticed blood soaked on the back of her shorts that was not of her own. she then pointed this out to the staff and after an exam confirmed that it was not her own, but that it was "from her iv line" where no blood could be seen to be the source. she had to remove the sheet with blood herself and put it on the floor. a nurse walks in and noticed that her fluid line had been dripping onto the floor with a huge puddle (also a health concern). also, how do you know the correct administered measurement of fluids if half of it ends up leaking? the sheet had someone else's blood on it, was wet and was on the on floor and the nurse proceeded to try and put it back onto to the bed. i am in shock of the hygienic practices being conducted in this hospital, especially during such a time of necessary cleanliness due to covid-19. no food or water was offered during her 8-10 hour stay. upon discharge, the nurse never offered a wheel chair and left her alone outside in the 100 degree heat without the arrival of her accompanied ride being present.

my sister went in with a hemiplegic migraine (a migraine that basically paralyzes half of your brain) and she has a history of them so we knew what it was. we brought her in to help with her pain and they didn't believe us that it was a hemiplegic migraine. she count speak couldn't move couldn't advocate for herself, and she was all by herself because of covid-19. they gave her a ct and a whole bunch of test and when those came up negative they decided she was psycho and they were about to send her to a psychiatrist facility without speaking to us first. thank god my dad called and asked what was going on, or else she would be involuntarily in a freakin nut house. worst doctors, worst experience, never again'!!!!!

horrible hospital!! my mother was taken there via ambulance as they thought she had a stroke (closest hospital) stroke was ruled out during er exam. they had sedated her in the er and then admitted her 8 hrs later. - due to her dementia my mom does do well with sedation- fast forward to 7 days later my mom has not anything to eat or drink. no plan of medical action, she is awake, confused and scared. medical staff (with the exception of a couple of nurses) do not seem to care. it's as if the dr has already signed the death certificate, just enter date. unfortunately we are stuck; with the coronavirus situation we can't just transfer her to another hospital. then the staff has the audacity to tell us we can only stay 1 hr once a day. nope my brothers and i are doing shifts. we will not allow them to kill our mother!!
just because she has dementia doesn't mean she was not living a quality life, all it meant is sometimes she didn't know what the date was. 
the medical team has not done any assessments since she has been in. they have punctured her lung due to inserting a g-tube incorrectly.

the one star is just so i can't post this. 
if anyone from dignity or banner is reading this please reach out to me. we need quality care for our mother (btw she has a excellent insurance)

oh the entire ed except for girl at front desk. is j o k e!!

i had a laparoscopic bilateral tubal ligation. after waiting more than a decade i finally found dr.ahad who took me seriously and performed the surgery. he did amazing work.  one of the kindest most empathetic doctors i've ever had the pleasure of meeting. 

the hospital itself was well prepared and maintained social distancing, took temperature and required masks. i was a bit nervous due to the pandemic but i felt i was in good hands once i went into the lobby. 

ida worked incredibly fast and was friendly during registration as the new restrictions caused time delays and she was the only one doing check-ins. 

the hospital itself was clean and all the nurses were incredibly kind. nora and nabiha both were wonderful, they chatted with me in a way that calmed me down. but really all the nurses were amazing. when i came to, i felt a bit confused, i had  what felt like strong menstrual cramps and since i'm fairly blind without my glasses i started to panic. a very nice and kind nurse who i couldn't see was able to calm me down and stopped me from trying to put pressure on my lower abdomen which is what i usually do with cramps. confusion + pain + inability to see is a bad combo. i'm grateful to her for not allowing me to hurt myself. 

i can't say enough nice things about my experience. i'm always a bit scared going into surgery but the staff at this hospital are phenomenal, i recommend getting an outpatient procedure here.

i have been aggressively pursued by telephone and by mail. i owe a balance of $125. my insurance company has paid thousands and thousands of dollars through the years. their lack of human empathy and respect is pitiful. also, we are in a world wide pandemic to top it off! unbelievable!!
fac_name: Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital - Hamilton

review:
labor & delivery review: 
awesome experience with my ob
result: healthy child 

risks that took place at l&d: 

-nurses joked about making bets on who which patient would push out a baby first while i was pushing 
-nurse missed my contractions because they were chatting about personal stuff
-i asked to see my contractions myself because they were apparently aloof from their job and they sed "we will tel ya" 
-one nurse had one glove on and mumbled "okay push okay good job" while looking into a computer screen... 
-one nurse gave me the wrong cervix measurement and turned off my pitocin, only for me to have to be back on it and labor 4 more hours... 
-broken labor bed (***future moms...they have this one old broken labor bed that they dont know how to use...i heard a nurse yell down the hall "who knows how to work the old bed?!?" 
-one nurse called me sensitive because my epidural insertion process hurt... 
-they put my child on my chest and i couldnt see the child so i asked for a pillow and nurse said "you have alot of pillows beneath you already" so i couldnt see my child face to face...
-last nurse brought my pain meds after delivery after 30minutes saying she was chatting with a doctor and rammed my wheelchair into a corner taking me to the post partum room

hey, i know its covid, i know the only thing people care about is to maintain good record keeping of paitent's vital signs, i know job security is important, and i know just doing the job can get by and treating multiple demanding patients can get draining. and i know its just some baby to others..but labor is the most vulnerable moment of a person's life.. 

hire professional nurses or check up on your "coasting" lifer nurses and update your equipment. that labor bed could have had my leg crushing down on a nurse or even my child... and educate them to not shake babies. do some type of staff assessment beyond sending online surveys that go nowhere.


anyhow, some nurses were angels, but the bad ones really make this place a no thank you place to be. 

future moms...if we can only pick our own nurses...that would be grand.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review:
during the height of the global pandemic...i cannot sing the praises of all georgetown university hospital employees loud enough! from transport, registration, pharmacy, housekeeping, cafeteria, technicians, nurses & doctors...all were thorough, professional, caring & practiced 100% safety!

there are no words to describe their dedication to their patients! health care workers rock & deserve all of the honor they are receiving!

the public health standards that i have seen employed by medstar georgetown employees during my last two in-person appointments should give potential patients very serious concerns about their alleged commitment to high standards during the covid-19 crisis.  at this point, i would recommend that potential new patients look for care elsewhere.  

during my last two visits to georgetown, i have personally witnessed over twenty of their employees either not wearing a mask or not wearing the mast properly (e.g. the mask is hanging off one ear, or lowered below their nose or even chin).  during a visit two weeks ago i even witnessed a hospital employee who was not wearing a mask, stand right in front of the screening desk near the patient pickup zone.  neither the screening team nor the security guard so much as asked him why he wasn't wearing a mask.  rather, he and the security guard told jokes and laughed.  this was less than two feet away from every patient entering the hospital!   high standards of excellence my butt!!!  i have never seen one of these individuals so much as spoken to by a supervisor!  absolutely no one seems to be in charge at the hospital right now at a time when management is unquestionably necessary!

tricia, please save your practiced, vacuous reply to this and all other reviews.  the hospital's current rating suggests that no one believes your bs.

update: i have attached a screenshot of tricia's reply.  she couldn't even get my name right!  more clear evidence that she and the hospital simply do not care about us!  medstar georgetown would do well to terminate her employment as well!

this is a review for the hospital's bmt (bone marrow transplant) unit. the staff that actually provides the care has been excellent but the coordinators have been inept, delaying my husband's transplant by a week and a half because the coordinator forgot to tell my husband she had scheduled an appointment for a specialist who is available only occasionally. 
   the first thing he knew about it was when she began frantically calling to find out why he wasn't there. he said nobody had told him he had an appointment. there was a pause and then she got off the phone, saying she would call him back. she didn't call him back. instead, he got an email saying that his surgery had been pushed back. keep in mind that this surgery has been scheduled for three months and my husband and i have scheduled leave from our jobs for it. he has been self-quarantined for two weeks so that he wouldn't get sick before the surgery (his white blood cell count is very low).
   this comes on top of a series of other problems that started with both of us having to remind the coordinator that she had not sent us a three-month schedule--as we discovered when we missed an appointment early on. later, my husband went to the hospital for the injection he needed to take before they collected his stem cells, only to discover that the medication hadn't been delivered. 
   in this area, your other options are johns hopkins, the university of maryland, and u-va. we thought georgetown would be more convenient, but knowing what i know now, i might have preferred one of the other places.

i had the worst experience here at the er. everyone was so rude, i didn't feel like a patient. i felt like cattle being herded through the system, i was being talked to like a dog, people wouldn't even look at me when they talked to me. i had to request to have a nurse in the room because i didn't want to be alone in a room by myself with a male doctor. they seemed upset that i would request that. any other place i've been to, it is a requirement to have another person in the room, but apparently not here. my feelings were so hurt after being there for 20 minutes i just wanted to cry. and of course covid-19 is going on so my husband couldn't come back with me. which is totally understandable, i know they have to do their jobs. it was just that i felt so alone and everyone was treating me so badly. i will never go back to this place ever again. at least not if i'm coherent enough to say so. if you can go to a different er, then do it. i will not spend my money at this place again. i am a human, not a bad dog.

the birthing center at sutter davis is an amazingly unique and special place to deliver a baby. i'm so thankful to have heard about this practice. despite having to drive to davis, i have no regrets about picking this spot for my prenatal care and delivery.

for the vast majority of pregnancies (non high risk), their midwife practice will definitely do the trick. i made a point to meet most of the midwives, and i really liked each of them. i was comfortable with any of them delivering our baby. they were easy to talk to you, thorough, and assuaged any concerns i had along the way. they and the broader care team were also very responsive online and on-call.

ultimately, jenn taylor delivered our baby, and amusingly she was one of the few midwives i had not met during the regular prenatal appointments. however, she was awesome, and i'm so glad she was on duty when we went into labor. the vast majority of the staff we met in the birthing center during our stay, too, were really thorough and warm. 

the birthing center itself is really great. they are conscientious about evidence-based practices. they care about the details, like dimming the lights. you can also labor or birth in a birthing tub (though, note during this current covid19 pandemic, they temporarily do not allow the birthing tub for delivery, though you can labor in the tub).

i enthusiastically recommend checking out the obstetrics and midwives practice here.

i have had 3 experiences with this poor excuse of a medical facility. i had a hysterectomy there and woke up with eye pain, they had tore the cornea from my eye when they removed the anesthesia mask. they did back surgery on my 87 year old mother and never checked on her once during her first night there. she was all drugged up and wandering the halls calling my name. her room mate told me this. last december my sweetheart went in there feeling fine and after all of the horrible things they did to him he died within 2 weeks.  they never even did anything for the reason he went there. i wouldn't go in that place even if i had a heart attack in the parking lot.

i came to this hospital actually to go to the gynecologist. one side of this place is a regular hospital and the other side is a bunch of doctors offices. the hospital was nice and clean and looked very new. there was ample parking all around. when i went inside they took my temp at the door as a safety precaution which i thought was very smart of them with this whole covid-19 going on. at the door the woman told me just where i had to go and everyone was super friendly and courteous. i would definitely come back if i had to get something done here.

during this pandemic,  i could more than understand if the stress these professionals are under could cause them to be less than pleasant. i went down to the er as my doctor suggested because i had been exposed to someone who had corvid19, had a cough and was short of breath. i was pleased to see the very effective system they used to isolate and treat me. hospitals are scarce up here but i will always choose munson gaylond if i have the option.

the nursing staff for inpatients can't get any better, but my experience in the er left a lot to be  desired.
i know they are dealing with a lot with this virus these days, but that is still not an excuse for poor patient care and dictating to the patient when they try to tell you why something doesn't work for them, especially older people. don't act like you know everything.
i was very sick and too sick to argue, and spent my time in there alone. cold, the nurse kept putting wet wash cloths on my blankets, thus leaving me freezing in wet blankets and leaving me for long periods of time without call bell handy. i can honestly say this was the most miserable night i've ever spent in my entire life, and was glad when i was admitted to the care of the competent, more compassionate nurses upstairs. now i have to pay them for that.

despite everything, i had no choice but to go to stay at a hospital.  in some ways lucky that the timing worked out well for my mandatory medical/surgical procedure.  during this time, they took/take a lot of steps to prevent spread of covid including very tight security at entrances.  majority of patients must enter through the er main entrance and noone is allowed in without prior approval from a doctor (at least in my case).  you're told to sanitize before entering and keep social distancing while in the queue.  in terms of customer service, it is hit or miss.  i've met some really friendly staff and some that could provide better bed side manner.  overall it was a fairly smooth hospital stay and i'm still in recovery.  one of the friendliest people were the food/cafeteria where i called from my room to preorder my meals so that i can get what i want.  and also thanks to my nurse assistant cinda who was so warm and friendly while i was there.  i really couldn't have asked for a friendlier and more comforting person.  i'm actually pretty impressed with the food here especially being hospital food

do not take your loved ones to this hospital!  due to my mom's serious medical condition, she was taken to bakersfield heart hospital.  they have completely ignored her advanced directive and failed to communicate with her family, even after she was rushed into the icu, where she was provided unauthorized treatment. we are trying desperately to get her transferred to a hospital that respects her, her family and her advanced directive.   the care she is receiving is torturous to her.  she has congestive heart failure, extremely painful wounds covering her legs and bottom, pneumonia and dangerously low blood pressure.  we are not allowed to see her due to covid-19.  neither the staff or the doctor treating her bothered to check the paperwork that was brought in by the family with her directives, nor did anyone at the hospital take the time to even pick up a phone to call her family while she was in critical condition.  i found out my mom was in the icu from the florist who could not deliver flowers to her room!    negligent and scary... how else are they failing her while we are stuck waiting outside the walls of the hospital?

just returned from an awful emergency room visit. i have taken my parents ,daughter and myself to other ers and have never been treated like this. i was sent by my pcp because of chest pain. because of the covid situation it appeared to be vacant.dr. huang entered the room and the first thing she asked me is why i was there. my ekg was normal. i told her my pcp wanted them to draw bloodwork on me. she never examined me. asked a few questions and left the room.i felt like i was the biggest burden and was so sorry my doctor told me to go there.it was a terrible experience.i left feeling very depressed.
fac_name: William P. Clements Jr. University Hospital

review: had my 2 year old son pre surgery covid testing requirement today and i'm thankful for the rn manager and the nurse for being understanding and patient with me and my son. especially to the manager (i forgot to get her name) for even going the extra mile and going to the testing site/tent to help (due to some minor issue/ miscommunication) before testing. thank you!

seriously?  providence st. john's suspended 10 nurses who refused to work inside a coronavirus ward unless they were provided with adequate protective gear.  a co-worker had already tested positive for the virus.  this is very telling as to how much the hospital values its employees.  shame on you providence.

update: as you can see there was a response to my comment/review. i did drive down thru the hospital area and side street, and saw that the discarded masks, gloves had been picked up. thank you for the prompt action and reply.

i am soooo disappointed about how houston medical center is handling giving information to families about the patients especially during this covid virus flare. i called to find status or any kind of information about my mother who was admitted through the emergency room. it took me 5 times to call and still was not able to talk to the nurse who was taking care of my mom. they did not even ask for my number to call back...showing how inconsiderate and not caring environment of these staff. front liners should also care for the panicking families of patients!!! perhaps they will only call to tell me if my family is deceased.....

prior to my surgery, i had to come in for pre-op labwork and registration, as well as be tested for covid-19 as part of their policy. all patients must do so regardless of whether they have symptoms or not. the nurse was very nice and gentle with me, explaining everything as she went, apologizing for any uncomfortableness i felt. she truly tried to make it as easy as possible for me. i got a phone call the next day with my results (negative of course) and was then explained currently policy for visitors and what i needed to do the night before surgery, as well as the morning of. 

surgery day, i arrived. i was called back quickly and got put into my gown and compression socks and put into a bed and nestled under a super neat inflatable warming blanket. all the staff was very friendly and kept checking on me while we waited my turn for surgery. the anesthesiologist (chris lambert) was super nice. he cracked jokes to keep me from being nervous, and said he would make sure i had zero nausea when i woke up, because i always do. he kept his word - not one bit of nausea when i woke up after surgery. good man, thank you! 
the surgery itself was done by my own chosen surgeon (dr. chris park) so i'll leave that part of the review on his page, but it's fantastic. 
after surgery, i woke up in my own room. i stayed overnight because dr. park said he prefers that after what i had done, because he knows my pain is controlled and he is able to pop in and check on me. it seemed like i good idea, and would've been, had it went according to plan. but it didn't. 
dr. park came in to check on me and tell me surgery went great. at that point, i was in no pain, which was good. he told me to go on and call the nurse to start my pain meds, and i'd get them every 4 hours. i set an alarm on my watch for every 4 hours (something i learned while fighting cancer) to make sure i wake up and take them on time to stay ahead of it. he said one the pain hits, it's 10x harder to get it back under control. i called my nurse for pain meds at 7:51pm. i called again at 8:30 because she never came. she finally showed up at 9:20 with my pills and an attitude. by then i was in tears from the pain. i refused to let my husband facetime me because he would see how bad i was doing and i knew it would stress him out. (hospital has a no visitor policy, so he had to drop me off at the door and leave, and then pick me up the next day when it was time to go home.) i took the pills and thanked her. i reset my alarms since that obviously messed up my schedule. 4 hours later, alarm goes off and i request my pain meds. nurse doesn't show up til nearly 2 hours later, again. i'm in tears, again. i ask her politely if my chart says every 4 hours or every 6 hours in case i was confused from anesthesia when i talked to dr. park, since she was bringing them every 6 hours. she said "chart says 4, but you're not my only patient, so you get them when you get them." that's how my night went. when dr. park arrived bright and early the next morning, he was surprised to see me in pain and asked what happened. i told him, and he left the room immediately. i heard words being exchanged, and he came back in and apologized profusely for the experience i had because that's not how it should've been. he said my entire reason for being there was so that wouldn't happen, and i could tell he was greatly upset by it all. needless to say, after that, things were different.  i had a different nurse until i was discharged. i was immediately given morphine to knock out the pain, then set back on my original schedule of percocet every 4 hours. once they saw it was working as it should be (as it should have been last night had it been given correctly) i was able to go home. 
my daytime nurse was a gem. super sweet, very attentive if i needed anything, but i try not to call unless it's necessary. the food was delicious. 
other than that one night time nurse, my entire experience here with everyone was wonderful. 

** i will not name the night nurse. i only know her first name and it's a common one, so i don't want to put negative light on innocent people with the same name. i found out later that she was reported for her behavior, so that's all i'll say about that.

my son was in a car accident. he is legal age, but was unconscious for more than a week. they called me for permissions but wouldn't give me any info. so fast forward another week. they gave me one hour notice that they were transferring him to a rehab. 2 days later, a nurse at the rehab told me he was there cuz he had a stroke! that the surgeon at banner caused during a surgery! now, we've been looking for some of my son's belongings and he was transferred without them! the charge nurse says they're not responsible for personal items. since all of the restrictions have started due to the covid-19 pandemic they have not allowed any visitors. so if they're not responsible for making sure that the personal items go with the patient to the new facility then who the hell is responsible for that. my son does not have use of his right arm and he cannot walk. he could not have carried his own things out of that hospital and nobody bothered to tell me whether i could go and get them or not.

the nurses who took care of my son at banner in the icu we're very good nurses and they did everything they could to help him and make him comfortable. they earned those two stars at the top of this review. the hospital itself and its policies regarding patient privacy and personal possessions sucks ass. no stars for the hospital administration. and if you're looking for a referral i would send you somewhere else

i had a situation with my first child in-utero a few years back, and went to a speciality clinic at stanford where the pa (not a doc) recommended an aggressive set of treatment upon the birth of my child for an unproven diagnosis. when i asked if it made sense to pre-emptive plan to treat something that we didn't know existed/wasn't validated, she asked me if i was a doctor - seemed like a rude & insecure response for a very reasonable question. i went to a specialist at ucsf for a second opinion, and she correctly went with a wait and see approach, which was ultimately the right response.

additionally, i have found hygiene/common-sense to be sorely lacking at the hospital. i've messaged the hospital about some of these issues with no response, so sharing here:

- re: covid - you walk in to lucille packard hospital and are asked to use their anti-bac gel (manual, not automatic), they then ask you to replace your existing mask with a new mask. what does that entail? using your hands to retrieve your mask from a stack of masks also touched by hundreds of other people. additionally, the person scanning your temperature is literally in your face...an outstretched arm would help to increase distance between you and this other party. finally, the parking lot still requires folks to touch a button to get a ticket...really, hundreds of people, touching the same button to get a parking ticket? seems like something the eng school could solve in a day.
- er: took my daughter to the er at stanford a year ago for a bad cold/fever; reception had no idea who was in the waiting room or already checked in (they kept calling the names of patients who had already gone inside for treatment over and over again), the triage nurse attempted to use filthy equipment to check my daughter's temp, and the er doctor never even checked her ears. i ended up going to urgent care at pamf a day later, where my daughter was diagnosed with an ear infection.
- l&d/in-patient hygiene: get ready for nurses to not be able to figure out how dilated you are or even tell you they can't find certain body parts - kind of not ok when you're in labor and in l&d. also be prepared to be constantly disturbed by residents, vendors, lactation consultants even after providing guidance to the team that you do not want anyone other than your doctor and nurses to come into your room. on the hygiene front, i experienced a lack of consistent hygiene - nurses in l&d did not always change their gloves before touching patients or infants, once, a nurse was about to stick a dirty glove in my infant daughter's mouth after touching the ac unit! don't even get me started on the lack of hygiene on the adult side of the hospital - that's for another review.
- prescriptions: my daughter was prescribed an incorrect dose (higher than what was appropriate for her weight) of antibiotics for an ear infection by an ent specialist; i happened to catch the error after her first dose, but seriously, that is an unacceptable mistake.
- facilities: the new campus is gorgeous, but i was stuck in a parking elevator at the older lcph building a few years back. the elevator phone was non-existent and the alarm button was out of order. i was 8 months pregnant and had no phone reception at the b level in order to call my husband, luckily my parents were with me and we literally banged on a small pane of glass until a passerby happened to see us. they called maintenance and we were able to get out of the elevator after nearly 45 minutes of being stuck. their patient success folks sent me a basket, which included pork sausages amongst other items that are clearly not compatible with my religious / dietary preferences on my file; not a big deal, but if you're trying to make nice with a pregnant woman who was trapped in an elevator, seems like they could have thought through their conciliatory effort a bit.

when covid-19 hit and the stay at home order was put in place, my wife's job allowed her time off to care for her mother who is a senior citizen with cancer and deemed extremely high risk. the hr specialist at my wife's company assisted her in applying for paid family leave (pfl) as my mother in law's only caregiver. the records office, who works with edd to process pfl claims, was very helpful. they told us that my mother in law's doctor must fill out a wasf in order to proceed. we requested the wasf from her primary physician but was told that her oncologist had to do it. we then requested it from the oncologist. after a couple of weeks had gone by, we followed up and were told that we had to resubmit the paperwork. we did that and, after about a month of trying, were told that northern california kaiser has a "policy" to not provide a wasf for cancer patients with caregivers during the covid-19 pandemic. i could not believe this so i called kaiser member services and the records office to inquire about this "policy" but no one had heard of it. they suggested that we ask the oncologist about it. she confirmed this strange, cold-hearted "policy" but said that her hands were tied. she offered to provide a letter in my mother in law's records but that doesn't help my wife's pfl claim. so, here we are almost two months later and she's been caring for her mother and receiving no assistance thanks to kaiser's "policy". has anyone else, or their loved ones, had to endure the extra stressed during these times because of kaiser's wicked "policy"? shame on them!

this review pertains to the care my 36 year old son received at mercy regional medical center almost two years ago.  two years is the length of time that i have spent trying to get justice for brian.  the lies, the condescending sympathy and partially released medical records has added greatly to the pain of losing my son.  brian arrived at mercy's ed on 5/16/2018 at 3:00 am.  on 5/17 ct/egds revealed brian had a giant pseudoaneurysm measuring 10.2 cm.  it also showed gastric and esophageal varices caused by thrombosis and erosive esophagitis most likely caused by multiple episodes of vomiting blood.  the gi and vascular surgeons said they did not have the skill sets to treat brian and recommended that he be transferred to another hospital.  the vascular surgeon had to have known that brian needed urgent surgery because of the high probability of the giant pseudoaneurysm rupturing.  brian was never told he had a giant pseudoaneurysm. he was told he had a blood clot.  a mercy hospitalist talked to a hospitalist and hepatologist at porter adventist hospital (denver) about brian's condition and request for a transfer.  the size of the pseudoaneurysm was never mentioned during 4 phone conversations. (after hiring an attorney, i finally received the phone conversation recordings that both hospitals' cmo told me i would never receive.) the hospitalist at porter told the hospitalist at mercy that porter doctors did not have higher skill sets than mercy doctors, but still accepted the transfer.  brian left mercy on a flight for life plane in fair condition, but he actually had dangerously high blood pressure, a map reading with alert next to it and 9 out of 10 pain.  he was given an opioid for the pain right before the plane took off.  there was no plan for surgery when brian arrived at porter, instead he was assigned to an inpatient room.  he died in his bed 11 hours later when the pseudoaneurysm burst.   my son's autopsy shows that he died from the rupture of a known aneurysm.  brian actually died from lack of treatment by an inept medical system.  per john hopkins hospital study - medical errors account for 1/3 of hospital deaths.  as of today, there is a reported 60,726 covid-19 deaths in the us.  as of today, the number of deaths caused by medical errors is probably much higher, but these deaths are recorded as the condition the patient had, not the medical errors that caused the death. medical errors are a silent, rampant epidemic

i was just traumatized at the memorial er hospital in southbend today.  i had been exposed to the coronavirus but was told my results would not be back for 7-10 days.  meanwhile, i got worse but then i got better, but then two days ago, i had taken a turn for the worse--fever, chills, cough, etc., all those symptoms came back with a vengeance. so, upon hearing that it could take up to 10 days for my results to come back, i looked at my sons and told them i couldn't wait any more. i had to go to the er. we called the cdc to see what we needed to do. they told me to call the er, so they could prepare for me. 

i called the memorial hospital er, and they told me to just go in and register. however, after self-quarantining for 8 days, i was not about to go into a public population and possibly expose anyone if i had the coronavirus. my brother called the hospital  and they gave him different instructions for me to follow, which was call them when i got to the er, and someone would come out to me. 

none of this protocol was followed once i arrived. i was told to just go in. yep. i refused to go in, so my brother called the hospital again, and the lady informed him that if someone is telling me to go in, then i should just go in. (all recorded by the way.)

now, i'm going to move directly to the er room with the doctor, and this is where i was completely traumatized, accused and made to feel like a criminal. (i'm a 56 year old professional--educator). 

the doctor came into the room and goes to listen to my lungs. he twists my shoulders away from him. (i get it, and i'm okay with it.  he didn't  want me to breathe on him), but then he used his elbow to turn my head so it faced the door. then after he had listened to my lungs, he started asking why i came to his hospital to expose people if i had the coronavirus . (i forgot to mention that an iv had been put in my arm but not taped down because the nurse had forgotten the tape, and at this point,  i totally understood that they wanted to spend very little time in my room in case i'm positive--and i'm okay with it up until this point.)

i had mentioned the iv to the doctor when he first came into my room, and i even told him that the iv looked like it had twisted in my vein.  while this doctor was on a tirade, blaming me for being at the hospital and accusing me of spreading sickness to everyone, he reached across the left side of my bed and jerked, not pulled, the iv out of my right arm. he then left while i was bleeding in that room. 

i called my brother, crying and panicked, and my brother told me to take pictures of everything. because of my hysteria, i had only taken two pictures when a nurse came into the room, telling me to calm down. i showed her my bleeding arm and told her that i couldn't calm down informing and showing her what the doctor had done to me. (by the way, my brother was still on the speaker phone.) the nurse then threatened to call security to take my phone if i took another picture. my brother then spoke up and said no one better not touch my phone or they would be sued. 

while i was still upset and crying, my brother called the administration of the hospital and informed him how i was being treated. 30 minutes later, the doctor came back into my room to apologize because he said it had been years since he had done an iv, and he didn't know that when he pulled my iv out like he had done that i would bleed like i did.  he then proceeded to say everyone's nerves were on edge because of the coronavirus. i continued to let him try to explain why i he had treated me so horrible. 

when he finished, i then reminded him that i had complied with everything that i had been told to do while awaiting my test results and that i had come to the hospital because i was getting worse instead of getting better--only to have a doctor accuse, blame and make me feel like criminal--when all i was seeking was medical help.

i still don't know if i'm positive or negative. i'm still waiting for my results to come back, and i've been on self-quarantine for 8 days. my nerves are also on edge, and a medical doctor traumatized me when i needed reassurance.  i'm the one who has done everything i've been told to do--not going out partying, gathering in groups, etc..  

i have self-quarantined for 8 days now, and i needed reassured that i was going to be okay today. attached are the two pictures of how the doctor left my room after jerking the iv out of my arm. today, i needed a doctor who was at his best to take care of me, not a doctor who was stressed whose nerves were on edge. i had gone to this hospital for medical treatment, but instead, i left completely traumatized.

i got to spend two nights here recently. luckily i wasn't the patient -- but i kept my man company after his surgery. i actually slept on two chairs bedside while he was there. 

i've been here before myself, but they seem to have upped their game. in addition to taking all the extra precautions for covid, every person we came in contact with was very professional and enjoyable to deal with -- from the cleaners on up to the doctors and nurses. there really was a great team effort. and it shows. 

each shift change, they came in and introduced the new people. they went over the necessary info and posted it each time on a board by the bed. each patient has a phone with the number to call to reach the attending nurse, the assistant and floor personnel. it's a very efficient system. and they are very informative to prepare the patient for what's going to happen and how to manage your pain. 

the food here was surprisingly way better than average for hospital food. every morning starting at 6:30 am you can call in your breakfast order from their menu. it takes about an hour or less to get your hot breakfast. you use your phone to call the kitchen extension. (hint: they're busy. don't hang up. just hold til they answer.) choices included various omelets, eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes, breads/cakes, fresh and canned fruits, juices, cereals, etc. the only thing they didn't have was toast! you also call in for your other meals at least an hour or so in advance. lunches, too, were good as well as dinners. there's a lot of variety and they try to accommodate all requests if possible. two standouts were their fresh sliced hot turkey with mashed potatoes and gravy and their mac n cheese.

the hospital offers free valet parking which is helpful as the lot fills up. 

the only downside was the day we came their computers were acting up so it  took longer to register and to be processed during pre-op. and a longer time than expected waiting for a room to be available. 

no one really wants to be in a hospital, but if you do need to be, this is one of the better options in town.

review:
took my infant to the er here after calling my pediatrician and describing her symptoms. she's had a fever for four days, lethargic, inconsolable crying, weak, distressed and in pain. she was having a hard time breathing normally and that's what i was most worried about. 

the receptionist was very friendly, took our information and we waited. the waiting room was nearly empty. due to covid 19 they only allowed one parent in w my daughter so my husband waited outside, even though there was a mom and a dad with their baby in the waiting room. 

they took us back to triage and left us waiting. finally a nurse practitioner came in, not friendly at all, almost annoyed that we were there, looked in my baby's ears and down her throat and said as she's walking out that they'll do a swab test her for flu, rsv and strep. she left and i hear her talking happily w another nurse right outside our door. would it kill her to be kind or friendly to us? oh well, i figured, not a big deal, i just want to take care of my baby. 

they take us to a room. 

shortly after that a nurse walks in and listens to my baby's heart. she said she needs to go see what tests need to be done and she leaves the room. 

we weren't waiting long when someone shows up to do a chest x ray. a chest x ray? the nurse practitioner had said nothing about that. i didn't even know they were going to get x rays. i wondered if they had heard something when they checked her a few minutes ago. of course my baby is freaking out the whole time. the guy is kind and we get it done. 

one hour goes by. two hours go by. my poor baby is restless and fussy. no one checked on us or told us what was going on. i walked out into the hall and asked the first person i saw what was taking so long. she said they were waiting for results from the swab test. i told her they hadn't done the swab test yet. she said oh they're probably waiting for the x ray results. 

another hour goes by and i called the nurse to the room and come to find out she thought another nurse had already swabbed my baby. after being there for three hours and hardly anyone else there we hadn't even taken the sample yet. 

another hour goes by and i walk out to the desk where the nurse is sitting there eating cookies. i told them we're leaving. my baby and i are both exhausted at this point and the whole thing has been a joke. another nurse snaps at me and tells me they have a skeleton staff and they don't even have a technician on staff.

i finally get the results of the swab test back and the nurse practitioner comes in and apologizes for everything taking so long and said there was a mix up with one nurse getting distracted and thinking someone else had already done the test. 

still heard nothing about the x rays, why they took them or what they showed. 

frustrating experience.

my 88-year-old mother presented to the er 5/8/20 for leg pain and weakness. at the time she was at full mental capacity, ambulatory with walker assistance.

on 5/10/20 we found it very difficult to reach her, her phone was not answered in her room and it was difficult to get in touch with nurse's station. we expressed our concerns about this. by 5/11/20 she was totally incoherent and unable to answer her phone. at times an aid would answer and we heard her screaming in the background. when they held the phone to her she was unable to speak and she had no idea where she was. she believed she was home. the dr. (raza) told me on 5/11/20 that she was on hydrocodone for pain and when i expressed my concerns about her wellbeing he informed me that her bloodwork was good and she could be discharged 5/12/20. on 5/12/20 we were informed by nurses that she had not had any pain medication since she had been there other than 1 tramadol and she was diagnosed 5/12/20 with a uti and was beginning treatment. on 5/13/20 we were told it would be yet another day due to possible small area of pneumonia. we insisted on her discharge 5/14/20. upon picking her up she was brought out in light summer pajamas, a blanket no mask and turned over to us and we thought they had made a mistake and brought the wrong patient out. we did not even recognize what was sitting in that wheelchair. the nurse stated that what we were seeing were probably residual effects from the ativan that was given to her to "calm her down" why did she need to be calmed down and why was she given ativan? we were rushed along and given no real discharge instructions. upon getting her home she laid in fetal position for the first 3 days crying for her mother. she was covered in bruises showing all signs of severe abuse, trauma and suspected sexual abuse. at first the home nurses though that she may have been catheterized for the urine sample and that was painful and traumatizing for her but we later found out that they never even did a urinalysis and she never had a uti that they claimed she had and was treating her for. after a few days she began to come around a small amount and she could only cry and ask why they had done those things to her in the hospital and why they hurt her. we also found out that she had a 14mm kidney stone that was never addressed or told to us. my mother went from being of total sound mind and ambulatory (only experiencing some pain and weakness) on 5/8/20 to now being on end stage hospice care.
we have had several incidents with this hospital that have always fallen on deaf ears.  in researching the many websites, we have come across several similar heart wrenching stories from patients and families in this hospital and i am currently corresponding with a woman who saw my post about her father in law who is currently in that hospital suffering abuse and neglect. i have every intention of contacting medicare, state board of medicine, health dept. and any other agency that will shed light on what happened to my mother in that establishment.
i have worked in the medical profession myself for the past 20 years and have never witnessed anything like this hospital. i am contacting the large benefactors for the hospital, the press and anyone that will listen and help me to stop another human being from suffering this type of tragedy and abuse in this facility. i also will fight as hard as i can to get the license of dr. raza taken from him. i want whomever abuse, assaulted, and basically killed my mother held accountable.
**update since this was first written.
on june 9, 2020 exactly 27 days after she has suffered the abuse, assault, medical misdiagnosis and gross negligence my mother has passed away.
also, the man i mentioned that his family had contacted me due to similar complaints of neglect and abuse was scheduled to be released from that establishment 6/8/20 but had passed on 6/5/20.
i will fight until i take my last breath for my mother, this man and all who walk through the doors of olean general hospital that are unable to speak for themselves.  there has to be change, people have to be held accountable.

nothing strikes more fear in all of us during this era of covid-19 (well, except for the virus itself), than the thought of a trip to the er.

under normal conditions, an er visit is very stressful, but in the era of covid-19, it's incapacitating.

yet, here i found myself on a monday morning after experiencing lightning streaks coming out of my left eye all weekend. it was mystifying and scary. 

a quick trip to dr. google led me to a possible diagnosis, a detached retina, and these words, " seek medical help immediately." 

i live smack dab in the middle between two ers. i found out the hard way, that while one will offer a slick, state of the art environment, you will encounter indifferent, uncaring staff and wait times up to 8 hours.

the other er features a setting reminiscent of the tv series, m*a*s*h, all due to ongoing construction of brand new facilities.

i chose the latter. why? 

because a previous visit 18 months earlier showed a well-oiled machine, despite er patients lying on gurneys in hallways. the staff were attentive, nurturing, and very efficient.

this er, providence cedars-sinai tarzana medical center, proves that it's not the setting that matters. it's the staff!

and this is where tarzana er excels. from the friendly check-in to triage to the er doc, everyone was top-notch.

especially the doc. 

i'm a veteran of many er visits, so i know an exceptional er doc when i see one, as in the case of dr. gregory scott brewster. 

i have not met a more compassionate, attentive, sympathetic and driven er doc. ever.

he goes far beyond what is required. i listened for two hours as he not only took care of at least a dozen patients, but chased down specialists and patients' personal mds on the phone. 

in my case, it took him 2 hours to find an ophthalmologist willing to see me. yet he never gave up.

even when he finally found one only to have the cell phone call dropped, he persevered. and found me the best retina specialist i could possibly get. 

and if that's not enough, dr. brewster followed up later with a call to see how my visit went!!! 

i am stunned and incredibly grateful that such a professional exists.
