i just got off the phone with brandy in the billing department. my husband has a bill for what they thought was a possible stroke back in aug. the bill is over $4,500. we called to set up a payment plan. she said it had to be paid in 12 months and the payments would be almost $380 a month. i told her in these times of uncertainty, we just can't do that. i begged, cried, pleaded to please lower the monthly payment so we wouldn't be turned over to the collection agency! she was rude, cold, and heartless! she even insinuated that we didn't pay on the account when we should have been doing so and if we did, we wouldn't be in this situation! (we did pay and were also told by the insurance company that they had not paid their part yet so just wait for the final bill to come which just did.) i informed her that we have never not paid our bills and would pay this one, too. we just need more time. we don't know from one day to the next if my husband will lose his job due to the coronavirus. she could not care less. she showed no compassion, empathy or kindness at all. she was dismissive, talked down to me and was very haughty! i let her know that next week it could be her on the phone crying and begging for help. she wished me a good day! i will lay in my house and die before i ever darken the door of cape fear valley hospital!

my son was a patient here and unfortunately it was during the covid -19 pandemic so he was not allowed visitors. in addition to that he is a quadriplegic so he couldn't just pick up the phone to call family . my son has a 1 year old daughter and she is the only thing that keeps his spirits up. gabby who is in public relations at kindred would go out of her way every day to check on him and call us on facetime so he could see and talk to his daughter. this small act of compassion had a huge impact on his mental well being. it's so nice to see people like gabby that genuinely care for people. it's my understanding she not only did this for my son but several patients there. kindred you are lucky to have her and we will forever be grateful. thank you !

i can't thank the staff of this hospital enough.  before we moved to the pass cedars sinai was our go to hospital. 
cedars is a fantastic hospital but the size and complexity are too much. 
sgh is small and easy to use.  
nurses and doctors take the time to reach out with phone calls and texts. 
in this time of covid 19 they quickly diagnose and care for the problem. 
moving here was probably the smartest thing i could have done for my age. 
everything for medical care is 5 minutes away.  thank you sgh.

my husband had been experiencing some numbness in his shoulders and on the side of his face. i took him here for care and they put him in triage without me.  that's fine for most people, but because i have a better recollection of his past medical conditions than he does at times, i really needed to be in the room with him.  one hour after he was taken in, i hadn't heard anything about what they were doing with him, no updates whatsoever. i complained and asked for an update three times and finally a nurse with an attitude came out and told me he was fine, i questioned her as to if he went over all of his history and meds and she said yes.  she didn't want to spend any time with me, and was extremely anxious, so i was really unable to tell her that there were things in his past that they should know about.  my husband flagged me down when the er doors opened and i gave him his phone so that we could communicate.  he called me and said he had no idea what was going on as they weren't communicating with him either.  the place was pretty empty because no one wants to be in an er room with covid being a scare and you can't be in the room with your loved ones.  he told me to go home, which i did, and a few hours later they released him.  they must have done it in a hurry because when he got home he still had all the ekg stickers all over his body, he had to remind them to take the wires off because he almost walked out with those still attached.  there was probably 12 patches on him, they couldn't take them off before he left?  really?  he's also allergic to the adhesive so his skin was inflamed, something they could have cleaned up before he was discharged.

my advice to this hospital is that they speak to the family member that brought the patient in so that they can get a complete medical history, including medications (which i had to convince the nurse with attitude to take a copy of). they have no idea what i remember compared to my husband because i've lived through his issues and have clarity as to what happened in the past. to think that i may risk life to travel to loma linda to get proper care upsets me.  it's pathetic.

once admitted the hospital is pretty good but the emergency room is awful. some of the staff is kind but i experienced some very rude nursing staff. i was in a life threatening situation so there was no wait for me but i'm sure it would be much longer for someone not in that situation. i am 18 years old and came in serious condition with covid 19 and i could hear nurses outside my room talking about my diagnoses who had no business knowing. they were somewhat making fun of me. i of course was by myself considering safety precautions. it was my first time in a hospital by myself so i was very scared and distraught. i cried because they told me i would be in the hospital for a week alone without visitation. the er doctor spoke to me and told me i was not allowed to cry and shamed me about crying. i was alone and would be for a week and the woman thought it was appropriate to tell me i'm not allowed to cry?! ridiculous and wrong. also there was a toilet in the room because i was not allowed to leave but no one ever knocked before coming in so everytime i used it i was walked in on. anyway the staff i experienced in the er were rude and made me, young and terrified, feel very unwelcome and even more afraid.

my husband went there after having shortens of breath, headache and cough. he has been exposed to multiple lab confirmed cases of covid in his line of work, and i sent him to resolute because their website claimed they do in house rapid covid 19 screenings. while he was there he was informed that the hospital doesn't do any covid testing there. he was given a list of places that do the screenings. this is false advertising, and as someone in the medical field i find it highly irregular that a hospital does not perform covid testing.

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

i see why this place is rated 2.5 stars!!!! i called in advance to get tested for covid (i am moving to a home with kids and elderly, i also have a friend who showed no signs of covid but gave it to his gf who is now very sick!) the woman on the phone was the best part of this experience, she was kind and answered all our questions. when i got there around 1:40pm it was clear why i came in, covid test!! two hours later i'm still waiting and when i finally asked for help they told me they were short on tests and i wasn't "sick enough" to get one. really?!? they couldn't tell me that when they asked me my symptoms two nearly three hours ago??? this place is total crap. i've had better service at a shopping mall. the nurses here also talk badly about their patients. this is disgusting behavior for "caregivers". while i was waiting i heard a tall overweight white male nurse talking about an elderly patient saying "she sounds like she's giving birth but she's not. she just has the shits".  im sure he wouldn't appreciate someone treating his mother that way. another female nurse who looked hispanic with highlights was very nonchalant about a patient who kept getting up with and iv on her. the poor woman kept getting up and this nurses attitude was "whatever she'll be fine".  it seems that these "caregivers" have no passion and can't perform basic and essential parts of their job. hospitality and communication. it's a scary time, this is a given but i'm sure none of the hospital workers went to school thinking this would be an easy or glamorous job. you are there to help people not flirt and talk bad about patients.
my friend works there and apparently they are doing elective surgeries during a time when medical staff and life saving equipment should be assigned  to treat corona virus patients.

to quote governor newsom:  "time to recognize that it's not just about the old folks, it's about your impact on their lives. don't be selfish."  hospitals across the state have cancelled non-emergency "elective surgeries" such as cosmetic procedures to preserve masks, gloves, and gowns to protect the front line medical staff caring for covid-19 patients.  this is not the time for surgeons and hospitals to practice "business as usual" when tens of thousands have lost their jobs.

don't go here.  they charge more that other hospitals and are aggressive with collections.

review: i spent 4 days here for ketoacidosis.   i realize this is a hard time because of covid but i unfortunately had an unacceptable level of care.   first the icu was great.   nurses angelia and jake went above and beyond to help me.   the next day when i was transferred to general problems began to happen.   it seems the nurses were overworked and rushing all the time.  i had medical waste repeatedly left on my bed including an insulin needle.     my meals were completely inappropriate for a diabetic.   sugary muffins, sugar for coffee with no sugar free option.    most meals had potatoes or other high carb food.   when i got home they had left 4 of the electrodes under my breasts.   the nurse just yanked the wire off and left them there.   if this had happened to an elderly person it could have caused a serious infection gone unnoticed.    i'm sorry to write such a bad review because the nurses were doing their best but i was feeling more unsafe the longer i stayed there.   please give your nurses more support.

review: i have been debating if i should go see my doctor lately because i figured they are all busy with the covid and all.  i finally got the nerve and spoke to my doctor who told me i need to get blood drawn as my condition was serious.  9am i go to the peterson park office for blood draw and greeted sandy.  i told her i was in for a blood draw.  she got up looked around and became very upset stating she has no orders for me.  i waited as she looked around the office and could hear her going on complaining that people come in without orders and why does she not know about this and how she should just have me leave and come back with orders!  i and everyone in the waiting room could hear her rantings.  i felt like a total idiot.  her ranting went on and on until she comes back to the window and said i should come back with orders after 10 am because that is when they do lab work anyway!  i was about to leave when another patient in the waiting room asked what her problem is, and advised i call the doctor to call in what labs i need done.  i decided i was already there and called the doc.  he asked me to stay and he would call the office with lab work again.  finally, a nurse called me in and drew my blood.  as i left i said bye but sandy was not having it, she didn't even acknowledge me.  i seriously question if i would want to put up with that bad attitude ever again and will ask that i schedule my visits on her off days!

review:
my wife has been a patient admitted from er during covid restrictions. (no visitors.)  so, the mds and the staff has free reign to do as they please without family oversight.
so far the nursing staff has been "too busy" to even speak with me about her diagnosis or status. 
no one from er told me that she was being admitted or why. there are so many doctors previously unknown to us. most are too busy to communicate at all.
on the positive side the mds from the cardiac group and from neurology have been very professional and communicative.
otherwise, visiting the er at this hospital under these conditions is insanity.

i had such a bad experience with this er and how they treated me and my sister.  my son was admitted and we are both nurses.  we were not allowed to be with him due to covid and we understand this. however, the lack of communication,empathy and overall attitude was despiscable as we were seen " as bothersome" just because we asked to speak to a doctor.  in fact, the nurse told my son to tell us to stop asking questions and stop bothering them.  we only requested to speak to the doctor on our phone to get a diagnosis.  im appalled and would never come here again.   to tell a patient that his mom and aunt are bothering them and leave them alone goes against the nursing code of ethics. the one star rating is only there as yelp requires a rating, i would rate this hospital a pure zero.

i was a patient at abington hospital during covid-19 peak 3/28/20-4/10/20. i have mixed emotions about my treatment and stay. i will say that i received excellent service from some of the nurses and staff during some shifts. on other shifts the staff could have been more attentive and shown more compassion. i had surgery, and one part of my recovery was to go on walks, some staff thought it would be okay for my to get off my ng tube and iv and just walk alone, and not even offer me a mask. not to mention each day, i had to ask about bathing, bringing me items, and little assistance was offered. there were times when i was due for medication and i went an hour or two past my scheduled time for my next dose, and had to call for the nurse to remind them. i know this was a busy time because of the pandemic, but i feel like if i wasn't coherent my treatment wouldn't have progressed as it did. i was on top of my treatment, for instance- a day post surgery my ng tube wasn't flowing, it took the night staff to come and figure it out and my progress depended on the production of bile coming or not coming out of the tube. the order was for my tube to be checked every four hours moving forward, this was not done on every shift, i had to prompt and remind staff to check my tube. even my day of discharge - i was left to get dressed without any offer of assistance. i had major surgery in my stomach in two different areas. i just thought there could've been a little bit more concern and care. 
to top it off, my prescription glasses -tom ford glasses "went missing". i was dropped off at emergency on 3/28/20 and my husband sent them back up on 3/29/20 in a bag with other items...i never received my glasses. i was told, that they're just missing. it has been a month post and they still haven't turned up. i haven't been contacted my the abington police as i was told by security to file a formal police report. 
overall - like i said there were great nurses who took great concern for me and care, as i was there for 13 days... and my surgery went well, the doctors did a great job. but there are always a few in the bunch that can ruin the experience.. and just simply need to do better. as at some points my health, progress and discharge date depended on their quality of work. 
currently i am without glasses, to see as i have to work from home from my pc... i hope my glasses truly blessed the person that felt they needed to take advantage of someone who was sick in the hospital for 13 days without a loved one there for comfort and to advocate for them because of corona.

i recently underwent a coronary artery bypass under the care of dr. hartmuth bittner and the uc cardiac surgery team.
dr. bittner worked with his excellent team , and with me, to plan the best approach to my surgery. he made me feel part of the process, and explained every step to me very clearly. my surgery was a great success, and i am already feeling much better than before the surgery (i am 8 weeks out). 
dr. bittner is extremely caring and empathetic, and he and his excellent team, including the cardiac icu nurses, made the whole scary experience a lot less stressful.  i whole-heartedly recommend uc med center and dr. bittner and his colleagues for any cardiac procedure you may need.

came in not feeling well treated me like shit.  had me in a cold wet tent left me alone half the time. outside wet freezing cold.  if this is the way they treat their patients i don't care if there's a virus going around better care.  the tent should've been dry and heated and there should've been staff in it taking care of the patients. or inside in an isolation room if you cannot comprehend that.

what people need to know before choosing this hospital is that it's a sinking ship. slu hospital, which supplies nursing and physicians to st mary's, is broke. they were broke before the pandemic, so imagine how bare the cupboards are now! the high caliber staff they have left leaves as soon as they possibly can, and take jobs at other hospitals. they have to hire locum doctors (travel doctors) because so few physicians in stl want to work here. and while i appreciate the care and efforts of the well- meaning hospital staff upstairs on the main floor, the emergency department is an absolutely disaster. the staffing quality is abysmal, and they will not lift a finger to help you if it inconveniences them. spoiler alert: everything inconveniences them. i know there are some good hearted people working here, but if you've ever experienced the caliber of care you get from nursing home employees, that's what you get from st mary's nowadays too.

this place sucks, to be quite frank. my infant daughter has had a lower grade fever along with breathing issues during this coronavirus pandemic and it's been 5 hours since we've arrived , seen 2 nurses and they were in and out of the room within 5 minutes, took one swab and said "sit tight" been sitting tight for 4 hours now , no information. this place is very clearly not busy down in the er. slow, no urgency, it's fine to take your time and wait for information and check in every once in a while, but i couldve done exactly what i'm doing now at home and not been stuck here into the early morning.

where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!

review: this review is for the nicu staff only.  my first born was delivered by emergency c-section prematurely at 25 weeks, at 390 grams (almost 14ounces). this was a very rare case for any pregnancy, but thanks to the neonatal doctors and the nurses at gmc nicu,  their expertise and care saved my baby. they cared for me, my husband, and my baby like we were family. we were there for 3 months and during that time we got to know how caring and knowledgeable each and every one of the staff were, including the respiratory therapists. fast forward to today, i just recently had my second baby, prematurely again. at 31 weeks, 2lbs 14oz, we're back at gmc nicu. being back was a little uneasy at first, because honestly - any parent would rather have their happy healthy baby at home. especially during this pandemic. after seeing all the familiar faces, it immediately put me to ease. i knew my baby was in good hands. i trust these nurses, and i know they're doing everything in their power to help me bring a happy and healthy baby home. we're so grateful for these nurses, and i don't know how i can ever repay them for saving both my children.

on friday, 4/17/2020, my grandma was taken to your medical facility, garfield medical center at around 4:00 pm. my grandma whom has tested positive for covid-19 began presenting worsening symptoms and due to her advanced age, we decided it would be best to take her to the hospital. we chose your facility because of your good reputation, nonetheless, we feel we were let down on this said day. my sister took our grandma in her car, taking a high risk of getting infected herself, for i could not transport her myself because i am also positive for covid-19 as well. we truly believe (my sister, my grandma, my mother, and i) that my grandma was de-serviced on this day. i understand the unique and precarious circumstances we are under does not allow for things to be normal, nonetheless, this does not mean for my grandma to sit in a car for two (2) hours, basically, unattended as my sister has no medical back-ground. the only thing that was done for my grandma was; insurance information, temperature, and basic vitals were taken on her upon arrival while in the car. as a matter of fact, my grandma never left the car for two hours, while waiting in the er parking lot under the assigned area. my sister kept on asking, politely, how much longer before grandma would be taken in, and she was given the runaround a few times. the staff did not take action to take my grandma in, until my sister finally lost some of her patience and composure, and raised her voice to let staff know she was leaving and she was taking grandma elsewhere. it was not until this moment that the staff finally came with a wheelchair and tried to do something trying to justify their delay. my sister stated to them that why did she have to raise her voice to get things done, that was not right, what if she had not raised her voice, how long would she have waited? that is a question my sister was not willing to gamble on with grandma. 
basically, nothing was done for my grandma, and yet, insurance information was taken which leads me to believe we will get billed for having had my grandma sit in her car outside the er for two hours. is this justifiable? consider the fact that none of us are currently working, therefore, income is a very serious issue. what will we get billed for, let me see, for nothing? how will you justify billing us for having had grandma, whom was identified as a senior citizen and positive for covid-19, to just sit in the car, hungry, and with uncertainty? my sister rushed my grandmother to alhambra hospital medical center and they quickly received her and attended to her care.

i can't speak to the services at rwj rahway hospital, itself, nor the quality of patient care you can hope to receive.  however, i can speak to the amazing community programs the hospital runs.  if the support groups run by the hospital are indicative of its patient care, i have to say the organization is truly invested in health.  

rwj rahway, at one of its namesake gyms, rwj fitness & wellness, offers community-based support groups.   i personally attend the fibromyalgia support group & i can only describe it as a "life-saver."  before the covid-19 pandemic, we were already a close-knit group who discussed the countless lifestyle/medication/nutrition/exercise changes we'd made to improve our situation.  but, when we all went into lockdown, we had unique issues.  

led by an rn who could not care more about us if she tried, our meetings are a mix of scientific information (some unfolding & yet untested) & anecdotal experience.  

i've seen an amazing increase in my health from (regularly) attending these community meetings.  but, & more importantly during this crisis, i've had the support from people who understand our special risks & needs.  people i'm proud to now call "friends."

during this time, rwj & mindy, our group coordinator, have made zoom support group meetings.  it has been a lifesaver, when we can't be physically close, to keep this sense of emotional community makes it seem less abnormal.

review: i couldn't not have been happier with doctor oleg and his staff.  my 76 year old mother had been in a nursing home for several years because of a severe case of parkinsons disease which left her bedridden and unable to move.  this led to bed sores, blood clots, and eventually a stroke around new years day leaving her unable to speak.  she was taken to encino hospital for the first time and we could not of been happier.  the place is very clean, the rooms are very quiet and it was very easy to visit. that is when i first got to spend about 30 minutes face to face with dr. oleg. i was extremely impressed with him and his caring attitude toward my mother as her condition deteriorated.  over next five months, she returned to the hospital three different times for various problems.  each time, the staff could not have been more accomodating.  even as visits became restricted,  i could talk to them on the phone without feeling rushed and still get the information i wanted.  sadly my mother contracted covid19 in the nursing home where she was at in early may.  dr. oleg called me personally several times that last week to share information as the end neared and even allowed me an end of life visit the day she passed away.  i am eternally greatful to dr. oleg and the staff at encino hospital for making a difficult situation just a little more bareably.  if you are in need to be in a hospital, i would strongly recomend this facility.

today, i checked my credit score, only to find out that they sent me to collections.  wtf?? they have ruined my credit score.  i lost my job in october, and had finally found one, only to have the offer taken away because of covid-19.  i am destitute, and i now cannot get a job in my profession because i have taken a huge hit on my credit report, and i need good credit because my industry requires it.  mission viejo medical associates has had my telephone number the entire time and never once attempted to call me about owing anything!!!   now they have ruined my credit, and my prospects for attaining employment.   there is no reason they could not have called my back then when i still had a job.  now my financial situation is worse than it was then.  and now those thoughts are quickly back in my mind.  mission hospital is there to save lives, yet they will probably cost me mine.

i have been going through a rough patch the past few months with really bad back pain. i had it under control most of the time but unfortunately it's with pain killers. it's a temporary thing but very much needed. i also have daily abdominal pain and discomfort from my past cancer surgeries that they already had be on the pain killers for. this back pain over shadows it. so they just have me take more for this. i recently moved and my new doctor wanted to try me on the pain meds he likes. unfortunately they didn't seem to take away any of the pain and it by the time i figured this out and told them i was already in very bad pain. then they took some time to respond due to the doctor being out. a little too long. this pain completely changes my life. i can't hardly get out of bed or do anything. i have my laptop in bed with me trying to work and it's rough. so i didn't know what else to do. especially with the covid situation. i wasn't sure. so i called the closest hospital to me, st. john's. they said come right down, they'd be happy to see me. it was a rough ride but at least they are very close to me. i got there and no one was in the waiting room. i thought this is great, get right in! so i got signed in, told them the whole story and went back to the waiting room. i then spent two hours curled up in pain on the floor of the waiting room before my pain doctor came through and they just put me back on the meds i was on before that were working. it was a rough ride but i got the prescription and took them and was back to life again. this was 4 hours after the time i arrived at the hospital.

it was a day or so after this that a friend of mine told me that they probably though i was an addict. this is the reason for this review. i am a clean cut professional, i can't even believe i could throw out that kind of vibe but he said that there are clever addicts that exhibit the same persona. all i can say, this is some of the worse pain i've ever experienced and i've had a lot with the gi issues from my past cancer. i was wondering why two different people came into the er after me and got right in. they just kept telling me all their beds are full. so i guess it's true. i will do all i can to avoid this place if i can. unfortunately it's the only hospital around me from what i'm seeing. but i am new to the area. i'll have to explore more and ask around.

having had a severe sore throat, cough and congestion for about a week, i went to my doctor (wearing a mask they gave me) yesterday.  i was told that i likely just had a severe sinus infection (non-contagious) but that i should probably consider being tested for covid 19.  they suggested that i go to the drive through testing at baptist east; so i did.

there was a quick drive through triage with two stops to determine that i "qualified" for testing.  then they instructed me to park my car, where i was called on my phone and told it was my turn for testing.  this all took no more than 10 minutes.  when i arrived at the first of two stops at the testing tent, i was asked for my insurance card and asked how much i wanted to put toward my $1400 deductible.  when i asked what the cost would be for the test, they told me that they did not know but that i would need to pay "something" toward my deductible for the emergency department visit.  emergency department visit!  you have to be kidding me!   those visits cost hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars and i was in a rickety tent in a parking lot trying to do my part to determine if i had exposed anyone to a terrible virus.   i got nowhere when asked why this was considered an emergency department visit instead of a minor medical or minute clinic visit.  i also told the payment staff that they should disclose the approximate cost at the very beginning of the testing process.  nonetheless, i put $50 on my credit card and proceeded to the second section of the tent to be tested for the common good.

two nurses swarmed me as i sat down in the testing section of the tent.  one took vitals while the other gave me a new set of sinus windows with five different swabs.  when i asked why so many, i was informed that they are testing for the flu, strep, covid 19 and one or two other tests.  five tests in all.  i told her that i had no idea they were going to do all those tests but she said that's what they are testing for at the current time.  and i am sure they are profiting for each and every separate test for each and every person being tested.  i went back to my car, a bit stunned from the encounter, and comforted my bleeding nostril with a tissue.

the covid-19 testing at baptist east took less that being in line at chic-fil-a and should definitely not be billed as an emergency department visit.  i feel that the hospital is taking advantage of the pandemic instead of doing its share to help those affected.  they should know better.  and they should be ashamed.

review:
this is a pretty top notch hospital.  i guess during the coronavirus crisis, not many people were at the hospital.  parking was pretty empty with no one to man the posts.  we came here while i was 3 cm. dilated.  since i wasn't in active labor, they checked me in and then had me walk around for an hour.  this was the most painful one hour walk that i've ever had.  i cried.  but all the nurses were really nice and supportive.  

after i started to become more dilated, i was checked in immediately and then they flew me down via wheelchair to my room, which was spectacular with an ocean view.  the anesthesiologist came in pretty fast to give me the epidural.  our dedicated nurse was super nice and helpful.  whenever i wanted some popsicle or some chicken soup, she brought it for me.  she was very informative too.  what a blessing to have a great nurse!

they were really efficient too, when i was in active labor, a herd of nurses came in to help out.  it was pretty awesome.  everyone knew what to do.  no one was super chatty, which was nice because i would have gotten annoyed.

the after care was awesome too.  the nurses again were all very helpful and kind.  the after care room was pretty spacious.  we really enjoyed the food offered at hoag. they gave us a celebratory dinner, which was so generous and thoughtful.  the food was very delicious.  we order the filet wrapped with bacon and had some cheesecake.  all in all, it was such a luxurious stay.  it was way better than the hospital that i delivered at for our first child.

hotel hoag is the best place to deliver. from the nursing staff to the service staff, customer service is top notch. i had an emergency c section 2 years ago with my son and was trying for a vbac with my daughter i just had 3 days ago. everyone was on board with the vbac and didn't make me feel pressured to do anything else. i ended up having a successful vbac with dr. illeck and it was the best redemption birth i could have asked for. giving birth during a global pandemic is scary and the whole experience was warm, inviting, and first class.

my 92 year old mother was taken to the hoag hospital emergency room by ambulance last week.  due to the covid 19 limitations, no one was allowed to accompany her, despite the fact she is hard of hearing and easily confused.  this is what two young women did to her because they had trouble with a blood draw and she had no one to advocate on her behalf.  she felt like she was being tortured for nearly an hour  she was terrified to be there without a family member to assist.  covid 19 or not, this type of treatment for elderly patients is completely unacceptable.  i do not recommend that anyone take elderly relatives to the hoag er until the policy changes.
these pictures were taken 4 days after the blood draw, so you can imagine what her arms looked like initially.
because of a virus that is less contagious and less deadly then the flu, i can't be with a loved one after bringing them in with appendicitis. please tell me how the hell this makes sense!?

i took my 9 yrd child to er due to a runny nose. during this covid-19 and one of the security officer's make a snark remark saying " this youngster is still here". this happened after i had stepped out to make a phone call. we had been in the waiting for a while, very common for an er waiting room. i didn't appreciate that remark.

i want to thank the doctors and nurses, as well as all staff members at hoag hospital for saving my 24 year old daughter's life several weeks ago.  we believe she had covid, was on a ventilator, in a medically induced coma and near death. the nurses and doctors worked tirelessly on her for a week and she came out of it good as new! they kept us updated during her stay,  which was vital especially since we are in another state and not able to be with her. thank you hoag staff, you have no idea how appreciative we are!

i was transferred here from the another campus' er because they thought i had the coronavirus and this is where they were sending covid-19 patients to consolidate them at one location.  i didn't think i had it - they just said my symptoms were likely to be covid-19 - i had one symptom, shortness of breath and valley fever scarred lungs - that combination apparently got me the golden ticket to get shipped on over to abrazo central campus.

i got there around 1pm, got one set of vitals, and was told by the nurse that they wouldn't come in, if you needed anything to call.  i talked to a doctor on the phone who said i probably didn't have covid-19 but they needed to wait for the results of the test.  so for several hours i was left alone until the night shift nurse came on (when i finally got a gown and a blanket).  she at least came in several times to check vitals during the night - got woken up in the middle of the night to get a second covid-19 test since they could not find the first one.  

the next day, surprise!, i don't have covid-19 and they are going to move me from the covid-19 section to another room.  i get a cardiologist who basically tells me i am ok to go home even though i am still having some shortness of breath @7am (also absolutely nothing had been done at this point since everyone was waiting for the results of that test).  they move me to another room on another floor @10am where the bathroom floor is always wet because the shower is leaking (where they give me toiletries finally - luckily i had someone drop off my phone charger, toothbrush and toothpaste, etc the day before so i didn't need anything).  

i am pretty much ignored for several more hours - i got an echo (the technician who did the test was awesome at least) and then "you are going home" @5pm (without talking to a doctor about what the echo showed or any information).  i asked to speak to a doctor and he came and really didn't explain much and just said that i could come see him and get another test done at his office - and at that point i was really ready to get out of there and go home and see my own doctor anyway.

granted, i do understand some of this because of the covid-19 virus going around, but even when i was moved to a regular floor, i couldn't get answers and i got discharged with a shortness of breath diagnosis and a diet plan.  i asked for the echo results to give to my regular cardiologist and was told that i couldn't have them because they hadn't been read yet

the nurses were nice enough when you saw one ...
and the food was not bad (except for the turkey sausage - don't ever get the turkey sausage) but i really hope not to return to this location especially not during the pandemic, but probably not ever

i am pretty sure i am going to be getting a big bill for basically getting misdiagnosed and ignored - can't wait to see the cost of that!

this time was awful. i really recommend going somewhere else if you have an emergency during covid time.
i had to leave my father, who has dementia, at the er in the middle of the night while he was having a memory lost incident that could be an stroke because of the symptoms. this was not his first stroke.
because of covid we were told that we had to leave the hospital and the doctors will communicate with us letting us know what was happening. we received a call 30 minutes after my father got in but it was more of a nurse/doctor asking questions about my father medical history that anything else because they needed test to find out what was happening.
next day we called several times and we were lucky to talk to a nurse like twice. i had to request to talk with the nurse manager (craig) who by reading notes of my dad's case told me he was getting moved to a room when they have a bed available. that more tests were needed. this guy was able to make a doctor to call me and tell me the same thing. 
three days later, after calling many times during the day and night, and talking with nurses on different shifts, i got a call that my father was ready to go home so i have to go and pick him up that he will be ready in 30 minutes. 
i step up and spoke with the nurse manager and told her that i would not pick up my father until i get a report of what happened from a doctor. i spoke during his stay with the nurses, nurse managers, nurse secretary,  case manager and social worker. none of the above did their job. none of the above were able to get a doctor and make him/she to call us as we requested multiple times since day one. my father has dementia. how a "doctor" would pretend to report to a patient who doesn't speak english properly, has dementia and it's at the hospital because of a memory incident?? i'm sorry but this doesn't make any sense to me. they had our contact numbers and notes on the room board and on the chart. please give me a brake and be human! someone with a heart and common sense would pick up the phone and give a simple report in 5 minutes. they charge a lot of money for their time but 5 minutes are too much to ask?? how can i get a reimbursement for that time that they didn't do their job?? because i waited for that call for 3 days so my nerves doesn't have a value for them?? 
the cherry on the top were the 2 hours that i had to wait downstairs because nobody called transportation to send my father downstairs. oh no, sorry, there was one more cherry when i finally got home and opened the bag with my father belongings, the nurse send me his dirty pants and the dirty diaper (with pee) from the day i left my father at er (3 days ago). yeap...the nurse put pants and diaper on a bag and send it with my father. 
i got my doctor courtesy call for 5 minutes. only because i said to the nurse manager that i would not pick up my father until i get a report from a doctor about my father condition. the doctor was polite and said that this was pretty much a dementia episode and that he had no evidence of a new stroke. so he can go home. 
as you can imagine i won't recommend anyone to go to memorial hospital at johnson street unless you are in an ambulance and you have no choice. 
i will drive longer next time anything happens to my family and take it to a different hospital. 
memorial team, it's time to check up on your staff and standards during covid.

after a decent emergency room visit a few years back, i thought using the same hospital for my pcp/urgent care/other exams would make things easier. instead, there have been more ways to screw up. 
-well woman's exam: the worst time to mention "this is what i'm doing" and "this might hurt" is after the fact. 
-walk-in clinic: sure, i was dehydrated and nauseous. but i shouldn't have to ask curiously about my numbers after hearing a nice lecture on stress (first thing), so as to finally find out "okay, there's something wrong with that blood pressure." should have known something was wrong when this doctor walked in with the mask below her nose. same one who'd acted very patronizing before about "well, we all get anxious" when i asked about my cough. 
-lab/walk-in clinic: my actually pleasant pcp left the hospital (probably for good reason), so the urgent care provider suggests that i go perform a blood test she ordered before my appointment with the new provider. of course the lab then declines this patronizingly: "well, that doctor left." yeah sure, i get procedure, but the urgent care providers couldn't have told me earlier?
-pcp: going through an appointment at lightning speed, addressing each issue in two canned sentences, then writing that down as "issues discussed" is a ripoff. and that goes for asking me very brief questions and answers, as well. 
-pcp: of course someone might want to verify my new diagnosis with my one outside doctor, not wanting to go off my word. however, would it kill you to at least ask him before writing down the outdated diagnosis in my chart? and he got my meds right, so for the second time in one appointment, no, i'm not switching that doctor to straub for your convenience. 
-pcp: i've fainted once last month, and almost passed out again this month. after four friends in one month suggested anemia or pointed out my odd paleness, looking at a previous lab result, i want one good reason no one discussed my hemoglobin is borderline. 
-pcp: i've got pretty entertaining hospital records. i'd think if the first person requested them, they'd be in my chart for the next person.

transparent billing practices are important in maintaining trust with the general public. you will not find that at pch. outpatient clinic appointments located inside the facility will be billed for a facility fee because it's inside the hospital. therefore, not only are you paying your regular office visit copay but because you walked into the hospital for your outpatient visit, they tack on an additional fee. the tricky part is that this isn't discussed at any outpatient visit and the bill doesn't drop until care has been completed. isn't that nice? they don't tell you until afterward. so, i call the billing department and get told they have to bring everyone inside the facility due to covid but they can't eliminate the $100 facility fee......so the burden is on the patient and family due to variable outside my control??? so then i as to talk to a supervisor, the billing clerk places me on hold several times and converses with said supervisor but when i ask to speak with them they are unavailable? i tell them to call me and ask for a deadline, she says by next day. i know this game of hoping to catch me off guard. one week later a supervisor calls me and is not helpful so i ask to talk to another supervisor. so....trish calls me and she is the inpatient financial counselor. she told me twice how she meets with families to review and explain bills. she talks nonstop, i barely get a word in. she states that i signed paperwork reviewing the facility fee and i will pay and if i don't these bills will get sent to collections. i advise her i did not sign paperwork for the outpatient visits but i did sign paperwork for the er visit but these are two totally different visits. so then she says there are pamphlets everywhere that explain how pch bills outpatient visits as hospital visits. really? i remind her that she just told me i signed a form and now she is saying i should have found a magical pamphlet laying around telling me i would be charged a much larger fee to receive outpatient care  at pch. i ask to speak to her supervisor. she pretty much tells me they won't talk to me. i am not important. she says they can set up a payment plan......trish, did you hear me when i spoke? it's not about the money it's about your billing practices. i remind her that she is obligated to have them call me and this needs handled appropriately. i am waiting on this call currently. 

this hospital is all about money. they are practicing shady business at the cost of the patient and their families. this is wrong on so many levels and the public needs to know. 

also important to note, my son presented to the er with an open fracture. the orthopedic surgeon on call should have come in and taken him to the or for repair but he was lazy and wouldnt. they reduced  his arm in er against my better judgement and told me to follow up with ortho. these appointments normally take weeks to getso i phoned a friend and got him in to see an amazing surgeon who said the arm needed surgery asap. he found a poor alignment of the fracture with muscle in between the pieces of bone that would have resulted in decreased range of motion in my sons arm had it been left and i not known enough to make calls to get him extra help. it is also important to mention here that if he were taken to or, the bill would have been much less because the er stay would have been rolled into a surgical admission. are you seeing a trend of they like to make more money instead of render the right care?????

my mother-in-law and i were next door to the hospital touring an assisted living care facility. when we were leaving she was having trouble breathing from the walk and needed her oxygen so i helped her put on the mask and she asked for help to get into the vehicle. i ran in and found two employees to come and help me. when we got out there to help she was coughing awful and then all of the sudden passed out so we laid her gently on the parking lot. 

as the workers called 911 and i called my husband my mother-in-law, karen, was starting to turn blue in the face..she wasn't waking up...more employees were starting to gather. it took 17 min for a small fire truck to come and start cpr, why hadn't any of the staff or i start to do this sooner? everything was going so fast except the ambulance they took forever!! when they did finally show up we got mom to the hospital right next door!

the doctor and nurses had her in an emergency room while i was answering questions in the back and handing over her medical cards. they brought her back thank god, but then she passed right back out, she did this several times. i was told i had to wait in the waiting room where i had to answer the questions all over again. then they wanted me back again and was asking more of the same questions then back to the waiting room, then back to the e.r. it was crazy! when i was told to go to the waiting room last my husband showed up and we could both go back, then they offered us drinks. it felt like they had no clue what they were doing at all. 

the doctor kept coming out of the room and doing different things, talking with other people and then they asked if mom had a d.o.r. in place? really!! i would've told them a long time ago if she had..is there no communication here? after mom had come back to us 4-5 times then shut down again the hospital decided to medi-flight her to the okc heart hospital. they brought her back and told us that she was having seizures from going without oxygen for those 17 awful minutes waiting on the ambulance. with the seizures mom would never be the same and she would be on machines for all of her remaining life, she wouldn't be the same. we had to make that tough choice to say goodbye and let her go. she had already been through so much and we knew she'd never want to live as a vegetable or have machines to keep her alive. 

if you ever have any other choice use another hospital!! this one has absolutely no communication. the doctor was out of the room more than he was with his patient than needed help from him. i don't have anything good to say about the ambulance or the living center next door to the hospital either. with those employees working at a place where the elderly spend the rest of their days you would think someone would've dropped down and started cpr!!

i know this post is long but bear with me....trust me.....

if you are a travel rn seeking an assignment in or around denver, co, i highly recommend avoiding this facility. i was recently a travel rn for parker adventist during the onset of the covid outbreak. right away the staff and the work environment were very off-putting. my "welcome" to the unit was anything but welcoming. the management and leadership were rude and didn't provide me any direction or answer any of my questions. i couldn't get the nurse manager to answer my emails or return my calls once in the few months that i was at the facility. a good portion of the nursing staff were cold and never offered assistance when a fellow teammate was struggling (i was in icu....you know we all need help in icu). on top of the nursing staff, the doctors were ignorant, impatient, and most had "god complexes". i was consistently ignored, talked over, and/or cut off when i had important information regarding my patients. not to mention, an anesthesiologist put his hands in my face for being "too slow" when drawing up the correct dosage of medication for my patient (it had only been maybe about 30 seconds at this point.....). lastly, what really got me frustrated was that i was told that i was going to be "let go" from my travel contract if i ever took another day off when i had to take a few days for strep throat and the passing of my grandfather. i am only talking like 2-3 days here in the six months that i was at the facility. after the way i was treated for taking a few days off for my mental and physical health, it was apparent to me that i was very expendable and just another warm body for this hospital to control. again, i highly recommend searching elsewhere. 

thanks for bearing with me. i just wanted to save my fellow travel rns and our patients from having to go through a similar experience at this facility. (:

my daughter was in this facility.  physical rehab, occupational therapy and speech therapy appeared to be very good. after a week it showed not much therapy was happening. 
 
the nurses ( most not all) lack empathy & caring skills.  not all seem to read charts or personal information. every shift has different ways to go about taking care of patients medication schedule.  a schedule is a schedule! 

my daughter was ignored having serious physical symptoms and i had to talk via facetime to the nurse since they were on pandemic lockdown.  i explained her symptoms that were a serious warning that something was seriously wrong!

after my being given a hard time by her nurse and being told "she knows her name and who the president is, "she's just fine"   well, she finally called the doctor on call. my daughter ended up in the hospital needing medical care immediately. 

if they would take the time to talk to the patients and get to know them, they would see something was very wrong!

the nurses lacked in the area comfort for my daughter.  like leaving the nurse call button, drinks,tv remote and bed controller within reach is important to those with physical limitations. most therapists get  it, the nurses do not.  

as for the nursing assistants, my daughter has some very thoughtful caring ones that she adores. they show patience ,brush her hair and tend to her needs, which can be a lot at times. then there are some that just don't want to be there and she feels like a burden when they walk in her room with a snarling face.

when my daughter was slipping out of her wheelchair, she had to have siri on her phone call me. not one person on that floor could hear her yelling for help! i had to call the reception desk! yes, she fell after the nurse arrived. pain meds took a bit after that.

i would not recommend this particular facility for rehab with patients that have memory issues and are unable to move their arms unless they are across from the nurses station!

after being home under my date my daughter made better progress.

review:

10 minutes later a nurse comes in with zofran to stop his nausea and vomiting. what?!??? i just told you he wasn't throwing up.

i ask her if it's something in my house because we're remodeling, she disregarded it. 
i told her my older son has asthma if this could be hereditary? she ignored me. 
he hasn't eaten in 36 hours now, asked if he should get an iv. she said no .. he's had diarrhea straight for over a week.

the nurse heard wheezing. dr lim listens for 2 seconds and says nope don't hear anything that it's probably a virus. i asked if we could do xrays she said it's not necessary. i said i will not leave until xrays we're done. ).
