review: during this time of emergency due to covid-19, i completely understand that the frontline is exhausted, overwhelmed, and frustrated.   i know this because i am on the frontline as a healthcare provider myself.  however, no matter what the situation presented to us, we are to be empathetic, compassionate and respectful to each patient that we treat.  i did not experience this from dr. mendoza or stacy, np (sp) during an e.r. visit with my daughter on march 22, 2020.  stacy was very dismissive, argumentative and continued to minimize my daughter's condition.  no matter what my daughter told her, the bottom line is that stacy was not actively listening.  because this was the second time within two days that my daughter had presented to the emergency room with these symptoms, this was an urgent situation for us.  who would go into an emergency room where there is a greater chance to be exposed to corona if it wasn't an emergency? in my experience, a patient knows their body and how they feel and we as healthcare workers should listen and not dismiss what they are saying.  we are not always right and don't have the right to tell a patient how they feel.  stacy comes in to discharge my daughter after barely assessing her a few hours before.  there was no end result except to go home.  no.  the problem has not been resolved.  the reason why we are back here a second time is because of the dismissive attitude  presented before.  apparently there is something seriously wrong.  i asked to speak to the charge nurse but somehow dr. mendoza, who never treated my daughter at all, found her way into the room.  she, just like stacy, refused to listen to our concerns and basically in a nutshell told us that they would not be doing anything for my daughter and for her to go home and 'stick it out'.  for hippa related issues, i won't go into detail my daughter's condition but it involves constant vomiting, diarrhea and severe stomach pain.  she cannot even keep down water.  severe dehydration is an overwhelming threat at this point.  dehydration leads to other medical conditions like heart problems or kidney failure.  because i have a healthcare background and know that there is a standard that should be met when taking care of people, my mind is completely blown by the behaviors of these two healthcare providers.  again, i understand the stress that we are all under but at the end of it all, when you are present with a patient, be present and actually be of help and not hinder an already stressful situation.  i have had pretty good experiences at south sub before so i am extremely disappointed and will be requesting that if myself or any family member is in the e.r. again, that these two not be in charge of our care.  they need sensitivity and active listening training asap.  if something worsens with my daughter's condition because of their insensitivity and dismissals, there will be legal action taken.

with the scare of covid19, i called the covid hotline and explained my symptoms to the nurse on the phones. she instructed me to go on to the er to be seen and possibly tested. i went to this hospital because they did amazing when my mom was transferred there after having 3 heart attacks. 
when i got there, everyone was confused and a little irritated that they didn't know what all was going on. this didn't bother me at all because i know it's a very scary time to be a nurse or dr right now. this covid19 is new and the rules keep changing. i appreciated everyone's demeanor and positivity. everyone. from the ladies at the screening desk, to the triage nurse, all the way back to the nurses elise and anne (i think were their names). i got taken back to a special area where they were screening for covid19. it was a little scary because they were wearing plastic robes over their clothes... 
elise was the nurse that took care of me and she was so amazing. super sweet, and did a good job of keeping my mind off feeling miserable. these doctors and nurses are working their butts off. i mean, elise had to write my info down on a paper towel bc they didn't have all the supplies that needed. everyone i saw was working double time, and staying positive for the patients. i could over hear conversations from my virtual bed, and they don't have it easy at all. please keep this in mind when you see a a nurse or doctor and they look worn out. they've for sure earned a gold medal during this time. i wasn't able to be tested bc i didn't meet criteria. but i still have to quarantine for 14 days. thank you, seton, for trying your best to stay ahead of this virus going around.

my father was recently a frequent patient here as he neared the end of his life with several health complications.  the entire staff was incredibly kind, caring, sensitive, and patient focused.  ellen in the er was especially great.  no emergency room/hospital visit is a good thing but the good people here make it as pleasant as it can possibly be.  i hope and pray for all the good people here to help get us through this covid19 mess.

i was admitted to ascension seton on 38th street on wednesday, june 10, 2020, with an infection which triggered a multiple sclerosis flare up.  i am on the 5th floor, being cared for by the nurses and clinical assistants from the 5th floor nurses' station south.  they are amazing. even in these dangerous times, with half the hallway reserved for covid19 patients, nurses and clinical assistants have shown me unparalleled amounts of compassion, kindness, understanding and concern.  even at end of shift, their attitude, never changes.  they remain patient, kind, caring. these nurses and clinical assistants are true heroes, flesh and blood angels. i pray that god showers each and every one of them and their loved ones with an abundance of blessings, good fortune, excellent health and a long life. i pray that god looks after each of them and their loved ones and keeps them safe. i wish i could do more to express my gratitude and appreciation.  i am humbled by their grace and generosity.

i hope you don't have to recover at this hospital after a major surgery!!!

the surgeon and physical therapist were fine. the one star is for the doctor overseeing her case and the nursing staff. my sister had a complete knee replacement, and due to covid, i was not allowed to visit her and be her advocate. 

she was not given her pain meds at the correct times so she would be in excruciating pain with no relief. she was never able to stay ahead of the pain. she was made to feel like a drug addict for asking for the pain meds she was allowed to have. one nurse was not even able to help my sister test her blood sugar because she could not manage to get the blood strip to my sister's finger.

the doctor did not seem to understand anything about my sister's type one diabetes and how to deal with her high blood sugar. the doctor also misread the chart and told the nurse to give my sister potassium. her potassium levels were fine, she was wrongly given potassium when she did not need it. 

i'm not sure if it's incompetence, not enough staff, or just laziness- most likely all of the above.

this is the worst hospital ever for medical bills! they owed my daughter over $300 for three months. thank goodness for the time off because she's had time to talk on the phone or hold on the phone for hours and hours. do you not give you them your money until you know you owe it to them. if she owed them money of this sorts they would send bill collectors out for her. this all started to before the virus and it is a matter of money not the hospital. thank you to all the front line workers! the billing department should be ashamed of themselves or get someone in there that doesn't lie!!! sad

i was very disturbed when i saw on the news this morning firemen and pd with their vehicles lined up, lights flashing waving and honoring the nurses for their fantastic job and dedication and hard work during this pandemic. now my explanation why this disturbed me so much!  my 88 yr old mother was a patient at o'connor's in may 2018. she had a serious case of sepsis. she has advanced alzheimer's and was unable to talk, feed herself so i stayed with her. she was on a continous iv of strong antibiotics for 8 days. the antibiotics tend to give a person diarrhea. i was there to feed her and be her voice. one day she had diarrhea very bad, i could hear it. i rang the bell for the nurse, 5 or so minutes she came. i said it is real bad i could hear it. she said well i have to find help. 10 minutes later i went searching for her, she was with someone else. i said my mom beeds changed now, it's been about 15 minutes. she said i'm still looking. she finally comes in with an aid about 10 minutes later. it was a mess. the aud did not even clean her well because the nurse told her to wipe her again. this was on the 5th floor. then twice they did not do the iv correctly. i reached over to pull my mom's blanket up and it was wet, her gown was soaked, the sheets were soaked. the nurse came in and changed it, then they changed the bed and her gown. well low and behold about an hour later her arm was wet again. they had to redo it. finally my mom was ready to be released. at home when i went to change her had a rash all over her but, between her legs and all over her thighs from their lack of proper care for my mom. if i would have seen it, i would have been arrested for smacking the shit out of all of the useless, uncaring worthless nurses. this was on floor 5. i called and complained and sent pictures of my mom. i was unable to go in person and complain since i was sole caretaker for her. but they got the pictures the day after she was released.
this did not happen during a pandemic when the nurses were streched to their limit. it was just plain negligence on their part. and now they being admired as godly. all they are doing is their jobs, which they should have done when my mom was their patient!  so yes i was irritated to see
the news this morning. i for one hope o'connor nurses one day you experience the same care you put my mom through!

in the next few days .. this wil be b re open for covid19 patients  as a shelter ,who are infected with coronavirus..i salute my collegues (nurses ) md's ,medical staffs who are risking lives to take care of these patients  .. i hope and pray that there will be an antidote already coming for this covid19  very soon .stay safe !! god bless us all!!!#registerednurses fight covid19!!!

called to see if i needed to call ahead before going into the er especially with covid-19 being taken very seriously. i just wanted to know if i had to call in advance before showing up. i don't work there, so obviously i don't know if they are doing anything different to keep everyone safe. my husband was in severe pain and his face was swelling from a tooth infection. i was already nervous and instead of making me feel at ease, the woman who helped me (lucy) on the phone was very rude. there was no empathy in her tone and it seemed as if she did not care. she even laughed when i expressed my concerns about going into the er. i have never had anyone in the medical field make me feel the way she did.

i went to st lucy medical center for a broken wrist . before i went i called the er cause i dint have a mask . i was told come on in there's a nurse outside that will give you a mask...so i went...they did not give me a mask outside...so at registration? nope..so when the doc came in..we momentarily talked..he noted that i have asthma...so i asked for a mask ..he said no..so then i hoped and expected i would get out quick as even the nurse acknowledged they were that busy...2 and a half hours with no mask..i left...so i called the hospital so they know people are giving out the wrong info regarding masks..risk management...not only didn't care but miss nasty began to lecture me on using walk in clinics,,,as if i wasn't aware...not only that she blamed my docs ofc who told me to go to the er..totally ignoring  the fact that called ahead to find out the situation re masks...she didn't seem to care her hosp was giving out wrong info.....so i hung up with her...and called the er...i then got to speak with nurse ratchet michelle who blamed me for not discussing this with her at the time..totally ignoring the fact that i asked the doctor and he said no...(i suppose i should have pulled a firearm on him and demanded one ),,,i called back and spoke with nurse ratchet number 2 heather..who at first refused to give me the name and number of the director... lex lalicon..who by some strange reason was not in today...i need to call back monday....you know how that goes......well all all it seems the priority of this hospital is just cya..not patient care... ..here i thought was doing a good thing by telling them they are giving out wrong info regarding masks during this medical crisis..yea until nasty woman risk management started the whole thing by being nasty and lecturing me...just wow !

horrible experience at the er here yesterday. my son had a cardiac procedure in the morning and was discharged around 5. he began bleeding profusely from the site and had to return to the er.  no one was allowed to enter the er with him, understandably, because of corona virus precautions. after a few hours he was discharged and sent outside to sit on a metal bench at dusk in 50 degree, windy weather in nothing but a hospital gown and tennis shoes. (he had no other clothing with him because he'd left that at home when he had to rush back to the hospital). when he asked to wait to be picked up in the waiting room he was told that the waiting room was for patients only and technically he was no longer a patient. the waiting room was not busy at all. in addition to this his phone battery was dead. i am appalled by the lack of care for someone who was less than 7 hours out from general anesthesia and had recently experienced significant blood loss. as a retired registered nurse i will certainly never use this hospital again for any reason.

#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!

i'm writing this review on behalf of my mom and sister who attended the facility yesterday friday may 29, 2020. extremely grateful and satisfied with the treatment my mom and sister received by rn carlos barraza. he was very professional, super friendly and made there experience a great one. they were both nervous about going to the facility and my mom a little more then normal since she doesn't speak english well. he was able to assist her in the language she needed and made her feel comfortable.  in the midst of a nation wide pandemic it is amazing to know that their are still health care professionals who give quality work and are truly passionate about what they do! we need more people like rn carlos is the health care system. [mom]-  "thank you so much for what you did for my family! definitely will be going to the foothill regional medical facility and will recommend to all my friends and family. hope to be help by rn carlos b again! "

we were here 3 times and have been sent home only to be brought back by ambulance. this place is the worst hospital i've ever been to and as a transplant patient from cedars sinai coming here was the worst thing. not only are the nurses rude but i was yelled at by a physician named maggie vargas. i have never been treated so poorly in all my times at a hospital and during this pandemic i tried to be patient with all the nurses and their hard work but, sadly this location isn't just does not care. i would definitely think 1,000 times before coming here or sending a loved one.

i was here overnight after surgery. i was told my daughter could be there during my pre op until they took me to surgery. they did not allow her back and actually had my family go home. the doctor came out to talk to my family and was not told they were not allowed to stay. everything went well until i was taken to my room. i was ignored. the iv machine beeped for 20 minutes. i could not get anyone to come help. i finally pushed every button till it was turned off. i was told i needed to walk to go home that day. no one came to help me.  i begged the nurses to help me get up to walk but no one came. i had to spend the night when i could have gone home. the nurses only came if i needed meds or to take my vitals. another patient screamed all evening and i was told by my nurses they were looking after her. i was ignored because she was screaming. if my family could have been there i could have gotten something to drink or gone to the bathroom. if you will not let families stay because of covid-19 then nurses need to pay attention to their patients. i owe more money because i had to stay the night when i wanted to go home.

i typically avoid the er at all costs but having kids there have been a number of times we have had to go to various ers over the years. 

this time i was by myself during the summer of covid and went to loma linda feeling rather anxious having to be alone and in so much pain. 
i was quickly evaluated, treated, and cared for. 

i wanted to write a review because i feel that i was treated with such dignity and exceptional care. 
my provider was rick oldenburg and my nurses were carrie and alexis. 

all three of them had plenty of patients but from what i saw they made each of us feel comfortable and did their jobs with a smile. i can only imagine how difficult these last months have been on healthcare workers yet here they are showing up for us in all the ways! bravo to llmmcer staff! thank you for your bedside manner in a sensitive time when as patients we don't have someone to hold our hand- it really means a lot!

brought my husband in tonight around 6:30 because he had a swollen gland in his neck and complained of lethargy.  he doesn't have a fever or any other covid related symptoms but yes let's jump to that conclusion.

i've been waiting in the car in the parking lot since he checked in....it's now 10:35 and i'm still waiting.  an hour ago he's was waiting to be discharged. 

good heavens how effing long does it take to discharge someone? 

this hospital is a joke.

i went in for covid-19 testing and was treated like pure scum of the earth. the nurse "jim" drilled me and asked why i was out so early getting a covid-19 test and why did i come to the er and not call my doctor? i told them that i had shortness of breath and i keep having the chills. i work in a warehouse that has had numerous cases of covid-19 over the last few weeks and it's possible that i was exposed. i was then advised that because i did not have a fever that i didn't have it. i was also advised that because i was not falling on the floor from shortness of breath that my shortness of breath was not serious. i then grew angry from the way the nurse was talking to me and left without testing. he would not even give me his name when i asked for it. not trying to make this a race thing, but studies show that when people of color visit the doctor our symptoms are often downplayed because we're not supposed to feel pain or that we're not truthful. the two clerks also told me that they didn't know the nurse's name that was giving me the hard time. how do you work with an extremely small group of people and not know your colleagues name?  i will be contacting the hospital later on today to speak with a supervisor.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review:
i had the fortunate opportunity to be a patient here at the end of february, 2020. yes, right before all elective surgeries were cancelled due to the corona virus, or covid-19. the staff was absolutely wonderful! check in was easy, as you go up to the 2nd floor, and the check in desk is right there by the elevators, you can't miss it. the waiting room is comfortable, with nice seating, and plenty of it. there are tables there for your use as well. free coffee and tea too.

they have a nice system in place, where there are rooms that you are taken to, once surgery/procedure is done, and your family/friends talk to the doctor/surgeon about how things went. this is done in private. there is also a board where your family/friends can watch the progress of your surgery/procedure as well, all by the number assigned to you when you check in.

the hospital is big, very big. it's clean too. there is a nice cafeteria, and a daz boggs as well. there is a gift shop on the first floor, and a baby joe's gift shop, if i remember correctly, on the 4th floor as well.

parking is easy too. there are several garages with free parking. or, use the valet service, which is right there by the front door. 

the staff is wonderful, as well as all volunteers, and basically, everyone. 

my stay at the hospital was a good one. i was always in good hands. i never needed anything either. the room was comfortable, and i had it to myself, i didn't have to share it with anyone. the food was good too.

if i ever have to have surgery again, i wouldn't hesitate when told that the surgery would be at st. joseph hospital. thanks for the excellent care!

this is specifically about the er. i went in for having covid symptoms that were irritating my asthma. they basically took me back to a room and scolded me for being there. the doc even admitted how shaky the test is. they didn't listen to my breathing or anything. i went home and had an asthma attack but was too scared to go back and face rejection and humiliation again. eventually went back and was hospitalized for covid. hospitalization was better than er but the er needs to rethink their priorities. this is a pandemic with a deadly virus and inaccurate test, treat all your patients with respect and listen to their symptoms, not their false negative. future hospitalization could have been avoided if you cared the first time.

this hospital is extremely under staffed. we took our family member here during the covid 19 crisis and there was example after example of a barely functional hospital staff on duty here. the communication between departments was atrocious. the dietary staff never asked about food allergies, and simply brought the meal of the day to include  unripe fruit. prescriptions were not sent to our pharmacy. these were just some of the things that we experienced. 

it seems like the hospital is understaffed and the small logistical issues are being forgotten or brushed aside. 

as far as medical care. we were satisfied with the medical care and experience of the surgical staff.

in the future, we will be driving the extra 20 minutes to a different hospital.

when my family member was transferred here 8 days ago my heart sank when i saw the reviews, but i vowed to keep an open mind. 8 days later, i have not been able to get a doctor to call me once. there are 3 patient phones in the unit but 2 of them are broken. no visiting at all due to covid19.  nice nurses did get my relative on the phone twice, after i kept calling, and my relative told me he had given permission for the doctors to talk to me. and still no
calls.  what kind of quack doesn't talk to family members who have information about a patient's history?   the people whose loved ones have landed in this place need to get together & press for action.  maybe media attention would be useful here?  local press might be interested in a story about substandard mental health care provided during this time of crisis.

i had surgery the other day and just am so impressed by all the staff at this hospital. from the front door employee to admitting, to lab, to surgery you all were just amazing. being there alone was so difficult because the no visitor policy due to covid, however you all made it a little less stressful for me. dana my pre op nurse you are an absolute gem!! thank you for talking with me and helping me through my nervousness!! thank you to the entire surgery staff for making me laugh and keeping things real but light!! i can't tell you what a difference it makes to have people around you make you feel comfortable in such a scary place! thank you from the bottom of my heart!!

i don't care what the bad review says, i love this hospital.  both of my kids were delivered here, 99% of the nurses here are super nice and super helpful.  my grandparents have stayed here during their surgeries and recoveries as well.  i literally have nothing bad to say about this place.  heart to all the doctors, nurses and staff during this corona virus crisis!  bless you all.

having a lifetime disease, i have been to many hospitals,  and this is by far the best experience i have ever had. 
even with covid 19 in full force, i was treated like the only patient there. not a single rude employee. i was a person, not a #. in and out in under 5 hours through the er.

thank you.

these people in the er are all very unprofessional. the conversations they are having while there is a pandemic situation in our country. complaining about how little they get paid, they never get any time off, lack of benefits, who has dating problems, who is going on vacation, i need my break i need a new boyfriend, my wife is cheating on me, i can't wait until my shift is over. passing notes to each other from doctors to nurses or nurses aides. it's like being in a high school classroom. everyone just standing around the nurses station running there mouths about things that have nothing to do with patients health. staff is very ride and treats patients like we're in the way of there responsibilities and tasks. if you call the nurse station they answer what do you want. than you can hear them back to there immature conversations. while people are coming to get medical help from these people who gladly deposit and spend there check and probably never once think maybe patients are the reason they have a job not a reason there job is a obstacle in there personal life. i've been through much worse over seas and in other countries but this is america. we're supposed to set the standard for the world not try and figure out how to to the minimum for our own citizens. god bless these united states and all those who love our country. good night.

thank you for everything you did for my grandson who was seen there for the past two and half weeks. your staff and doctors took very great care with him. i like to thank dr m. kho for all his help and care for him. also want to thank ms mary beth social worker for all of her help. the compassion and care and help you gave us helped us through the hardest time in our lives especially  with (cov19 virus ) keeping us all locked in, my grandson was cared for in a very safe and healthy environment.  god bless all the people who work here and your families and friends all our best to you in the future. ms p. dyson.

i went in to get surgery on my foot a few days ago. in the midst of this covid 19 crisis, the nurses and doctors were hustling to make sure everything was absolutely spotless. and they still found time to be extremely kind and caring. every single person that i came in contact with at this hospital was incredible. dr. lanier (my podiatrist) was exceptional and did a great job with my surgery. the equipment in the hospital was 5-star worthy. would definitely recommend.

i can't even begin to express my gratitude to the staff in the emergency department, and all of the other nurses, doctors, and technicians who treated me with extraordinary patience and kindness during my stay at mercy general. 

i went to the emergency department in serious condition (both physically and mentally,) and due to the covid-19 crisis, i was skeptical that the hospital would have the energy, means, interest, or (wo)man-power to address my medical and psychiatric needs. that skepticism soon vanished after experiencing the care and thoughtfulness of each and every nurse and doctor who treated me during my 4-night stay.

what's more is that my insurance partially lapsed and would only cover one night of care. the hospital ate the bill for the remaining nights, which saved me much heartache and financial strain down the road. it was an unmerited act of mercy. this hospital lives up to it's name!

in addition, i had no family that was able to pick me up due to the shelter in place ordinance, so i was concerned about traveling back home to santa cruz on amtrak fresh out of the hospital from a severe illness. once again, mercy stepped in to save the day- they arranged a ride all the way home to santa cruz.

i have been hospitalized on two other occasions in my adult life, and this experience far exceeded all of my other visits, and the attention to detail and empathy of the staff here far surpassed my expectations. i am so grateful for all of the providers who helped save my life. thank you all!!!

this has to be the worst emergency department in sacramento, with methodist coming in a close second. be prepared to wait many, many hours in the waiting room... just to be sat in the hallway for many more hours. it's an extremely small ed and they are limited on beds and space for that matter. 

i wanted to completely avoid hospitals during this pandemic, but unfortunately my daughter was sent here twice by both her primary doctor and urgent care. they have a tent set up just outside the entrance to check for fever and ask covid-19 related questions. reasonable right? nope! it apparently doesn't matter if you have symptoms or not because they lump everyone together in the same small waiting room anyway.

oh yeah, i almost forgot to mention that all the communication were through the rn's, a doctor never even spoke to us once during the second visit. patients are almost completely neglected here. it's as though... if you are out of their sight, you are out of their mind. 

thankfully her ppo healthcare plan allows her to have other options.

this place is a complete and total rip off. i just found out i am pregnant and went in to get basic labs which were ordered through their women's center which were in-network with my insurance company, they didn't talk to me about what labs they were going to do (i could have told them not to order any sti screening or blood type because i already know all the results for that since i was last pregnant) so i go in, they take 4 small vials, and no one even calls me with the results, it's been weeks, no i get a bill tho that says they are charging $2500 for what i could have gone to lab corp and paid a fraction for? and then i call their financial help line, and the woman was just like "oh, your insurance company is saying you have to pay this because you have a deductible" oh, fuck me right? low income, pregnant, at home and out of work because of covid with a toddler, and they aren't going to do shit for me, very cool! fuck this place, fuck their service, all they give a shit about is getting paid. i am not going back, i refuse to deliver here, canceling all my prenatal appointments i had with them. 

oh, and those labs they took? my thyroid came back abnormal, thank god i manage my own shit directly with my endocrinologist, because tho it could mean very bad things for my pregnancy and adversely effect my baby, no nurse or the doctor who was supposed to be managing my case contacted me to let me know. always be your own advocate, this place is obviously money first, patients last.

please read, i will be reporting this to the media and will file a law suit for what has happened to me at john muir emergency room. absolutely horrible service. here i am thinking all nurses and doctors are heroes, well not at john muir walnut creek. i began having all the symptoms of the coronavirus yesterday and my symptoms got worst over time. my symptoms included and still include fever, shortness of breath, chills, and a cough. i woke up this morning at 5am not being able to breath or talk and as they say, if your shortness of breath gets worst, go to the er. i went in right away and the first two nurses that came in to see me were nice, and doctor was okay. but my biggest complaint was the nurse that discharged me. let me just first say that i had called for a nurse by pressing the button and no one came in to help me. the light was on for at least 15-20 mins before a nurse finally came in and she came in aggressively to say "you can leave now". she didn't let me know about my test results or even give me any information in general. i asked her, could you give me instructions or any information on whats going on? usually when a visit to the emergency room is involved, it tends to be a frightening, confusing, and even distressing at times. one would expect to have medical professionals to show compassion, patience, and helpfulness during such a time. unfortunately, my family's most recent experience with the emergency room staff at holy cross hospital was the polar opposite to each of the traits i just listed above. during this global pandemic, it is completely understandable that no family members can enter the emergency room. this new dynamic requires even more need for there to be open channels of communication between patients, staff, and kin. based off of my recent experience, any attempt to contact our family member (who was admitted to the emergency room) over the phone was greeted with alarmingly unfriendly hospital staff who verbally articulated their frustration, annoyance, and irritation with our phone calls. at one point, the hospital staff who picked up the phone began to openly complain about my family calling too frequently, and to add injury to insult, we could hear other hospital staff join in and express their unbelief and disdain. there seems to be a workplace culture of viewing (and treating) patients' families as obnoxious irritants. is bedside manner dead at holy cross hospital? based on my experience it is a disturbing yes. this is deeply concerning considering holy cross hospital is meant to be a faith-based hospital. not only does the staff reveal a void of professionalism, it gives a terrible representation of what a faith-based hospital should be to people in urgent times of need and care. i know this is worded strongly, but it needs to be said. unless it is a life-and-death matter, i will never choose to seek medical help at holy cross hospital. what a shameful way to represent the hospital, and trinity health.

my family and i had been under immense stress due to my moms critical condition for the first 3 months of the year where there were several, consecutive admissions and discharges at a local major hospital.  when my mom's condition improved, she was transferred to kindred.  kindreds staff are very attentive, caring and hard working. even my mom's doctor was superior, dr. wong, whom my family felt is providing the best and quality care to my mom. he speaks to us to often, so we know our moms status and made sure we understood. the facility is clean. most of the nurses are very personable and helping with my moms recovery. they even celebrated my mom's 82nd bday with balloons and a beautiful flower arrangement. the nurses and rt's understand the challenge of not having physical contact due to covid-19 and have been gracious enough to answer our daily and multiple phone calls, in spite of them being busy, to open my mom's window blinds for us to interact with her, see her and she can see us!  what impressed me was their metrics of zero covid-19 + cases. kindred's competence is facilitating with my moms recovery.  forever grateful for kindred! kindred staff are my heroes!

recent covid 19 update! do not deliver your baby at st francis medical center!!

ok so where do we start. my wife and i were waiting in anticipation for the birth of our baby girl. our obgyn at all safe medical group,  referred us to st francis & said they were highly recommended. so that was the plan.

2 months prior to giving birth in march we kept trying to call to pre register & no one would pick up the phone, despite leaving numerous voice mail messages & calling many times.

now we are 2 days out from giving birth. cut to 2 days past our due date (april 29th) when she started getting contractions & again had continually tried to call with no luck getting a hold of someone. finally after 4 phone calls throughout the day, someone finally picked up the phone. he said that there is no one available to check guests in and to just come in when her contractions are 5 minutes apart. after pushing back and explaining that we were upset with the lack of follow up, he revealed that the girl in charge of registering patients had just been furloughed by the hospital due to covid19 and to just come in and someone would take care of her. 

on the night of sunday may 1st, 2020 at 10.30pm the contractions hit my wife hard and fast and she was in excruciating pain. 

once we arrived, a nurse at the front checked us for covid related systems. neither of us had any symptoms & i explained that i just had surgery and was tested for covid 19 & was negative. the nurse then said unemotionally that unfortunately they are not allowing a support person to come into the delivery ward until the patient is 10cm dilated, and at the point would then be submitted into the room for pregnancy but would have to leave once the baby is born & would not be able to stay during recovery. as this was our first child, and we were both already scared and nervous, my wife instantly bursted into tears, and kept saying she can't do this without me. she was begging me not to leave while nurse was edging her to come with her. 

at first, i tried to calmly explain & the nurse that i was covid free & she kept unemotionally and unapologetically repeating company policy. i said it didn't make sense, and said if i am covid free or was re-tested (which i was prepared to do) then why would they not let me in.

then this extremely obnoxious security guard starting screaming at us saying that it was part of cdc guidelines & they were just doing their job. at this point (understandably) i was distraught with the lack of empathy and kindness. they both kept telling my wife to come hack & we both looked at each other and said f*ck this, we are not staying here. it was disgraceful, especially as the security guard continued to yell at us and my wife's mother who said this was unfair and not right.

we pulled ourselves together & then called 2 other hospitals in la (adventist health white memorial & la county usc) mid her heavy & painful contractions while in tears crying. both hospitals said that she (the patient) would have to be tested and that if she was negative, they would allow me (one support person) to not only stay with her prior to giving birth but also in recovery, but said the covid test may take a few hours). i just would not be able to leave the hospital.

we decided on white memorial because the night before i had ankle surgery there and we were both blown away by all of the staff's kindness, empathy and the way they communicated to us. looking back, this was the best decision we could face ever made. i had to wait in the car for 3 hours for my wife to get a covid test, but after it came back clear i was finally allowed in. my wife was in labor for 27 hours before she gave birth and then we stayed for another 24hours in recovery. the staff went above and beyond and were the kindest nicest people we have both ever met. everyone was so accommodating and went above and beyond to make sure our stay was comfortable. i couldn't imagine her being alone for all that time. the actually birth only took 20 mins so what good what have that been to her?

what this leads me to believe was that st francis's stance on support guests during covid 19, had nothing to do with the cdc guidelines, rather their own personal hospital guidelines. 

st francis medical center, how dare you, treat my wife with such a lack of compassion & empathy, especially during such a scary time. we are fair!& rational people & understand there are some accommodations that need to be made, but covid 19 aside, believe that that is no excuse for being unprofessional, rude & unkind.

for anyone considering giving birth here, i would never recommend this hospital to anyone, especially if you want to bring a support guest, partner or husband with you, which i'd imagine is every women on the planet.

just created an anonymous profile on here to keep my dad's info somewhat private and write a review that is long overdue, but what better time than national nurse's day to write my review right?! 

i just want to first start by thanking all those involved in the care of my father, in early january, before all this covid pandemonium started. he unfortunately had a stroke and suffered much of the loss of motor function to the right side of his body. as you can imagine, this took quite a toll on my dad and our family. 

as we went in to see my dad everyday to be there for support, there was one nurse in particular that i wanted to send a very special shout out to. his name his aaron and he works on the recovery unit next to the mri building. 

although we encountered a number of amazing staff members, aaron sticks out to myself and my family for our own reasons. i know we were not always easy to deal with during that frustrating time, and aaron was always composed, empathetic, never left us in the dark, and always made us feel like our time was extremely valuable to him. 

but ultimately, the reason i chose to recognize him on national nurse's day, is for what he did after my dad was discharged from northbay to a rehab center in napa. on that day, he told my dad he'd try to visit him and check on his progress if that was okay. lo and behold, two days later, on a saturday, there was aaron to the surprise of us all. he took time from his day off to visit my dad and offer words of encouragement. aaron ended up spending the entire day with my dad and our family until visiting hours were over. 

oh gosh! i'm crying now, so let me wrap this up. aaron, if you get to read this, i just want to say how incredibly grateful we are to you for being the nurse that you are, but more so, for just being the kind-hearted human being that you are, which isn't always easy to find these days. your mom raised an amazing young man, and never change k. happy national nurse's day. 

with love, from our family to yours, 
amy

i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!

i had the unfortunate experience of having to visit the er for my teenage son last night.   i was headed straight for dell children's, as all parents of children should, but he was complaining of horrible dizziness and he had a head injury, so i did not feel comfortable driving that far with him.  in hindsight, i wish we had gone to dell.  

screened at front door for covid and masked.  no problem here other than we were not given any introductions.   from screening, through initial triage, i don't have any serious complaints.   my son was identified as a "trauma alert" in triage, due to the mechanism of his injury, and we were quickly wheeled back. i am uncertain of anyone's role up to this point as all staff who came into contact with us failed to tell us their name or role (with the exception of being told we were  "in" triage, no name or role to the person who completed that task.)

once in the room, my son was taken for ct within 5 minutes.  he had been wheeled to the room, placed on a monitor and left lying in a cold, wet swimsuit. upon return from ct, the pa came by to see him.  she was attentive and concerned.  she gave him a thorough exam, but had trouble finding any nursing staff who could assist her to roll him properly to clear c-spine.  throughout the duration of our stay, the nurses were much less than attentive.  there is an informative board on the wall that tells you the date.  ours read yesterday's date and it is unlikely the male nurse attending to us was named paige or esther, as identified by the board.   

the nursing staff was very disappointing.  they were standing at the nursing station conversing about the 6 year delinquency of required trainings for one of the nurse's at work that evening.  never offered a call bell, had to search for a nurse every time, the bathroom floor was covered in urine, my son was never removed from his wet clothes, taken off the wet fitted sheet (despite multiple bed transfers), never offered a warm blanket (standard of care for trauma alert). they did not operate as a team.  if i asked for something, the other nurses relayed the request to our assigned nurse rather than offering to help. when my son left for mri, evs actually assisted mri staff with the bed transfer because the nurses were sitting at the nurses station and did not offer to help.  

the pa was attentive.  if it were not for her, this review would be 1 star.  the pa
took pictures and relayed them to her attending physician, who was apparently involved in care but never came by to see him.  my son was never asked to rate his pain.  no follow up for the tylenol i requested he be given.  the nurses never asked him about his symptoms.   they did not ever assess him.  the only true assessment was completed by the pa and one by a triage nurse.  discharge instructions by the nurse included reading me the titles off the papers and i was told to fill the cephalexin, "which is an antibiotic, i think", the nurse said.  yes- it is.  nurses make all of the difference.   unfortunately, the nurses this evening showed the difference it makes when they don't take pride in their work.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

switching to kaiser permanente is definitely on the table right now.

my husband tore his patella tendon this morning around 2am. got him to the va hospital by 3 and they had him home by 4am, gave him a brace and told him they would get the referral. by 8am he got two phone calls scheduling him for his covid test and another to inform him that surgery was scheduled for the following day at 0930. we went got his labs, ex ray, surgical consult, pre admission and covid test done by 1330 and we had our first appt at 10am. what service! thank you to the pre-op admission staff - specifically delma who provided the best treatment!  dr. grey was informative as was the rest of the staff.... 

radiology top notch...

then.... labwork - the front desk receptionist (i couldn't catch her name - all i could catch was her bad attitude) was a older woman with short dark hair. thankfully she had a mask on because if her face matched the coldest, rudest most unwelcoming demeanor i've ever experienced i would have turned right around and paid another facility to take his blood. never in my life have i experienced such rudeness in a medical facility. 

the va should really think about replacing her. she's bad for business.

overall, thank you va for your service

my boyfriend came to this er last week for a fever (we couldn't find a thermometer anywhere so we had to go to the er and this one is closest to our house.) dr. kevin truong took his temperature then prescribed him tramadol, which is an opiate (!!!!) for a headache due to a fever. that's it! tramadol! a drug that is way too severe for a simple headache. but it gets worse, my bf went home and continued taking tylenol for the fever. the next day he started having pains suggestive of uti (burning while urinating, etc.) so we went back to this "hospital" and they basically told him he has an std and / or that he got his uti from me, his girlfriend. they never asked if he was in a monogamous relationship, nothing. blamed it on an std, or something contracted from me, no questions asked. the results came back vía his mychart but they are impossible to discern as a non medical professional and, of course, no one from the er called him to interpret them. thankfully, our landlord is an er doctor (at another hospital further away) so my bf emailed the results to our landlord who said, yes, it's a uti, not an std. my bf and i have been living together over three years; this thoughtless, careless assumption that any patient has an std without asking further questions could easily sow distrust in someone's relationship and possibly cause people to break up. not to mention that had my bf taken the tramadol dr. truong prescribed the night before, it would have completely masked the symptoms from his uti that he experienced the next day. pill poppers, take note, it's easy to get opioids at this (irresponsible) er. perhaps they are taking kickbacks from pharmaceutical companies? also, their er staff is perfectly comfortable blaming a woman, without any questions whatsoever, for an infection that a person can literally get out of nowhere, so if you value your relationship i would stay away.

i had a woman come in and try to give me painkillers through an iv. i rarely take medication and if i do it's an antibiotic. with family history i am ultra wary of any substance. i have really high clinical anxiety, so situations like this especially with brain fog from hyper, are really uncomfortable. i asked her, what the medicine was. she said it's (insert name) i asked how big the dose is, she said 30ml. i said is that a high or low dose? she immediately turned around, crossed her arms and said yes or no. i said well i drove myself ect ect, she said again, yes or no completely ignoring my concerns which truly upset me. once i said no she just walked out and said "k the doctor will deal with that" because of that i refused to take it. why would i allow something shot into my veins that they won't even bother to explain? especially if i'll be driving shortly after!!!!

nobody from this facility has contacted me 2 full days after my wife transferred there, and when i call, they refuse to even acknowledge if she is a patient there, even though i was the one who had her transferred there from a kaiser hospital.  kaiser nurses assured me prior to the transfer to this location that i would have full access and be able to advocate on my wife's behalf.  apparently, even though this is a kaiser-contracted facility, they have their own rules and totally disregarded the information provided to them by our health insurance provider who contracts with them.  i even dropped off clothes while my wife was still being admitted (the front desk took them and told me she'd get them when she was done admitting), and also they told me someone would call me that day (never happened).

when you call this place, you better have the patient code or they will not even acknowledge the existence of the patient, but even with a code, there is a consent form they make you sign or nothing can be released, so if your loved one is catatonic or in a coma or other type of frame of mind that is not rational and is unable to sign the form, be ready to not hear from anybody for an extended period of time.  my wife has been there for 2 days and not one person from this facility (doctor, nurse, case worker, etc) has contacted me to update me or speak about my wife's situation.

once i was given a code to receive information (and they actually acknowledged she was a patient), they transfer you to the nurses station and phone rings for hours before anybody picks up.  when a nurse finally did, he told me the code is useless because the consent form isn't signed.  i told him wife is catatonic and cannot sign anything, and then he hung up on me.

my wife has sleep apnea and needs a cpap machine nightly.  the entire reason she was sent to this facility versus others, was because they are supposedly equipped to handle breathing emergencies.  so the first night she was there, she was not provided her cpap.  when my wife finally called me early on the second evening, i told her to ask the nurse for her cpap machine and it was given to her.  then the next morning my wife called me to tell me that all of the electrical outlets in all of the patient rooms weren't working, and the only room that had working outlets was the game room and they would put in there if she wanted.  unacceptable!

they have one phone for the patients to call out on, but when my wife uses it to call me, patients routinely walk up to her and harass her and there is zero privacy for patients who want to speak to loved ones.

once it became clear that this hospital was not "cpap friendly" as they proclaimed they were to our health insurance provider (kaiser), they could not get rid of my wife fast enough (it was great!).  rather than keeping her for a prolonged period of time while they "balanced her meds" or ensured she was safe and ready to return to her home (for those of you in similar situations, you know exactly what i'm referring to), they discharged her without even having a doctor sign off on the discharge form (apparently it must have been done either after she left or remotely, because she was not seen by a doctor the day they discharged her, which is basically unheard of).  

in fact (and to date its now been two weeks since my wife was released and also since i began writing this review), we have never heard from one single medical professional at this facility.  not a doctor, nurse, or anybody else regarding my wife's hospitalization.  the only person who was nice enough to reach out to me while she was still in their hospital, was a social worker who facilitated the quick release.  

the last thing i want to mention is that all of this went down during the current coronavirus event.  you would think that under those extreme circumstances without any visitation possible, that they would ensure the patients and their loved ones (ie i'm her husband who had her sent there!), would have as much access to the patient as possible (via phone, etc).  this place wouldn't even acknowledge to me she was their patient for two full days while i stressed out and worried incessantly, and then i find out that she was without her cpap for her entire stay.  these people are damn lucky i don't sue their ass.  (but i have filed a nice grievance with the major health plan that they contract with, so we'll see how that goes)....

during this whole covid-19 i had some amazing employees help me out! i couldn't risk going inside the store, so i asked if it was possible for the pharmacist to gather up the vitamins i needed. i spoke to a young lady who wrote and gathered everything, i forgot to get her name. when i came to pick up, andrew helped cash me out at the drive through. he made sure i had exactly what i had asked for and didn't make me feel like i was taking up too much time. thank you cvs for your awesome customer service!

so i came here today with my spouse for an outpatient appointment for a follow up with the oncology department.  we were not told before hand that i would need to call to accompany her and she has mobility issues.  i was stopped at the front entrance and told i could not go with her, despite having ppe on and no one in the house having had any contact with anyone with covid either before or after my spouse tested negative both previous times coming here.  so i am sitting in the lobby and another group of two comes in with the exact same situation.  they are not on the visitor list and guess what?  both of them got to go through.  this is some discriminatory bs that some people get turned away at the lobby and others just get to go right on through.  sibley really needs to make a policy that isn't imposed on a case by case basis because this is a bunch of bs!

i'd like to take a moment to simply offer my feedback on this facility. my situation is different given that i've not been able to visit my brother as the hospital is taking great measures to protect the patients from covid-19 which in my opinion is commendable. what the staff has done, is accommodate me with video conferences which have helped eased my families anxiety.

i'd rank them a 10 all day long.

i've had my dad with traumatic brain injury here for 20 days now.  this place is horrible and i will update my review with names and full details of every miserable experience with them as soon as we have him moved out of this hell hole.  they are delaying providing records and doing everything they can to keep him as long as possible so that they can get the $$$$$, but he will be out of there soon.  they are taking full advantage of the covid-19 no visitation policy and abusing the families every step of the way.  zero compassion, zero common sense, zero communication, phones unanswered or rings forever and then someone just slams it to hang up on you.  i am livid with this place and all the negative reviews are 100% accurate.

i had taken the time to write a fair and honest review of this facility where i was a patient from the beginning of february 2020 to the middle of may 2020. i praised the nurses who did well and blasted the case manager for dropping the ball and making the discharge process a nightmare. i think they are more accustomed to people either moving to rehab centers or dying there, not going home. he clearly had no clue how to order and have prescriptions ready for after discharge to continue medications. he was terrible at ordering the necessary ambulance transportation when outside medical appointments or treatments were necessary. i was in the middle of a series of infusions but because he ordered the ambulance to come too late and not leaving enough time, on top of the ambulance running late, he took it upon himself to cancel the infusion and reschedule it for the following week: no concept of the importance of the infusion schedule. after that, i was constantly confirming and reconfirming ambulance transportation because usually it was not scheduled in a timely manner. i had to figure all this out on my own. 

the chief clinical officer also put me at extreme risk by moving me twice during the covid-19 pandemic while i have a suppressed immune system. she argued with me that my immune system is not suppressed. (it is; i confirmed with my medical team and i was told that i am at high risk and must take extra precautions at all times, on top of the pandemic.) she was constantly bugging me about moving me out of my single room - which was the only way i was discharged from the full service hospital facility to kindred: it must be a private room. 

i asked for a covid-19 test before discharge because there were positive cases in the hospital while i was still there. nobody called me with the results, even after i called and left a message a week later. i ended up getting another one just to be sure. 

the wound care department did a great job taking care of my wounds which was the primary reason i was there. they were caring and very careful with the twice daily dressings. luz and william were awesome. the entire wound care team brought me joy everyday, even though i was suffering through extreme pain from the wounds. every single nurse who tended to me gave me very good care. 

it seems i was also lucky with most of the floor nurses. kristine c. was super amazing, always anticipating my needs and checking up on me. i tried as often as i could to request her when i knew she was working. most of the nurses were responsive and everyone was nice to me. but then i was nice to them too. it's true that there were some who spoke with such strong accents that i could not understand what they were saying. i even got lucky with the cleaning crew in the wing where i was for the most part. we always had a nice visit when they came in to clean. 

i posted a couple of pictures of the squirrels frolicking outside my window.

this place and the staff saved my life. i was admitted to detox then went to residential treatment. at first i thought i was in the wrong place, but those were my own feelings and not based on the environment or the staff. i was happy to have my own room and counselors that were there for me 24/7. staff wore masks, patients wore masks, sanitizer was everywhere and cleaning was rampant. i felt safer than i ever have, and this is during covid! i am so grateful for robin, angelica, melissa, nataly, and everyone employed here. thank you all so much! i'd likely be dead right now if it weren't for this facility and it's staff.

i visited this aurora charter oak due to a family member being involuntarily sent to this facility during the pandemic. i personally observed staff walking around without covid masks and gloves in their intake department and main lobby. this facility didn't even require me to wear a mask before entering. 

the patients are given free cigarettes, but they aren't given masks to wear during the pandemic due to "costs." patients are coughing and sneezing without masks and proper covid testing. their communal phones are being used by multiple sick patients and not being wiped down after use. it's almost as if this intentionally violating governmental sanitation standards concerning covid.  

most of the staff i spoke to were nice people (ie, matthew and stephanie). the nurses were professional and caring. however, when i spoke to alicia rivera, the patient advocate, she was rude, curt, and dismissive. she kept dismissing our complaints by saying "every patient says this, every family member says that" etc. 

i was repeatedly told that dr. gogna, the psychiatrist, had the power to discharge our family member, but he failed to personally visit the patient once. in fact, i eventually learned he was the only member of their staff that felt our family member should be kept in the facility longer. 

i'll repeat: dr. gogna (the psychiatrist that never once visited the patient) was the only staff member that felt the patient should be held longer.  how does this make any ethical and logical sense?

this facility purports to help people but it simply drags out the process as long as possible to increase fees and medical bills. this place thinks like a business and not a hospital. how is that helping patients?

a class action lawsuit will be brought against this company for their improper procedures and handling of patients during covid.

if i could rate this hospital negative five stars i would. my mom went to this hospital for a broken arm and ended up dead. how does this happen? while recovering from her arm surgery she experienced trouble breathing. this was a week after the first surgery. she was then diagnosed with small intestine scar tissue and was told she needed an immediate operation. the hospital told her this wasn't a byproduct of this first surgery however independent doctors told us otherwise. she had the second surgery to remove the small intestine scar tissue and was told recovery time with an ng tube for
feeding and managing stomach regulation was a week. after a week with no tangible post operative recovery achieved (her bowels were not yet working) out of frustration, pain and stress she removed the ng tube and refused to have reinserted. the doctors then told her she was healing slowly but well but due to swelling needed the ng tube for another week to complete the post operative process and to get her bowels started,
my brother who had medical power of attorney was refused his request to have my mom's ng tube reinserted because she said she didn't want it. what was clear to anyone that was listening is that mom
was suffering from distress, disorientation from the anesthesia and meds and not in her right mind. north shore doctors did not meet her where she was at. they should have originally told her that recovery would take 2-3 weeks (typical) at her age to appropriately manage her expectations and that her prognosis was good. instead they kept sharing with her negative news about corona virus scaring her even though she didn't have corona. they
 also shared so many potential negative complications without emphasizing their professional opinion that she would recover well and live relatively independently with another week with the ng tube. she became more depressed telling me she would need a colostomy bag which was not the case at all. she was believing things that we're not true. great medicine north shore. since mom sounded coherent the doctors abided by her wishes against the wishes of her medical proxy - my brother. this was on a friday. however this was not my true mom who was saying this. my brother requested a social worker meet with her immediately and asked for mom to be put on antidepressants knowing that she would likely change her mind on the ng tube when she was not so depressed and disoriented. we couldn't get this to happen until monday since the social worker was not available on weekends. thats a good protocol in a life and death situation. does the hippocratic oath mean anything?? in the meantime her doctors told me and my brother that they would start some iv feeding and give her liquids orally. these did not occur until her condition rapidly declined because of handoff delays. apparently the handoff between internal medicine and medical intern doesn't work here. huge medical failure. north shore is a hotbed for miscommunication,
lack of medical follow through and poor medical judgement by monday, mom was on a death spiral and she passed on a wednesday.  if you are looking to heal, i highly recommend avoiding this place. if you have corona go to a professional hospital not here where you most likely will die! god help anyone that goes here
